ORDER

 

 NARESH KATYAL, JUDICIAL MEMBER:
There is delay of 1187 days in filing of present appeal. To condone the same; application has been filed. From perusal of text of application, it becomes apparent that at the time of filing of this appeal, appellant had not gained anything by filing it, belatedly. It is settled law that Courts of Law should endeavor to decide the lis between the parties on merits, instead of throwing the cause of any litigant, overboard, on technical considerations like limitation. It is also settled law that liberal approach should be adopted in matters concerning condonation of delay (limitation) and acceptance of explanation projected in the application should normally be the criteria, unless said explanation is accentuated by ulterior motives and mala fide intention. In present case, no such mala fide intention or ulterior motive is deciphered. To the contrary, cause projected in application for condonation of delay and accompanying affidavit do constitute 'sufficient cause' as per
Section 5
of Limitation Act. This being so; application seeking condonation of delay is allowed and delay in filing of this appeal is condoned.
2.      Challenge in this Appeal No.1

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
ient cause' as per
Section 5
of Limitation Act. This being so; application seeking condonation of delay is allowed and delay in filing of this appeal is condoned.
2.      Challenge in this Appeal No.163 of 2022 filed by appellant has been invited to legality of order dated 14.12.2018 passed by District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum-Sirsa (In short "District Consumer Commission") in complaint case No.77 of 2017, vide which complainant's complaint has been allowed.
3.      Factual matrix: Complainant purchased one mobile set make Apple Iphone 6S 16GB from OP No.1/dealer/appellant herein for Rs.49,900/- vide invoice No.22444 dated 23.02.2016 with one year guarantee/warranty. As per plea; OPs No.1 and 2 also convinced complainant to get insured mobile set with OP No.3/insurer against all risks and liability i.e. risk against theft, burglary, physical damage including fluid damage. In November-2016 mobile set of complainant was damaged as he was on bike ride, and unfortunately mobile set slipped out from his pocket; fell on road and its display/ screen was damaged and it became dead. Complainant approached OP No.1 (appellant) along with insurance of mobile set. OP No.1 on checking handset found it as damaged but put off the complainant and gave assurance that if he approaches OP No.2/insurer, it would redress his complaint. Complainant approached OP No.2/insurer; lodged complain

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text: andset found it as damaged but put off the complainant and gave assurance that if he approaches OP No.2/insurer, it would redress his complaint. Complainant approached OP No.2/insurer; lodged complaint on 05.11.2016, upon which insurer/OP No.2 kept the mobile with it and charged Rs.2,495/- from him without any reason, despite that at the time of insurance; OP No.2/insurer assured that in future if his handset suffer any damage, then it would not charge any amount and he would be entitled for refund of amount. As per plea; OP No.2/insurer stated that mobile is completely dead and needs to be replaced with new one but since new mobile set is/was not available with OP No.2/insurer, he (complainant) was told to approach again, after 21 days. When he again approached OP No.2/insurer; it put off the matter and did not supply new mobile to him. He again approached OP No.2/insurer but it told to complainant that it will not keep any mobile set and it had never insured his mobile set on any occasion and it has no liability to replace/change his mobile set. It is pleaded that he also served legal notice upon OPs on 31.01.2017 but OP No.1/dealer/appellant herein has/had refused to receive notice intentionally and deliberately, whereas OP No.2/insurer in collusion with postal authorities forged the postal report by mentioning on it 'address change'. OP No.3 after receipt of notice did not

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
ice intentionally and deliberately, whereas OP No.2/insurer in collusion with postal authorities forged the postal report by mentioning on it 'address change'. OP No.3 after receipt of notice did not give any reply while OP No.4 replied to notice through email in a vague and casual manner by escaping itself from liability. By pleading negligence in service and unfair trade practice on the part of OPs and by asserting that he suffered harassment and financial loss, he filed complaint for replacement of mobile set and for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.
4.      OP No.1/dealer/appellant did appeared through counsel but had not filed written statement and his defence was 'struck off' vide order dated 27.03.2018 of learned District Consumer Commission. Earlier, vide order dated 08.02.2018, learned District Consumer Commission proceeded ex-parte against OP No. 2 & 3.
5.      OP No. 4/Apple India Pvt. Ltd. raised contest. In written defence; contents of complaint have been pleaded as incorrect by asserting that I-phones are sold by it through their authorized dealers; I-phones undergo strict quality test to ensure that the product maintain its high standard. Complaint is not maintainable against it (OP No.4). As per plea, entire claim is made against other OPs (No. 1, 2 & 3). Complaint has been filed to mislead the forum. It is pleaded that when consumer cause damage to product by exte

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
gainst it (OP No.4). As per plea, entire claim is made against other OPs (No. 1, 2 & 3). Complaint has been filed to mislead the forum. It is pleaded that when consumer cause damage to product by external factors which are not associated with its manufacturing/inherent conditions and which are in complete disregard to and in breach of warranty policy of manufacturer; then he/she cannot claim relief under
Consumer Protection Act
. OP No. 4 has specified the warranties in its written version and pleaded that complainant's mobile phone was damaged by his own carelessness, rendering it out of warranty. It is pleaded that when warranty explains that in order to get replacement or service of I-phone within the warranty period; complainant would have had to get his I-phone inspected by its authorised service provider, but he has not produced any documentary evidence to show that his I-phone was inspected by Apple authorised service provider of OP No. 4/manufacturer. The claims are not identified and complaint is liable to be dismissed. Complainant knows that his I-phone has/had been damaged and it could not be repaired under warranty as he had breached warranty provisions. It is pleaded that complainant has concealed material facts that damage to his I-phone was solely attributable to his own action which is/was in breach of terms and conditions of Apple warranty. Further, it is plead

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
hat complainant has concealed material facts that damage to his I-phone was solely attributable to his own action which is/was in breach of terms and conditions of Apple warranty. Further, it is pleaded that manufacturer cannot be made liable until it is proved by adducing expert evidence that there was any manufacturing defect and present case is not related to any manufacturing defect. It is pleaded that complainant had met with accident in November-2016 and device's display was damaged; since device was allegedly insured by OP No.3/insurer, so liability is of OP No.3 to repair or replace it, as per terms of insurance policy agreed between OP No.3 and complainant. OP No.4 never tried to deny any service to complainant, in fact, he never complained about i-Phone being faulty of having manufacturing defects in it. It is further submitted that as per warranty policy, complainant should visit an Apple Authorized Service Provider to diagnose his device and seek for its repair or replacement. However, he did not visit any service provider and allowed third party intervention rendering device out of warranty. Basically, on these pleas, dismissal of complaint has been prayed.
6.      Complainant as well as OP No. 4 led their respective evidence, oral as well as documentary.
7.      On analyzing the same; learned District Consumer Commission-Sirsa has allowed complaint vide impugned o

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
plainant as well as OP No. 4 led their respective evidence, oral as well as documentary.
7.      On analyzing the same; learned District Consumer Commission-Sirsa has allowed complaint vide impugned order dated 14.12.2018 and directed OPs No.1 to 3 to get mobile of complainant repaired without any cost and to make it defect free, even by replacing any part and hand over mobile handset to complainant within 15 days from date of receipt of copy of order. In case, it is found that mobile handset is not repairable, then OPs No.1 to 3 shall be liable to give replacement of mobile with new one of same make and model within further period of 15 days or in the alternate to refund price of mobile in question. OP No.2 was also directed to refund Rs.2,495/- charged by it, to complainant. Rs.3000/- has been awarded to complainant as compensation and litigation expenses.
8.      Feeling aggrieved; OP No.1/dealer has filed this appeal. In proceedings of this appeal, respondents No. 1 to 3 were proceeded against ex-parte vide order dated 28.11.2023 of this Commission. Record of complaint case too has been perused. None has appeared on behalf of appellant/dealer and consequently, there has been no assistance from appellant side, so far as text of memorandum of this appeal is concerned, so, this Commission proceeds ahead to dispose of this appeal by itself perusing the averments raised in memor

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
assistance from appellant side, so far as text of memorandum of this appeal is concerned, so, this Commission proceeds ahead to dispose of this appeal by itself perusing the averments raised in memorandum of appeal.
9.      It has been stated in memorandum of this appeal by appellant/OP No. 1/Shree Satyam Mobiles that impugned order dated 14.12.2018 is illegal. Major fact has not been properly appreciated by learned District Consumer Commission that appellant herein had sold mobile set to complainant in sealed packed condition, as it has/had received from manufacturer. There was no warranty given by appellant/dealer to complainant. Guarantee/warranty, if any, is given by manufacturer alone, in case, there is any manufacturing defect in the purchased mobile handset, as it has been so mentioned in the Bill No. 22444 of 23.02.2016. Appellant never asked complainant to get insurance cover qua purchased mobile set, as it is not an authorized agent of any insurance company. It is pleaded that Bill of subject mobile mentions that all guarantee/warranty will be provided by the company. Inter alia on these pleas; acceptance of appeal has been prayed.
10.    On the other hand; respondent No. 4 has urged that no liability has been fastened upon manufacturer as there was no manufacturing defect in the subject mobile phone. Damage to it has/had been caused by complainant himself due to mis

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
. 4 has urged that no liability has been fastened upon manufacturer as there was no manufacturing defect in the subject mobile phone. Damage to it has/had been caused by complainant himself due to mishandling of handset which allegedly fell from his pocket. It is urged that on given facts there is no warranty attracted for subject mobile handset.
11.    Admittedly, subject mobile phone set has/had been purchased from appellant/dealer on 23.02.2016 by complainant-Jagsir Singh for Rs.49,900/- as it is so evident from perusal of invoice dated 23.02.2016-Ex.C-6. Complainant has alleged that his mobile phone handset got damage due to its fall from his pocket in month of November-2016. Its display screen suffered damage and it became completely dead. There is no plea that damage mobile handset was ever handed to appellant/dealer for repair purpose by coordinating with manufacturer. Even manufacturer/Apple India in its written version has specifically stated that damaged mobile phone was never brought by complainant for its inspection by Apple authorized service provider. As per plea of complainant, he had handed over the damage mobile phone handset to OP No. 2/insurer on 05.11.2016.  Consequently, only insurer/respondent No. 2 herein was to explain as to what had happened thereafter on allegedly receiving mobile handset from complainant, but said respondent No. 2/insurer has chosen n

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text: sequently, only insurer/respondent No. 2 herein was to explain as to what had happened thereafter on allegedly receiving mobile handset from complainant, but said respondent No. 2/insurer has chosen not to raise any contest to the complaint by not appearing, either before learned District Consumer Commission or in proceedings of this appeal. In wake of this fact, there is gross deficiency in service only on the part of OPs No. 2 (insurer-Appasdaily Mobile Protection). OP No.1-dealer/appellant herein has/had only sold the mobile handset to complainant in sealed packet as it has/had received from manufacturer. Complainant had not delivered the damaged mobile handset to OP No. 1/dealer/appellant herein. Matter does not end here. Sale Invoice Ex.C-6 dated 23.02.2016 expressly recites by mentioning attention that "Mobile will carry only warranty, not guarantee and warranty would be provided only by company's service centre". Admittedly, appellant is only a dealer and not service centre. Hence, appellant/dealer is completely is absolved of any liability with regard to damaged mobile phone handset. This being so, collectively, at judicial pedestal, there would be no liability of dealer (OP No. 1/appellant) to answer any claim of complainant, because of damage caused to mobile phone set due to its fall from complainant himself. The learned District Consumer Commission has committed a f

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
P No. 1/appellant) to answer any claim of complainant, because of damage caused to mobile phone set due to its fall from complainant himself. The learned District Consumer Commission has committed a fallacy to hold appellant herein/dealer being liable along with others OPs No. 2 & 3. There is neither any deficiency in service on the part of appellant/M/s Shree Satyam Mobile nor any unfair trade practice on its part in view of above factual scenario. Accordingly, findings of learned District Consumer Commission in its order dated 14.12.2018, against appellant herein/dealer cannot legally sustain and same are hereby set aside qua appellant herein/dealer only. Complainant can only raise his grievance qua other OPs, who too have been held liable by learned District Consumer Commission in its order dated 14.12.2018.
12.    As a sequel thereto, this appeal of appellant/dealer is allowed. Impugned order dated 14.12.2018 passed by learned District Consumer Commission-Sirsa is hereby set aside qua appellant/dealer alone. It would continue to hold its light of day, so far as other OPs are concerned who have been held liable by learned District Consumer Commission-Sirsa and complainant can legally enforce the impugned order dated 14.12.2018 qua them by adopting due recourse of law.
13.    Statutory amount of Rs.25,000/- deposited by appellant at the time of filing of this appeal be refund

title: Shree Satyam Mobiles vs Jagsir Singh And Others on 19 December, 2024
text:
gally enforce the impugned order dated 14.12.2018 qua them by adopting due recourse of law.
13.    Statutory amount of Rs.25,000/- deposited by appellant at the time of filing of this appeal be refunded to it, after due identification and verification as per rules and on expiry of period meant for further appeal /revision, if any.
14.    Application(s) pending, if any stand disposed of in terms of the aforesaid judgment.

1. This Second Appeal, preferred under
Section 51(2)
of the Consumer Protection Act,
2019 ["Act"], assails the Order dated 20.08.2025 passed by the Delhi State Consumer
Disputes Redressal Commission ["Impugned Order"], Delhi in First Appeal No.
A/292/2023, whereby the State Commission, while exercising its appellate jurisdiction,
 upheld the Order dated 31.03.2023 and the Review Order dated 23.05.2023 passed by the
District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Delhi in Complaint Case No. 10 of
2022, and dismissed the First Appeal preferred by the Appellant. Though the controversy
is modest in its monetary compass, it raises a question of some practical significance to
consumer jurisprudence, namely, whether a service-provider who has collected monies in
advance towards a subscription/brokerage plan, and has admittedly rendered service
commensurate with only a fraction of the said advance, can resist a claim for return of the
unutilized balance on the ground that the consumer has not independently established
"deficiency in service" in the classical, fault-based sense understood in cases involving
disputed allegations of negligent

d balance on the ground that the consumer has not independently established
"deficiency in service" in the classical, fault-based sense understood in cases involving
disputed allegations of negligent performance.
INTRODUCTION OF THE PARTIES

2.1 Sh. Ashok Kumar Goel ["Appellant"], is stated to be a senior citizen, aged about 75
years, resident of 1st Floor, 110-A/4, Krishna Nagar, Safdarjung Enclave, New Delhi-
110029, who subscribed, for himself and as Karta of "Ashok Kumar Goel, HUF," to an
advance-brokerage plan offered by the Respondent for trading in shares/securities. The
Appellant has appeared in person throughout these proceedings.
2.2 M/s Yes Securities (India) Limited ["Respondent"], having its office at First Floor,
Plot No. 1/9, West Patel Nagar, Opposite Metro Pillar No. 203, New Delhi-110008, is a
stock-broking entity engaged, inter alia, in the business of providing broking, research and
allied advisory services to its subscribers/clients, including the Appellant, for consideration,
and is accordingly a "service provider" within the meaning of
Section 2(42)
read with
Section 2(7)
of the Act, the Appellant being a "consumer" within the meaning of
Section
2(7)
thereof.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE

3.1 On 08.11.2019/11.11.2019, the Appellant subscribed to an advance-brokerage plan
bearing Plan Code "V-13" offered by the Respondent, by paying a sum of Rs. 5,90,000/-
(Rupees Five Lakh Ninety Thousand only), debited from the linked bank account of Ashok
Kumar Goel, HUF, upon the Respondent's assurance that seven categories of services,
namely, (i) Research on e-mail, (ii) Research on SMS, (iii) Call & Trade, (iv) Dedicated
Dealer, (v) Call with Expert, (vi) Portfolio Update, and (vii) Stock-specific Research, would
be made available to him during the subsistence of the plan.
3.2 On 11.11.2020, the said plan was renewed/extended for a further period, under Plan
Code "VSP-103" (recorded by the District Commission, on the material before it, as
"SVSP-32"), upon payment of a further sum of Rs. 12,980/- (Rupees Twelve Thousand
Nine Hundred Eighty only), the Respondent having represented telephonically that the
promised services would continue to be provided.
3.3 On the Respondent's own subscription-utilization records, annexed by it as Annexure
Rj-1 and Annexure-5 to its Reply filed before the State Commission, only 2.23% of the sum
of Rs. 5,90,000/- and 5.98% of the sum of Rs. 12,

subscription-utilization records, annexed by it as Annexure

leaving Rs. 5,76,430/- and Rs. 12,204/- respectively -- aggregating to Rs. 5,88,634/- --
unconsumed and lying with the Respondent.
3.4 By letter/notice dated 07.12.2021, the Appellant called upon the Respondent for refund
of the unutilized amount, together with compensation, alleging that the promised services
had not been provided. It is the Appellant's case that the said letter/notice was never
replied to or denied by the Respondent.
3.5 On 14.01.2022, the Appellant instituted Complaint Case No. 10 of 2022 before the
District Commission, praying, inter alia, for (i) refund of the unutilized subscription of Rs.
6,02,980/-, (ii) compensation of Rs. 6,10,000/-, (iii) interest @ 24% p.a., (iv) litigation costs
of Rs. 1,00,000/-, (v) return of an earlier subscription of Rs. 1,33,045/-, (vi) costs of Rs.
10,000/- for delaying proceedings, and (vii) a direction restraining the Respondent from
charging brokerage on delivery trades.
3.6 Notice of the Complaint was duly served upon the Respondent; the Respondent,
however, did not file a written reply before the District Commission and was accordingly
proceeded against ex-parte vide Order dated 06.07.2

8.1 SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE APPELLANT

8.1.1 The Appellant, appearing in person, at the outset submitted that the impugned Order

It was submitted that the decision in
B.F. Pushpaleela Devi v. State of
A.P.
, reported at (2002) 5 ALT 103, is a Full Bench decision of the High Court of Andhra
Pradesh rendered on the question whether an intra-court appeal lies, under Clause 15 of
the Letters Patent, against an order of a learned Single Judge declining to review his own
judgment. The concluding paragraph of
the said decision
, on which reliance was placed,
reads as under:
"54. By the impugned order, the learned single Judge

question of deficiency in service, refund of

. According to the Appellant, the citation of this

occurrence of negligence was in dispute and required affirmative proof; it does not,
according to the Appellant, apply to a case suc

that the ratio extracted above is confined to a case where the very

8.2.3 As regards the second decision, the Respondent placed principal reliance upon the
following paragraphs of
SGS India Ltd. v. Dolphin International Ltd.
, 2021 SCC OnLine
 SC 879, for the proposition that the onus of proving deficiency in service lies squarely upon
the complainant, and that in the absence of discharge of such onus, the opposite party
cannot be held liable:
"19. The onus of proof of deficiency in service is on the
 complainant in the complaints under the
Consumer
 Protection Act, 1986
. It is the complainant who had
 approached the Commission, therefore, without any
 proof of deficiency, the opposite party cannot be held
 responsible for deficiency in service."
"22. ...The onus of proof that there was deficiency in
 service is on the complainant. If the complainant is able
 to discharge its initial onus, the burden would then shift
 to the Respondent in the complaint. The rule of
 evidence before t

deficiency in

 to discharge its initial onus, the burden would then shift

8.2.4 On the strength of the above, the Respondent submitted that the concurrent findings
of the District Commission and the State Commission, both of which applied the ratio in
SGS India Ltd.
(supra) to hold that the Appellant had failed to discharge the initial onus of
proving deficiency in service, warranted no interference, and that the Second Appeal,
being devoid of merit, was liable to be dismissed.
ISSUES ARISING FOR CONSIDERATION
9. On a conspectus of the pleadings, the impugned Orders and the submissions advanced,
the following issues arise for the consideration of this Commission:
(i) Whether the impugned Order dated 20.08.2025 of the State Commission suffers from
any error warranting interference in the exercise of this Commission's jurisdiction under
Section 51(2)
of the Act?
(ii) Whether the two judgments relied upon before the State Commission, viz.
B.F.
Pushpaleela Devi v. State of A.P.
and
SGS India Ltd. v. Dolphin International Ltd.
, were
correctly applied so as to defeat the entirety of the Appellant's claim?
(iii) Whether the District Commissi

.
Pushpaleela Devi v. State of A.P.
and
SGS India Ltd. v. Dolphin International Ltd.
, were
correctly applied so as to defeat the entirety of the Appellant's claim?
(iii) Whether the District Commission and the State Commission erred in treating the
Appellant's claim for refund of the unutilized/unconsumed balance of the advance
subscription as indistinguishable from, and as governed by the same onus-of-proof
 standard applicable to, a claim of qualitative "deficiency in service"?
(iv) Whether, on the admitted documentary record -- including Annexure Rj-1 and
Annexure-5 to the Respondent's own Reply -- the Appellant is entitled to refund of the
unutilized balance of the advance brokerage/subscription paid by him, irrespective of the
fate of his other claims?
ANALYSIS

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
to the Respondent's own Reply -- the Appellant is entitled to refund of the
unutilized balance of the advance brokerage/subscription paid by him, irrespective of the
fate of his other claims?
ANALYSIS

10.1 We have heard the Appellant in person and Learned Counsel for the Respondent,
and have perused the record, including the impugned Orders, the pleadings and the
documents relied upon by both sides.
10.2 We may first deal with the two decisions relied upon before the State Commission.
The decision in
B.F. Pushpaleela Devi v. State of A.P.
, reported at (2002) 5 ALT 103, is a
Full Bench decision of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh, rendered on the question
whether an intra-court appeal under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent lies against an order
of a learned Single Judge declining to review his own judgment. The ratio of that decision
turns entirely upon the appeal ability of an order refusing review under the Letters Patent,
and has no bearing upon any question of deficiency of service, refund of subscription, or
unfair trade practice arising under consumer law. We find force in the Appellant's
submission that reliance on this decision, being unconnected with the subject matter of the
lis, does not advance the case of the Respondent, and, with respect, ought not to have
found mention as a precedent bearing upon the merits of a consumer dispute of this
nature.
10.3 The second de

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
the
lis, does not advance the case of the Respondent, and, with respect, ought not to have
found mention as a precedent bearing upon the merits of a consumer dispute of this
nature.
10.3 The second decision,
SGS India Ltd. v. Dolphin International Ltd.
, 2021 SCC
OnLine SC 879 (Civil Appeal No. 5759 of 2009, decided on 06.10.2021), lays down the
well-settled position, reiterating the earlier decision in
Ravneet Singh Bagga v. KLM
Royal Dutch Airlines & Anr.
, (2000) 1 SCC 66, that:
"19. The onus of proof of deficiency in service is on the
 complainant in the complaints under the
Consumer
 Protection Act, 1986
. It is the complainant who had
 approached the Commission, therefore, without any
 proof of deficiency, the opposite party cannot be held
 responsible for deficiency in service."
"22. ...The onus of proof that there was deficiency in
 service is on the complainant. If the complainant is able
 to discharge its initial onus, the burden would then shift
 to the Respondent in the complaint. The rule of
 evidence before the civil proceedings is that the onus
 would lie on the person who would fail if no evidence is
 led by the other side."
10.4 The correctness of the above proposition is not in doubt, and it binds this
Commission. What has, however, escaped the attention of the fora below is that the ratio
in
SGS India Ltd.
(supra) was rendered in the context of a claim of neg

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
tion is not in doubt, and it binds this
Commission. What has, however, escaped the attention of the fora below is that the ratio
in
SGS India Ltd.
(supra) was rendered in the context of a claim of negligence in the
performance of a specific, disputed act -- namely, whether the inspection agency had
been negligent in certifying the quality of a consignment of groundnuts at the time of
loading, a matter on which the evidence was squarely at issue between the parties and
which the complainant therein was unable to substantiate. The present case, in the limited
respect with which we are concerned, stands on a different footing. The claim for refund of
the unutilized balance of the advance subscription is not founded upon a disputed
allegation of negligence in the performance of a specific act; it is founded upon an
arithmetical and documentary fact -- the extent of utilization of the subscription -- which is
not disputed by the Respondent and which stands established from the Respondent's own
record, viz. Annexure Rj-1 and Annexure-5 to its Reply, a record which the District
Commission itself noticed while recording the facts of the case (Order dated 31.03.2023,
Para-5). Where a fact stands established from the opposite party's own record, the
question of onus becomes academic; the initial onus, even if it lay upon the Appellant,
stood discharged the moment the Respondent's own ann

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
tands established from the opposite party's own record, the
question of onus becomes academic; the initial onus, even if it lay upon the Appellant,
stood discharged the moment the Respondent's own annexures corroborated the extent of
utilization of the subscription.
10.5 It bears emphasis that a claim for refund of an unutilized advance is, in substance,
distinguishable from a claim of qualitative "deficiency in service." A subscriber who pays an
advance sum for services to be rendered over a defined period, and who is subsequently
found, on the service-provider's own record, to have utilized only a marginal fraction of that
advance, has an independent and freestanding entitlement to the return of the
unconsumed balance, irrespective of whether a separate case of qualitative deficiency in
the services actually rendered is made out. To hold otherwise would permit a service-
provider to retain monies for which no corresponding service has been, or realistically can
be, rendered -- a result productive of unjust enrichment of the service-provider at the
expense of the consumer, which the beneficial and welfare character of the Act was never
intended to countenance.
10.6 In this connection, it is apposite to recall the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in
Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
, (1994) 1 SCC 243, wherein it
was authoritatively held as under:
"The provis

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
ion, it is apposite to recall the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in
Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
, (1994) 1 SCC 243, wherein it
was authoritatively held as under:
"The provisions of the Act thus have to be construed in
 favour of the consumer to achieve the purpose of
 enactment as it is a social benefit oriented legislation.
 The primary duty of the court while construing the
 provisions of such an Act is to adopt a constructive
 approach subject to that it should not do violence to the
 language of the provisions and is not contrary to the
 attempted objective of the enactment."
10.7 Adopting the above constructive and purposive approach, we are of the considered
view that the fora below fell into error in treating the entirety of the Appellant's claim --
including the discrete claim for refund of the unutilised balance -- as governed by, and
defeated under, the onus-of-proof standard properly applicable to disputed allegations of
negligent or qualitatively deficient performance. The unutilised balance, amounting to Rs.
5,76,430/- (out of Rs. 5,90,000/- paid on 11.11.2019) and Rs. 12,204/- (out of Rs. 12,980/-
paid on 11.11.2020), aggregating to Rs. 5,88,634/-, stands substantiated by the
Respondent's own record and remains, on the material placed before us, unrebutted by
any evidence to the contrary.
10.8 We may also note, without returning any fina

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
,634/-, stands substantiated by the
Respondent's own record and remains, on the material placed before us, unrebutted by
any evidence to the contrary.
10.8 We may also note, without returning any final finding thereon since it is not essential
to the disposal of this Appeal, that Condition No. 8 appended to the subscription plan,
which purports to permit the Respondent to discontinue the plan "for any reason without
giving prior intimation to clients," is a term of a kind that has attracted judicial disapproval
where included in a standard-form contract offered to a consumer with no meaningful
power to negotiate its terms. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Central Inland Water
Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly
, AIR 1986 SC 1571 : (1986) 3 SCC
156, held as under:
"...the courts will not enforce and will, when called upon to
 do so, strike down an unfair and unreasonable contract, or
 an unfair and unreasonable clause in a contract, entered
 into between parties who are not equal in bargaining
 power... It will also apply where a man has no choice, or
 rather no meaningful choice, but to give his assent to a
 contract or to sign on the dotted line in a prescribed or
 standard form..., however unfair, unreasonable and
 unconscionable a clause in that contract or form or rules
 may be."
We leave the question of the validity of Condition No. 8 open for examination in an
a

ard form..., however unfair, unreasonable and
 unconscionable a clause in that contract or form or rules
 may be."
We leave the question of the validity of Condition No. 8 open for examination in an
appropriate proceeding, as the limited relief we propose to grant does not require its
adjudication.
10.9 We may further note that the retention of monies received for a purpose that has
substantially failed, without corresponding consideration having passed, offends a basic
principle of restitution recognised in Indian law even outside the specific framework of
consumer legislation -- that a person who has received money without corresponding
consideration cannot, in equity and good conscience, be permitted to retain it. This
principle finds recognition in the interpretation placed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on
Section 72
of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, in
Sales Tax Officer, Banaras v. Kanhaiya
Lal Mukundlal Saraf
, AIR 1959 SC 135, wherein it was observed as under:
"
Section 72
of the Indian Contract Act is in the following
 terms: 'A person to whom money has been paid, or anything
 delivered by mistake or under coercion, must repay or return
 it.' As will be observed the section in terms does not make
 any distinction between a mistake of law or a mistake of
 fact. The term 'mistake' has been used without any
 qualification or limitation whatever and comprises within its
 sco

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
in terms does not make
 any distinction between a mistake of law or a mistake of
 fact. The term 'mistake' has been used without any
 qualification or limitation whatever and comprises within its
 scope a mistake of law as well as a mistake of fact."
"Held, that the term 'mistake' in
Section 72
of the Indian
 Contract Act comprises within its scope a mistake of law as
 well as a mistake of fact and that, under that section a party
 is entitled to recover money paid by mistake or under
 coercion, and if it is established that the payment...has been
 made by the party labouring under a mistake of law, the
 party receiving the money is bound to repay or return it
 though it might have been paid voluntarily, subject,
 however, to questions of estoppel, waiver, limitation or the
 like."
10.9.1 Though rendered in the context of recovery of tax paid under a mistake of law, the
decision illustrates the wider principle, applicable with equal force by analogy, that the law
does not permit one party to retain money received by it where the corresponding basis for
such retention -- whether described as consideration, contractual entitlement, or service
actually rendered -- does not, in fact or in law, subsist. This general principle reinforces,
 rather than displaces, the more specific and beneficial relief available to a consumer under
the Act.
10.10 We accordingly hold that the District

title: Ashok Kumar Goel S/O. P.C.Goel vs Yes Securities India Ltd on 22 July, 2026
text:
in law, subsist. This general principle reinforces,
 rather than displaces, the more specific and beneficial relief available to a consumer under
the Act.
10.10 We accordingly hold that the District Commission and the State Commission erred in
dismissing the Complaint and the First Appeal, respectively, in their entirety, without
independently examining and granting the Appellant's claim, at the very least, for return of
the unutilized/unconsumed balance of the advance subscription paid by him, which stands
established from the record and is not seriously in dispute. To this limited extent, the
impugned Orders cannot be sustained and are liable to be set aside. We, however, find no
material on the record before us to independently sustain the Appellant's further claims for
compensation, interest at the rate claimed and the other ancillary reliefs prayed for, which
were declined by the fora below for want of proof of deficiency in the qualitative sense, and
we decline to disturb the said findings on those limited aspects.
Order

The Air India
preferred appeal F.A. No. 943/2008 contending
that alternative arrangements were made
for their travel to Singapore. There was no deficiency in service on their
part. In view of position of the flights, some of the passengers were off loaded and
alternative arrangements were made and
on that score it cannot be said that
there was deficiency in service. Therefore, they prayed that the appeal be
allowed.
It is an
undisputed fact that the complainants purchased three confirmed tickets for their journey from
 Hyderabad to Singapore through R1
booking agent of R2 in a non-stop flight
No. 424 on 11.5.2002 at 9.20 a.m. operated by Air India. The journey time was 4-1/2 hours. It is also not in dispute that by the time
they reached the air port at 6.45 p.m. the Air India expressed its inability to
accommodate them on the ground that the flight was full. No doubt, when the Air India offered
alternative flight in the evening at
10.00 p.m. on the same night, however
the flight being from Hyderabad-Mumbai-Singapore via Chennai, as they have no other go they traveled in the
said flight. Again they reached the air
port at 7.00 p.m. at Hyderabad, boarded the
Mumbai flight at 10.00 p.m. and since there was no connecting flight they sat
in the Mumbai Air port up to 02.30 a.m. They boarded another flight at
2.30 a.m. and reached Chennai at 04.30 a.m. Again they boarded the

title: Thomas Cook India Ltd Hyderabad vs . Vuppala Venkateswarlu And 3 Others ... on 9 September, 2008
text:
10.00 p.m. and since there was no connecting flight they sat
in the Mumbai Air port up to 02.30 a.m. They boarded another flight at
2.30 a.m. and reached Chennai at 04.30 a.m. Again they boarded the flight
at Chennai at 05.30 a.m. and ultimately
reached Singapore at 12.00
noon i.e. on 12.5.2002. Undoubtedly, this is an unnecessary and forced travel. They must have felt inconvenience waiting for
long hours in the air ports as well as
traveling for long hours. This would undoubtedly cause mental agony and physical strain etc. 

 

  

 

The journey to Singapore is on an
international flight. Necessarily the
complainants have to have visa for the
journey. This must have been informed to the authorities
at the time when the immigration check was made.
It is the duty of the booking
agent to see that confirmed tickets are issued and the complainants were able to take the
boarding passes. When the complainants informed the booking
agent for not accommodating them on the ground that the flight was full, the
agent did not respond nor question Air India, as to why confirmed tickets were given. Equally, the Air India did not give any plausible
explanation as to why it could give
confirmed tickets when

title: Thomas Cook India Ltd Hyderabad vs . Vuppala Venkateswarlu And 3 Others ... on 9 September, 2008
text:
nd nor question Air India, as to why confirmed tickets were given. Equally, the Air India did not give any plausible
explanation as to why it could give
confirmed tickets when 

 

  

 

  

 

  

 

flight was
full. Undoubtedly, selling tickets more than the seats provided
in the air flight, would amount not only to deficiency in service but also an
unfair trade practice, obviously, to see
that the passengers would not purchase any other flights. The Air India did not choose to contest the
matter when it has received the notice.
It did not even choose to reply for the legal notice issued by the
complainants. Necessarily, adverse inference has to be drawn against
their plea. Even in the appeal there was
no plausible explanation as to why the complainants could not be
accommodated in their direct
flight. Arranging an alternative flight
could not be a solace for the complainants, more so, traveling a tedious
journey for 14 hours instead of
4-1/2 hours on a non-stop flight for which they have taken the tickets. From the contentions taken by both the
appellants, one fact is clear that they could not give any plausible
explanation as to why the Air India had sold more tickets than the seats that it could
accommodate, nor the booking agent for not taking up the cause of the
complainants, when it sold the confirmed tickets. The
duty of the booking agent would not stop on issuing con

title: Thomas Cook India Ltd Hyderabad vs . Vuppala Venkateswarlu And 3 Others ... on 9 September, 2008
text:
seats that it could
accommodate, nor the booking agent for not taking up the cause of the
complainants, when it sold the confirmed tickets. The
duty of the booking agent would not stop on issuing confirmed tickets. In case the confirmed tickets were not honoured, it was his duty to find out the
reasons and see that the passengers to
whom the tickets were sold were adequately compensated.
A strange contention was taken that the complainants
could have cancelled their journey, took
refund of the amount instead of
pursuing alternative recourse. It is not for them to suggest the alternative. The
complainants for the reasons best known
had arranged their travel to Singapore. They intend to meet their son and family
members more so on weekends. If they do not travel it may also entails refusal of visa. The postponement cannot be done immediately. As the complainants had no other go, they have
taken the ordeal
of
traveling in a circuitous manner.
The question of
traveling with protest will not arise. The complainants are at liberty to claim
compensation for the inconvenience caused due to loss of time. Had
the Air India contended that there was technical failure or some other
ground that was beyond their
control one can understand and could exonerate by stating that it was
beyond their control. Evidently flight 424 from Hyderabad to Singapore left Hyderabad on time, with passengers f

title: Thomas Cook India Ltd Hyderabad vs . Vuppala Venkateswarlu And 3 Others ... on 9 September, 2008
text:
was beyond their
control one can understand and could exonerate by stating that it was
beyond their control. Evidently flight 424 from Hyderabad to Singapore left Hyderabad on time, with passengers full. The complainants could not be accommodated on
the ground that the flight was full. Neither
the agent nor the Air India could not have sold the confirmed tickets. This amounts to deficiency in service. The plea that the terms and conditions on the ticket would absolve them from their
liability were all specious, they would not in any way
restrict debarring the complainant from laying the claim. In the
very invoice under the liability of the agent, it is mentioned that its liability is restricted to making reservation, issue of Travelers Cheques etc. The
liability will cease on issuing travel documents, tickets to the customers. We do not see how the liability of the agent
is absolved when the Air India did not
honour the confirmed tickets and accommodate the complainants in the
flight. It is for them to rectify the
problem and see that the passengers who
had been given confirmed tickets board the flight. In case of any eventuality or any difficulty
encountered by the passengers, it has to be resolved
by the agent in such
circumstances. The Air India has no defense, in fact, and
rightly it did not choose to contest. Even in the appeal no defense, much less plausible defense was

title: Thomas Cook India Ltd Hyderabad vs . Vuppala Venkateswarlu And 3 Others ... on 9 September, 2008
text:
has to be resolved
by the agent in such
circumstances. The Air India has no defense, in fact, and
rightly it did not choose to contest. Even in the appeal no defense, much less plausible defense was
raised from issuing boarding passes to the complainant and taking them in
another flight. This is a case of clear deficiency in service
on their part. The Dist. Forum has awarded Rs. 10,000/- to
the complainants for the ordeal suffered
by the complainants on the journey. Because of the conduct of the respondents, the
complainants were denied their pleasure of seeing their children and spending more time with them. The
compensation that was granted was modest and reasonable. We do not see any merits in the appeals.
In the result, the appeals are dismissed with
costs computed at Rs. 2,500/- each.

or respondent No.2: Ex parte.
JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL, PRESIDENT:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant/opposite

party No.1 against the order dated 13.12.2016 passed by District

Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Jalandhar (in short, "the
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 2
District Forum"), whereby the complaint filed by Daler Singh,

respondent No.1/complainant, under
Section 12
of the Consumer

Protection Act, 1986 was partly accepted and opposite parties were

directed to repair the mobile set of the complainant and return the

same to him within 15 days from the date of receipt of copy of the

order. They were further directed to pay compensation of ₹5,000/-

for harassment and mental agony.
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties will

be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Forum.

Facts of the complaint:
3. Brief facts, as averred in the complaint, are that the

complainant purchased from opposite party No.1 one mobile (YU

YUPHORIA ON ANDROID, BUFFED STEEL) B015W4UQJS

bearing Serial No.911476050250620, vide Invoice dated 6.10.2015,

Ex. C-1, for a sum of ₹6,499/- including taxes. It is averred that after

some time the mobile phone started giving trouble. The complainant

contacted opposite party No.1-Company. Then the complainant was

informed to approach opposite party No.2, which is the Service

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
text:
ter

some time the mobile phone started giving trouble. The complainant

contacted opposite party No.1-Company. Then the complainant was

informed to approach opposite party No.2, which is the Service

Centre of the Manufacturer-Company i.e. opposite party No.1.

Accordingly the complainant approached opposite party No.2 on

18.7.2016 and explained the problem; as a result of which opposite

party No.2 issued Job Card No.2122046-0716-24455337 dated

18.7.2016 and sent the mobile phone to the Company by making a

report regarding the problem i.e. "Power Switches Off". The

complainant thereafter visited opposite party No.2 i.e. Service Centre

on various dates and his mobile phone was received at Service
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 3
Centre on 9.8.2016. However, it did not work again. Opposite party

No.2-Service Centre again issued Job Card No.2122046-0816-

24844025 dated 9.8.2016. The complainant was assured that the

same will be repaired or replaced within 15 days but they did not do

anything upto 22nd of August 2016. The complainant continued to

remain in touch with opposite party No.2-Service Centre but no

response was given. The mobile phone was under warranty.

Despite repeated requests neither it was repaired nor replaced.

Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties, the

complainant filed the present complaint to provide him new mobile

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
text:
pite repeated requests neither it was repaired nor replaced.

Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties, the

complainant filed the present complaint to provide him new mobile

phone in lieu of the previous mobile phone along with compensation

of ₹20,000/- for mental tension and harassment.
4. Notice was given to the opposite parties but despite service

opposite parties did not come present and were proceeded against

ex parte by the District Forum.
Finding of the District Forum:
5. In order to prove his case, the complainant tendered into

evidence his affidavit as Ex.CA and documents Ex.C-1 to Ex.C-3.

After going through the same and hearing the complainant in person,

the District Forum partly accepted the complaint, as stated above,

vide impugned order. Hence, this appeal.
6. We have heard learned counsel for appellant/opposite party

No.1 and have carefully gone through the records of the case,

including the affidavits of Mrs. Komal Patwari, Authorised Signatory

of appellant-opposite party No.1 tendered in the appeal by way of

leading additional evidence.
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 4
Contention of appellant/opposite party No.1:
7. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the

appellant/opposite party No.1 that the appellant/opposite party No.1

is merely the seller on the website and the Company, who

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
text:
site party No.1:
7. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the

appellant/opposite party No.1 that the appellant/opposite party No.1

is merely the seller on the website and the Company, who

manufactured the mobile phone has not been impleaded as a party.

So appellant/opposite party No.1 is not responsible for payment and

repair of the same. The complaint is, thus, liable to be dismissed.

Consideration of Contentions:
8. We have given our thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the learned counsel for appellant/opposite party No.1.
9. Admittedly immediately after the purchase of mobile phone on

6.10.2015 it started giving problem and the same was brought to the

notice of opposite party No.1 from whom the complainant had

purchased the cell phone, vide Invoice Ex.C-1. The Job Card dated

18.7.2016 was given but after service, the cell phone was given to

the complainant on 9.8.2016. However, the same did not work

again. In fact, another Job Card No.2122046-0816-24844025 dated

9.8.2016 was given. Meaning thereby that when the cell phone was

handed over on 9.8.2016, it was not working at that particular point

of time. The complainant deposited the same with opposite party

No.2-Service Centre on the same very day. It was the duty of

opposite party No.1 to inform the manufacturer Company about the

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
text:
r point

of time. The complainant deposited the same with opposite party

No.2-Service Centre on the same very day. It was the duty of

opposite party No.1 to inform the manufacturer Company about the

defects in the mobile phone once the complainant had purchased

the mobile phone from it and should have claimed its rights from that

Company as that Company had not provided workable mobile phone

to the complainant. In these circumstances, though the
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 5
manufacturer-Company has not been impleaded as a party in the

present complaint but it becomes the duty of the dealer i.e. opposite

party No.1 from whom the complainant had purchased the mobile

phone to inform the manufacturer about the complaints of the

complainant. It is not the case of opposite party No.1 that they ever

made a complaint to the manufacturer from which they were/are

purchasing the mobile phones with regard to the defects in the

mobile phone of the complainant. In view of this, we are not satisfied

that the complaint should be dismissed on the ground of non-

impleadment of manufacturer-Company.
10. Since the purchase is from opposite party No.1 and the repair

was done by opposite party No.2, as advised by opposite party No.1,

therefore, opposite party No.1 is certainly liable for the same. In

view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
text:
s done by opposite party No.2, as advised by opposite party No.1,

therefore, opposite party No.1 is certainly liable for the same. In

view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

impugned order passed by the District Forum specifically when the

defect had occurred in the mobile phone within the warranty period.

However, it will be open to opposite party No.1-Dealer to claim its

rights from the manufacturer-Company from which it had purchased

the mobile phone. Moreover, opposite party No.1 has not annexed

any document on record from which Company it had purchased the

mobile phone nor made any application for impleading the

manufacturer-Company as a party before the District Forum or

before us. Certainly the complainant has suffered sufficiently for a

long period. So he is certainly entitled to the compensation so

awarded by the District Forum.
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 6
11. In view of our above discussion, we do not find any merit in the

present appeal and the same is hereby dismissed.
12. The appellant/opposite party No.1 had deposited a sum of

₹2,500/- at the time of filing of the appeal. This amount, along with

interest which has accrued thereon, if any, shall be remitted by the

registry to the District Forum, after the expiry of 45 days of the

sending of certified copy of the order to the parties. The complainant

title: Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017

which has accrued thereon, if any, shall be remitted by the

registry to the District Forum, after the expiry of 45 days of the

sending of certified copy of the order to the parties. The complainant

may approach the District Forum for the release of the above

amount and the District Forum may pass the appropriate order in this

regard.
13. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory period

due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL)

         The following order of the Commission was delivered by A. K. Tiwari, Acting President:
Being aggrieved by the order dated 25.07.2018 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chhindwara (for short 'District Commission) in C.C.No.101/2017 whereby the complaint filed by complainant/respondent no.1 has been allowed, the opposite party no.1/appellant-Shubham Electronics has filed this appeal.
2.                The facts of the case as narrated by the complainant/respondent no.1 (hereinafter referred to as 'complainant') are that She had purchased a 43
-2-
inch Samsung LED TV for a sum of Rs.46,000/- from the opposite party no.1. She after depositing Rs.25,000/- had obtained finance for a sum of Rs.21,000/- from the opposite party no.2-finance company.  The opposite party no.1's engineer installed the TV at her residence and when it was started it is found some lines are displaying on the screen. On complaint being made to the opposite party no.1-it is told that it was due to disc problem. The disc person told that it is company's fault. Again on complaint being made, the opposite party no.1 assured to replace the same within one month. But when the TV wa

title: Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
text:
hat it was due to disc problem. The disc person told that it is company's fault. Again on complaint being made, the opposite party no.1 assured to replace the same within one month. But when the TV was neither repaired nor replaced, the complainant alleging deficiency in service on behalf of opposite parties in supply sub-standard quality of TV approached the District Commission seeking refund of cost of TV or in alternate to replace the TV with new one along with compensation of Rs.10,000/- and costs.
3.                The opposite party no.1 in its reply before the District Commission denying the allegations made in the complaint submitted that after getting all the information, the complainant had purchased the subject TV. Authorised representative technician of the opposite party no.1 after installation started and had given all information regarding operation. After two days the complainant complained about display of lines on the screen. Salesman Krishna Chourasia approached the complainant's house and found that there was physical damage in the LED TV set. Service Engineer Arshad also after inspection found that the two panels of LED were damaged and photo system is also damaged which clearly goes to show that the complainant mishandled the same. In such
-3-
circumstances, the service engineer of the company and the employee of the opposite party no.1 informed her that i

title: Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
text:
aged which clearly goes to show that the complainant mishandled the same. In such
-3-
circumstances, the service engineer of the company and the employee of the opposite party no.1 informed her that in case of physical damage and water injury the company is not giving any guarantee/warranty to electronic appliances. The TV damaged due to negligent maintenance of the complainant for which the opposite party no.1 cannot be held liable. There has been no deficiency in service. It is therefore prayed that the complaint be dismissed.
4.                The District Commission allowing the complaint directed the opposite party no.1 to repair the subject LED TV of the complainant within a period of one month or in alternate refund the cost of LED TV Rs.46,000/- to complainant failing which the amount shall carry interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of order till payment. In addition, compensation of Rs.2,000/- with costs of Rs.1,000/- is also awarded.
5.                Heard learned counsel for the parties. Perused the record.
6.                Learned counsel for the appellant/opposite party no.1 argued that the complainant did not implead the service centre as a party to the case. The engineer of the service centre approached the complainant and therefore, it cannot be said that the complaint was not lodged with the service centre. He argued that the District Commission has wrongly concl

title: Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
text:
er of the service centre approached the complainant and therefore, it cannot be said that the complaint was not lodged with the service centre. He argued that the District Commission has wrongly concluded that it is responsibility of the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects pointed out in TV and the opposite party no.1 did not attempt to remove the same. In fact, the complainant wants to replace the penal which is not possible. The impugned order passed by the District Commission is against the law. He therefore prayed for setting aside the impugned order.
-4-
7.                Learned counsel for the complainant/respondent no.1 argued that the subject TV was suffering from defect from the day one of its installation. The employee and engineer of the opposite party no.1 inspected the said TV and found defects in the TV i.e. within warranty and therefore, the opposite party no.1 is liable to remove the defects or in alternative to refund the cost of the TV. He argued that the District Commission after appreciating the evidence available on record has rightly passed the impugned order. He therefore prayed for dismissal of appeal.
8.                Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having gone through the record as also the impugned order, we find that immediately after installation of TV defects were found in the TV and this fact was confirmed by Krishna Chour

title: Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
text:
r the parties and having gone through the record as also the impugned order, we find that immediately after installation of TV defects were found in the TV and this fact was confirmed by Krishna Chourasia, sales man and Engineer Arshad of the opposite party no.1 who found physical damage and click system damage. It is also not denied by the opposite party no.1 that there was no warranty/guarantee of two years on the said product. Thus when the subject TV was within warranty/guarantee period, it is the duty of the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects to the satisfaction of the complainant and when they failed to do so, they have committed deficiency in service.
9.                It is also pertinent to mention here that the opposite party no.1 failed to demonstrate by way of any documentary evidence that the TV got damaged by the complainant as also the physical damage and water injury does not cover under the warranty/guarantee period in case of electronic appliances.
-5-
10.               In view of the foregoing discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the District Commission has committed no error in allowing the complaint and directing the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects or in alternative refund the cost of the TV.  Accordingly, the impugned order passed by the District Commission is hereby affirmed.
11.               In the result, this appeal fails

title: Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
text:
emove the defects or in alternative refund the cost of the TV.  Accordingly, the impugned order passed by the District Commission is hereby affirmed.
11.               In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.  No order as to costs.
