13.     The complainant having filed a consumer complaint on or about 21/1/13 before the District Forum the same was contested by OP No. 2.  Although OP No. 1 and OP No. 2 were both represented by the same advocate, OP No. 1 chose not to contest the complaint by filing a written version and suffered an exparte order and thereafter chose not even to make any attempt to get the exparte order dated 28/06/13 set aside.
14.     The OP No. 2 in their written version took the plea that OP No. 2 was not in the business of manufacturing or repairing the handsets.  It pleaded that despite various requests made to the complainant to go to the authorized service centre at Margao, the complainant insisted for a new handset which is not as per the warranty.   OP No. 2 stated that the complain

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
ious requests made to the complainant to go to the authorized service centre at Margao, the complainant insisted for a new handset which is not as per the warranty.   OP No. 2 stated that the complainant had used the handset for a period of six months and suddenly started complaining about the same in the name of faulty handset.  OP No. 2 stated that the handset was under warranty and not under guaranty and therefore there was no question of any replacement as desired by the complainant and that under a warranty only a fault could be removed and there not be any replacement as alleged by the complainant and that the complainant was informed about the same that the complainant could approach the service centre at Margo for needful repairs.
15.     The case of the complainant is entirely based on the alleged promises made by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith, from the shop of OP No. 1, for replacement of the handset, by the former on 30/11/12 and by the latter by endorsement on purchase receipt on 14/12/12.  The complainant seems to be conscious that in terms of the warranty the defective parts were required to be repaired or replaced (para 25 of the affidavit) but his entire case for replacement is based on what Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith allegedly told him.  The complainant had stated the following in his affidavit in evidence:
" Therefore when the entire set stops working or overheats and is

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
nt is based on what Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith allegedly told him.  The complainant had stated the following in his affidavit in evidence:
" Therefore when the entire set stops working or overheats and is defective, the Company is bound to furnish me a replacement for the handset and this is exactly what was explained to me by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith."
"I say that I had never insisted for a new handset but was informed by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith that I was entitled for a new handset."
16.     The Lr. District Forum has proceeded to accept the case of the complainant by observing that:
"7. We observe that the written promise of replacement was made by Shri. Keith in the premises of OP No. 1; in effect, in his own turf, on his own grounds. At least one colleague, the other employee, Shri. Aman was then present. May be other employees, office peon etc. were also around. We hence find it unlikely that complainant and her husband could force these employees of OP No. 1 in their own premises to write down such promise against their will. We hence conclude that the senior employee, Shri. Keith, made this promise in writing due to the fact that he recognized complainant as a genuine customer whose grievance it was his duty to resolve."
"9.     There is no doubt that is a supplier is willing and able to repair a defective product, Consumer Fora should not needlessly order replacement.  Howeve

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
se grievance it was his duty to resolve."
"9.     There is no doubt that is a supplier is willing and able to repair a defective product, Consumer Fora should not needlessly order replacement.  However, in the present instance, not only have Opposite Parties been incapable of rectifying the admittedly defective  instrument, but at least one i.e. Opposite Party-1, has exhibited a markedly obvious preference to intentionally harassing Complainant by making false promises and committing dates promising action but repeatedly failing to keep them."
17.     The Lr. District Forum has discharged OP No. 2 and 3 from any liability.
18.     Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr. advocate of OP No. 1, would submit that OP No. 1 is only a retailer and not an authorized service centre of OP No. 3, who has an authorized service centre at Margao.  Lr. advocate submits that when the complainant came to their shop on 22/11/12, the complainant was told to go to the service centre at Margao but the complainant forced the employees of OP No. 1 to take the handset and send the same to the service centre.  Lr. advocate submits that next time the complainant and her husband came with another complaint that the handset was getting hot and made a hungama in the shop of OP No. 1.  Lr. advocate submits that Mr. Keith is not an employee of OP No. 1 but of OP No. 2.  He submits that on 14/12/12 the complainant and her

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
t was getting hot and made a hungama in the shop of OP No. 1.  Lr. advocate submits that Mr. Keith is not an employee of OP No. 1 but of OP No. 2.  He submits that on 14/12/12 the complainant and her husband compelled Mr. Keith to take the handset and forced to make the said endorsement that the handset was received for replacement.
The lr. advocate submits that the handset is now with the  police and they have filed a charge sheet not only against Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman but also the two partners of OP No. 1 .  Lr. advocate submits that the said endorsement made by Mr. Keith has no value in the eyes of law as   it  was  made  under  pressure.   Lr.  advocate  submits  that   the

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
of OP No. 1 .  Lr. advocate submits that the said endorsement made by Mr. Keith has no value in the eyes of law as   it  was  made  under  pressure.   Lr.  advocate  submits  that   the

 

 

 

 

 

complainant did not examine any expert to show that the handset had a manufacturing defect and a bare statement of the complainant that the handset had a defect could not have been accepted, and, in this context Lr. Adv. Shri. P. P. Singh had placed reliance on The Commercial Officer, M/s. Piaggio Greaves Vehicle Pvt. Ltd., & anr. vs. Ramakant Samal, & ors., 2014 (4) CPR 75 as well as on
Chaitanya Educational Society vs. The Manager, Eicher Motors Ltd. & Ors.
, 2014 (4) CPR 624.  Lr. advocate submits that the complainants had not filed any income tax returns to show what business losses they had sustained.  Regarding the impugned order, lr. advocate submits that the same is based on presumptions and assumptions which cannot have a place in rule of law and the order was passed without any expert opinion.  Lr. advocate submits that Lr. District Forum was not right in referring to the dictionary to know the meaning of the word "warranty" when the same was available under
Section 12(3)
of the Sales of Goods Act, 1930, as amended and has placed reliance on Svenska Handelsbanken vs. M/s. Indian Charge Chrome and others, AIR 1994 SC 626.  Lr. advocate submits that the complainant cunnin

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
f the Sales of Goods Act, 1930, as amended and has placed reliance on Svenska Handelsbanken vs. M/s. Indian Charge Chrome and others, AIR 1994 SC 626.  Lr. advocate submits that the complainant cunningly did not produce the warranty card when the complainant was seeking reliefs on the basis of the warranty.  The lr. advocate submits that the complainant sought replacement of the handset but has been awarded refund of sale price, after using the handset for more than seven months.
19.     On the other hand Shri. Kalokhe, (complainant's representative and husband, complainant's alter ago, if we may use that expression) concedes that the warranty was not produced on record but the same was shown to the Lr. District Forum.  Shri. Kalokhe concedes that the handset worked for about six months and that  Mr. Keith  and Mr. Aman are the salesman of OP No. 1 and this

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
he same was shown to the Lr. District Forum.  Shri. Kalokhe concedes that the handset worked for about six months and that  Mr. Keith  and Mr. Aman are the salesman of OP No. 1 and this

 

 

 

 

 

fact was conceded by Lr. Adv. Shri. P.P. Singh before the Lr. District Forum as reflected in para 5 of the impugned order.  Shri. Kalokhe concedes that on 22/11/12 Shri. Aman was reluctant to receive the handset but only when he was told that the complainant would give a police complaint for cheating that he accepted the same to be sent for repairs and on 30/11/12 Mr. Aman told him and the complainant that it was being sent to the Company for replacement.  Shri. Kalokhe submits that on 9/12/12 when the complainant and he went to collect the handset the said Mr. Aman was politely told that the police complaint would be lodged against him.  Shri. Kalokhe submits that on 14/12/12 Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman gave in writing that they had received the handset for replacement and as such they are bound to replace the same.  Shri. Kalokhe would submit that OP No. 1 was bound to replace the handset under vicarious liability of OP No. 3.
20.      There are certain misconceptions which need to be cleared before we proceed further.  Lr. District Forum was right in ignoring the decision of the National Commission dated 20/4/12 in R.P. No. 3780/2011 and the case of
General Manager, Telecom vs. M.

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
leared before we proceed further.  Lr. District Forum was right in ignoring the decision of the National Commission dated 20/4/12 in R.P. No. 3780/2011 and the case of
General Manager, Telecom vs. M. Krishnan
and anr. on which it is based, as not applicable to the facts of this case. The case proceeded exparte against OP No. 1 and  therefore, the complaint has to be decided, and now the present appeal, on the basis of the evidence produced by the complainant and OP No. 2.  Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman were found in the establishment of OP No. 1 and the complainant was bound to infer that they are employees of OP No. 1 who made the said alleged promises/endorsement on 14/12/12.  OP No. 2 did not state in their written version or in the affidavit in evidence that they were their employees  but  on the contrary Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr advocate who

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
on 14/12/12.  OP No. 2 did not state in their written version or in the affidavit in evidence that they were their employees  but  on the contrary Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr advocate who

 

 

 

 

 

was then appearing for OP No. 1 and OP No. 2 before the District Forum made a statement that Mr. Keith was the employee of OP No. 1 which statement is recorded in para 5 of the impugned order.  It is not the case of Shri. P. P. Singh, the lr. advocate, that the said statement is wrongly recorded, and if that be so, lr. advocate ought to have taken steps to get the statement duly corrected. Only because Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr. advocate, now appears only for OP No. 1, it has become convenient  for him to submit that Mr. Keith is the employee of OP No. 2.  Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith are the employees of OP No. 1 with whom the complainant had dealings when the complainant alongwith her husband visited the establishment of OP No. 1.  However, only because the complaint proceeded exparte against OP No. 1, does not mean that the version given by the complainant has to be accepted lock, stock and barrel or as a gospel truth (see II 2009 CPJ 40).  Complainant's version cAN be accepted only in case it is found to be probable.  Complainant's husband was always alongwith the complainant but has chosen not to file any affidavit to support the case of the complainant, his wife.  It is well settl

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
ase it is found to be probable.  Complainant's husband was always alongwith the complainant but has chosen not to file any affidavit to support the case of the complainant, his wife.  It is well settled that only self serving statements of a complainant bereft of any material on record are not sufficient to establish deficiency in service (see Ashwani Kumar, 2009(1) CPR 420).
21.
Section 12(3)
of the Sales of Goods Act may provide that a warranty is a stipulation collateral to the main purpose of the contract, the breach of which gives a rise to a claim for damages but not to a right to reject the goods and treat the contract as repudiated, but we have
Section 14
of the C.P. Act, which enables a District Forum to direct an OP to remove the defects or to replace the goods or refund the price or to order payment of compensation as contemplated  therein.   This legal position has been taken note of by

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
ect an OP to remove the defects or to replace the goods or refund the price or to order payment of compensation as contemplated  therein.   This legal position has been taken note of by

 

 

 

 

 

the Apex Court in Indochem Electronic & anr. vs. Additional Collector of Custom, (I) 2006 CPJ (1) in the following words:
"27.  Although in terms of sub
section 3
of
section 12
no right accrues to a purchaser to reject the goods on breach of stipulation of warranty,  the same would not mean that the extent of damages cannot be equivalent to the price of the goods in as much as such a power has specifically been conferred upon the Commission."
22.   A warranty is the manufacture's or seller's promise to stand behind the product, and, in this case it was given by OP No. 3, the manufacturer, to the complainant.  A warranty is not one of the essentials of sale but it is collateral undertaking and in this case was given by the manufacturer, OP No. 3, to the complainant, to repair the defective items, but not to replace the whole handset, at its sole discretion.
23.     The complainant argued before the Lr. District Forum that OP No. 2 importer was vicariously liable for the acts of its dealer, OP No. 1.  The complainant now argues that OP No. 3 is vicariously liable for the acts of OP No. 1.  The expression "vicarious" means "done or suffered by one person on behalf of another".  The

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text: aler, OP No. 1.  The complainant now argues that OP No. 3 is vicariously liable for the acts of OP No. 1.  The expression "vicarious" means "done or suffered by one person on behalf of another".  The concept of vicarious liability ordinary arises in master and servant relationship where the master is held liable for the acts of his servants.  A manufacturer cannot be held liable for the acts of his dealer or retailer.  The complainant's case that the complainant did not insist for a new handset but was informed by the said Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith that he would be entitled for one because the handset was over heating is a story which cannot be accepted as gospel truth without any corroboration.  Moreover, such a story appears to be improbable as it opposed to the warranty conditions. The complainant  knew,  and  in  any  event  ought to have known that in

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
ut any corroboration.  Moreover, such a story appears to be improbable as it opposed to the warranty conditions. The complainant  knew,  and  in  any  event  ought to have known that in

 

 

 

 

 

terms of the warranty, a defective unit alongwith the sales invoice was required to be brought or sent to the authorized service centre.  The endorsement made on the sales invoice on 22/11/12 clearly shows that the handset was received to be sent to the service centre.  The complainant accepted the handset duly repaired on 9/12/12 and there is nothing on record to say that the handset was not repaired. Subsequently, as per the complainant herself, the handset developed the problem of overheating and was again accepted to be sent to the authorized service centre on 14/12/12.  There is nothing on record to suggest that the handset was not repaired of the said overheating problem and OP No. 1 must have certainly got it back duly repaired by the service centre.  The complainant did not even find out whether it was working either on 22/12/12 or 24/12/12 before lodging the Police complaint on 26/12/12.  The Lr. District Forum observed, and in our view rightly, that if a supplier is willing and able to repair a defective product a consumer forum should not needlessly order replacement, but wrongly concluded, without any material on record, that the OPs were incapable of rectifying the d

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
and able to repair a defective product a consumer forum should not needlessly order replacement, but wrongly concluded, without any material on record, that the OPs were incapable of rectifying the defective instrument.  The facts on record clearly established that the handset had work well, without any problem for seven months and later, the two problems which it faced were attended to by OP No. 1 by sending it to the authorized service centre. We are inclined to believe that on both the occasions the handset was brought to OP No. 1, they had got it duly repaired, and this was as per the warranty given to the complainant by OP No. 3.
24.     The complainant and her husband are business people.  It is not their case that they did not know the scope of warranty given by OP No. 3.  It is also not their case that they did not know that as per terms  of  the  warranty  they  had to go either at Panaji or Margao to

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
d not know the scope of warranty given by OP No. 3.  It is also not their case that they did not know that as per terms  of  the  warranty  they  had to go either at Panaji or Margao to

 

 

 

 

 

the authorized service centre of OP No. 3.  Still they choose to go to the retailer, OP No. 1.
25.       In our view, the Lr. District Forum has entirely lost sight as to under  what  circumstances  the  so called promises or endorsements came to be made by the servants of OP No. 1, the said Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith.  On 22/11/12 when the complainant alongwith her husband went to the shop, they were told that it had to be sent to the service centre.  This was in conformity with the warranty.  Initially Mr. Aman refused to give a receipt but when threatened with filing a police complaint for cheating, the said Mr. Aman yielded and made an endorsement that he received the handset to be sent to the service centre.  Again, on 9/12/12 when the complainant and or her husband threatened Mr. Aman of lodging a cheating complaint that Mr. Aman handed over the repaired handset to the complainant.  The complainant would not have accepted a repaired handset on 9/12/12 in case the complainant was promised a replacement earlier.  Are we, therefore, to believe that Mr. Keith made the endorsement on 14/12/12 for replacement without any such threat from the complainant and/or her husband? Subsequent

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text: omised a replacement earlier.  Are we, therefore, to believe that Mr. Keith made the endorsement on 14/12/12 for replacement without any such threat from the complainant and/or her husband? Subsequently, the complainant indeed lodged a cheating complaint against Mr. Keith on 26/12/12.  If the complainant could get his way through on 22/11/12 and 9/12/12 by threats of filing police complaints for cheating, the only inference is that the complainant also got his way through on 14/12/12 by making a similar threat, or otherwise Mr. Keith would not have accepted the handset for replacement contrary to the warranty given to the handset. The probabilities of the case clearly suggest that replacement was promised by Mr, Keith out of fear of being implicated in a false criminal complaint of cheating and in  such  a  situation  the  said endorsement made on 14/12/12 is not

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
replacement was promised by Mr, Keith out of fear of being implicated in a false criminal complaint of cheating and in  such  a  situation  the  said endorsement made on 14/12/12 is not

 

 

 

 

 

binding on Mr. Keith and much less on OP No. 1. Secondly, no retailer or dealer would have accepted the handset for replacement when  the  liability,  if  any,  for repair or for replacement, if at all, was that OP No.3, the manufacturer, and the manufacturer in terms had agreed for such replacement.  As already stated the warranty was only for repair, not for replacement.  Suffice to state that the said Mr. Keith had also no authority from OP No. 1 to receive the handset for replacement, in as much as OP No. 1 had also no authority to receive the same on behalf of OP No. 3, for replacement.  The said endorsement dated 14/12/12  in  the  circumstances  does  not at all appear to have been out of free will but out of coercion issued by the complainant and/or her husband to lodge a police complaint for cheating which was eventually lodged on 26/12/12 even without ascertaining whether the handset was duly repaired of its heating problem.
26.     Lastly, we may observe that the handset had worked well for seven months or more without any defect.  It would not have worked, if it had manufacturing defect.  Complainant had not examined any expert to prove that it had any manufacturing d

title: Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
text:
ad worked well for seven months or more without any defect.  It would not have worked, if it had manufacturing defect.  Complainant had not examined any expert to prove that it had any manufacturing defect.  When the handset had network problem it was got repaired by OP No. 1 and handed over to the complainant on 9/12/12.  When the handset developed problem of overheating, the same was got repaired again.  The complainant and/or her husband did not even try to find out whether it was repaired or not but went and filed police complaint for cheating against the said Mr. Keith on 26/12/12.  OP No. 1 had tried to help the complainant, as a dealer, although the complainant was required to approach the authorized service centre.  The Lr. District Forum therefore was also not right in passing  the  impugned  order  for  full refund, after the handset was

 

 

 

 

 

used for seven months, and compensation of Rs. 25,000/- which would have enabled the complainant to purchase 4 of such sets.
27.     In view of the above discussion we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned order and proceed to dismiss the complaint but considering the facts with no order as to costs.     [HONABLE MR. JUSTICE N.A.Britto] PRESIDENT

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
. 

 

  

 

Also
At:

Ms. Rumnita
Mittal Member
1. Whether Reporters of local newspapers
be allowed to see the judgment?
2. To be referred to the Reporter or not?
Justice J.D. Kapoor, President (Oral)
1. Respondent
is running a department store in Sant Nagar, Burari. Since there was erratic power supply by the
Delhi Vidyut Board, he purchased two generator sets of different kws. from the
appellant at the cost of Rs. 1,80,000/- and Rs.2,40,960/-. The said generator sets carried a warranty of
one year. The generator set started
giving trouble from the very next day of installation. It is alleged that the appellant never cared
to attend to the problem and so much so was unable to rectify the snags. On 7th March,
 2001 when
the respondent started the set, the engine
of generator set bursted and almost all parts of the engine and alternator were
damaged. Inspite of this no set was
replaced and some broken accessories/parts were removed by respondent-1. The performance of the generator set was
deteriorated and went out of order. Consequently, he filed the instant complaint
for refund of the cost of generator sets on account of business loss.
2. While
allowing the complaint the District Forum has vide impugn

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
went out of order. Consequently, he filed the instant complaint
for refund of the cost of generator sets on account of business loss.
2. While
allowing the complaint the District Forum has vide impugned order dated
30.09.2003 directed the appellant to refund the aforesaid cost with interest @
9% and pay Rs. 2,000/- as cost of litigation.
Feeling aggrieved the appellant has preferred this appeal.
3. The
impugned order has been assailed firstly, on the ground that the appellant
being the manufacturer of the generator set was proceeded ex-parte and not given an opportunity of being heard
secondly, that the respondent-1 dealt with the dealer independently who was not
their dealer and did not purchase the set from the appellant and did not verify that the appellant was indeed
the authorized dealer and whether the
appellant was at all the manufacturer of any DG set, thirdly, that the respondent-1
fitted a different type of alternator viz. Stamford and there was mis-match
between the diesel engine of the appellant fitted in the DG set and the
alternator which was of a different make and lastly that the District Forum did
not obtain any expert opinion about mis-matching and manufacturing defect in
the DG set. Only expert engineer could have ascertained whether the
DG set was having some manufacturing defect.
5. In
our view none of the aforesaid contentions holds water. Once goods have

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
efect in
the DG set. Only expert engineer could have ascertained whether the
DG set was having some manufacturing defect.
5. In
our view none of the aforesaid contentions holds water. Once goods have a brand name a consumer is not expected to open
up each and every part to see whether it
bears stamford branded
name or not. The perusal of the impugned
order shows that engineers of the appellant had visited and had seen generator
set on some occasions and found some defect but they could not rectify. It was only after the burst that some parts were
destroyed in the process.
6. It is a misconceived notion that unless and until new goods
suffers from inherent manufacturing defect it cannot be held defective for the
purpose of replacement or for the purpose of refund of the cost or for the
purpose of refund of compensation as to the actual loss or injury suffered by
the consumer for the mental agony. The
quality and standard of every goods much less the branded new goods has to be
tested on the anvil of the definition of a word defect provided by
section 2(1)(f)
of the Consumer
Protection Act which means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the
quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be
maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or (under any
contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by the trader in any manner
whatsoever in rela

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
standard which is required to be
maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or (under any
contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by the trader in any manner
whatsoever in relation to any good.
7. If
a consumer after purchasing the branded new article starts visiting the dealer for
the service time and again and every
second or third day for removing one or other defects and if the job cards show
several defects, goods has to be held as
defective. It is not for the consumer to
engage an expert or engineer or some other expert to verify whether the goods
have manufacturing defect or not. He is a wronged person and to expect him to
incur unnecessary expenses in availing the services of an expert is too
much. The onus lies upon the trader or
manufacturer to show that their goods did not suffer from manufacturing
defect.
8. We
even go to the extent that even if the
manufacturer has a report in his favour that the goods does not have a
manufacturing defect, still he cannot escape
from the liability to compensate the consumer by
supplying defective goods and in terms of
Section 14(1)(d)
every
consumer is entitled to an amount as compensation as to the injury or actual
loss suffered by him due to the negligence of the opposite party. The word injury has a wide connotation in
terms of every remedy in the context of every contract. It was with an object to
inculc

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
tual
loss suffered by him due to the negligence of the opposite party. The word injury has a wide connotation in
terms of every remedy in the context of every contract. It was with an object to
inculcate high standard of quality or standard of the goods and the
efficiency in the service to be provided by the service provider that the
legislature defined the word defect in
a manner that any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality,
quantity, potency, purity or standards which is required to be maintained by or
under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or
implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to
any goods renders the goods defective.
9. Taking
over all view of the matter and finding
of fact returned by the District Forum as to the generator set having been
highly defective, the interest awarded by the District Forum in our view was not awardable because
interest is awardable only in those cases where there is a term of contract
between the parties or where there are equitable grounds. We have taken a view that ordinarily interest should be awarded in cases like fixed
deposits or by way of lump sum payment running into lacs towards purchase of
land or flats or wrongful rejection of insurance claims and not in those cases where the goods have been
sold against consideration and have been used by

title: Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
text:
payment running into lacs towards purchase of
land or flats or wrongful rejection of insurance claims and not in those cases where the goods have been
sold against consideration and have been used by the consumer reluctantly or grudgingly.
10. In
the result, we partly allow the appeal by retaining the order for refund of the
cost of the generator set and
substituting the interest by lump sum compensation of Rs. 20,000/- which shall include the
cost of litigation.
11. The aforesaid payment shall be made
within one month from the date of receipt of this order.
12. Bank
Guarantee/FDR if any, furnished by the appellant, be returned forthwith.
13. A
copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the
parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter
the file be consigned to Record room.
14. Announced
on 1st day of October, 2007.
(Justice J.D. Kapoor)

M.L. SAHNI, MEMBER
1. M/s Air India Ltd.-the
OP before the District Forum, have filed this appeal challenging Forums
order dated 04.06.2008 whereby the OP
(hereinafter referred to as the Appellant)
have been directed to pay to the Respondent (complainant) Rs. 87,667/- the price of the ticket , Rs.
1,00,000/- towards compensation for causing mental agony and harassment and Rs. 10,000/- towards cost of litigation, on variety of
grounds , inter alia,
that the father of the complainant
did not have proper authorization to file the consumer complaint and
that the District Forum awarded and exorbitant amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- towards compensation as against prayer of the complaint asking for Rs. 50,000/- for mental agony and harassment.
2. Briefly stated the facts of the case,
are that Respondent had booked return ticket from New
 York to Delhi for 26.01.2001 and
from Delhi to New York vide flight No. AI-III for 04.03.2001 via London with the
Appellant/OP under a highly concessional scheme from
its agent at United States.
The said ticket under the excursion fare was inter-alia
non-refundable and non-endorsable as was clearly ment

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
with the
Appellant/OP under a highly concessional scheme from
its agent at United States.
The said ticket under the excursion fare was inter-alia
non-refundable and non-endorsable as was clearly mentioned on the ticket
itself. The complainant/respondent
utilized the aforementioned ticket for one side and arrived in India on
26.01.2001.
3. According to the Appellant, Respondent through its agent
Mr. Anwar approached the tele-reservation
facility of the Appellant/OP and requested for postponement of the confirmed
ticket of return flight to New York
dated 04.03.2001 to 11.03.200. In view
of above request, the Appellant entered the details in its computer system and
a separate PNR number was generated for reservation on 11.03.2001. As a matter of policy and business prudence,
two bookings against the name of one person cannot be left open, therefore, the
system is made to provide a time frame within which the passenger has to decide
his option. The system for reservation granted a time limit on 13.02.2001 for
confirmation of date of the return flight and the same was communicated
instantly to the agent of the complainant/respondent. In view of non-confirmation, the ticket could
not have been left open endlessly and hence the system automatically cancelled
the entire PNR of the Respondent/complainant on the basis of expiry of time
limit. Respondent approached the
Appellant on 03.03

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
ve been left open endlessly and hence the system automatically cancelled
the entire PNR of the Respondent/complainant on the basis of expiry of time
limit. Respondent approached the
Appellant on 03.03.2001 for purchase of fresh ticket in the same flight i.e.
AI-111 for 04.03.2001. Due to peak season, the ticket of economy class was not
available in the flight in question and the same was conveyed to the Respondent
personally. Since no seat was available
in the economy class and keeping in view the urgency of the Respondent, he was
informed that the seats are only available in J-class category and if he wishes
he could avail the same. The Respondent opted for J-class ticket and the same
was made available to him on due payment.
4. Conversely, the case of the Respondent, as per his sworn
testimony filed before the Ld. District Forum in the form of Affidavit was that
he had not authorized Mr. Anwar for making request
for postponing of the confirmed O.K. Status ticket of the flight from
04.03.2001 to 11.03.2001. He had requested M/s South End Travel, New Delhi to enquire from Air India Authorities about the
position of booking for 11.3.2001 for New York
( USA).
On enquiring on telephone from Air India Reservation Representative for Air
India Flight IA -111 to New York,
the Representative of Air India Authorities intimated that there is no
possibility for 11.03.2001. He did not
know

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
e from Air India Reservation Representative for Air
India Flight IA -111 to New York,
the Representative of Air India Authorities intimated that there is no
possibility for 11.03.2001. He did not
know the alleged Shri Anwar
and he did not authorize anybody for postponement/ cancellation of the
confirmed O.K. Status ticket for 4.3.2001.
5. We
have heard the Ld. Counsel for the parties and have examined the impugned order
passed by the District forum, New
 Delhi (KG Marg).
6. It
shall not be in-apposite to recall the observations of this Commission, make on
25.09.2008, while admitting this appeal. The same are extracted below :
In view of the contention of the counsel
for the appellant that respondent had asked for compensation of Rs. 50,000/- besides refund of ticket amount on account of
wrongful cancellation of the ticket but the District Forum has acted to obverboard that it directed the appellant not only to pay
the price of the tickets amounting to Rs. 87,667/-
but also compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/- and Rs. 10,000/- as cost of litigation, if it is so, the
District Forum has exceeded its brief and the impugned order reflects utter
non-application of mind and element of whimsicality and capriciousness.
Protection of rights of consumer does not mean enriching the consumer unjustly.
He has to be compensated reasonably for mental agony and harassment or actual
loss. It appears t

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
ity and capriciousness.
Protection of rights of consumer does not mean enriching the consumer unjustly.
He has to be compensated reasonably for mental agony and harassment or actual
loss. It appears that the District Forum is not adhering to the guidelines and observations made by this Commission as almost in every case
compensation is being awarded in lacs whereas
the actual loss suffered by the consumer runs into few thousands.
5. Holding
the Appellant guilty of unfair trade practice and for deficiency-in-service,
the Ld. District Forum have recorded in its findings that time limits are set for purchase of tickets and not for getting
confirmed reservation. Assuming, what Air India states can be given credence,
then, Air India should itself have a contacted the complainant on 13.2.2001 and
told him that seat would not be available to him on 11.3.2001, whether he would
like to travel on 4.3.2001 for which he had confirmed booking. It is clear that
the booking for 4.3.2001 was cancelled on 14.2.1001 at 7.17 hours without
notice and consent of the complainant. The system ought not to have removed the
booking for 4.3.2001 without the consent of the complainant. There is nothing
on record to show that the complainant had authorized Air India to cancel the reservation.
Having erroneously and recklessly cancelled the booking of the complainant for
4.3.2001 the Air India
provides seat

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
ord to show that the complainant had authorized Air India to cancel the reservation.
Having erroneously and recklessly cancelled the booking of the complainant for
4.3.2001 the Air India
provides seat in the same flight by charging Rs.
80,667/- without giving the credit of the cost of the ticket held by the
complainant.
6. Considering
the affidavit of the complainant filed before the Ld. District Forum there
appears to us no fault in the findings recorded by the Ld. District Forum, as
cited above. However, we agree with the Ld. Counsel for the Appellant that
award of the compensation in the form damages is highly unjustified and irrational in the given facts
and circumstance of the case. The respondents stands
fully compensated when the refund of the price of the ticket paid by him in
lieu of the alleged wrong cancellation of his confirming Ticket for 4.3.2001 is
ordered. The appellants are not liable to be doubly penalized, especially when
the alleged confirmed booking of return flight was a highly concessional
excursion ticket issued under highly concessional
scheme in United States having restrictions attached to it as stated in exhibit
filed alongwith the affidavit of Shri M.B. Loker,
Commercial Manager, NI of the Appellant before the Ld. District Forum in their
evidence and which fact was not discussed by the Respondent (complainant).
7. We
are, therefore, of the considere

title: Air India Limited vs Shri Manoj Kumar Dewan on 25 January, 2010
text:
Loker,
Commercial Manager, NI of the Appellant before the Ld. District Forum in their
evidence and which fact was not discussed by the Respondent (complainant).
7. We
are, therefore, of the considered view that the impugned order is liable to be
modified to the extent that compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/- awarded in this case is un-warranted. Hence,
allowing the appeal partly , it is directed that the
Respondent shall be refunded Rs. 80,667/- the price
of the ticket purchased by him for
undertaking the return journey from USA with cost of litigation of Rs. 10,000/- , as awarded by the Ld. District Forum, within
30 days from the receipt of this order by the Appellant , failing which they
shall be liable to pay interest @ 9% p.a. on the above stated amount till
realization.
8. FDR,
if any , deposited by the appellant, be released after completion of due
formalities.
9. Copy
of this order be provided free of cost to the parties, as per statutory
requirement. Copy of this order be sent to the
concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to record room.
(JUSTICE BARKAT ALI ZAIDI)

The first fundamental question that arises is whether the
 Bank is responsible for an unauthorized transfer
 occasioned by an act of malfeasance on the part of
 functionaries of the Bank or by an act of malfeasance by
 any other person (except the Complainant/account-

 If an account is maintained by the Bank, the Bank itself
 is responsible for its safety and security. Any systemic
 failure, whether by malfeasance on the part of its
 functionaries or by any other person (except the
 consumer/account-holder), is its responsibility, and not

 Consumer/Complainant deposits or invests their hard

 bounden duty of the bank to protect and safeguard the

OPs by the complainant. Even the report of Hemant Sony Ex.C-8

duly supported by his affidavit Ex.C-9 is on the record lending

corroboration to the case of the complainant that there was

manufacturing defect in the mobile set. We find that the order of the

District Forum suffers from no illegality or material infirmity in this

case.
Consumer Protection Act
is consumer orientated Act and it has

been designed by the legislature with the sole purpose to protect the

innocent consumers from their exploitation by big business houses.

We are in agreement with the finding of the District Forum holding

the OPs deficient in service jointly and severally. The order of the

District Forum Ferozepur under challenge in the above referred

title: Hcl Infosystems Ltd. vs Vishal Arora on 16 March, 2017
text:
We are in agreement with the finding of the District Forum holding

the OPs deficient in service jointly and severally. The order of the

District Forum Ferozepur under challenge in the above referred

appeals is, thus, affirmed in these appeals.
9. As a result of our above discussion, we find no merit in

first appeal no.37 of 2015 and first appeal no.167 of 2015 and both

the above appeals are hereby dismissed.
10. In First Appeal No.37 of 2015, the appellant had

deposited an amount of Rs.12,165/- in this Commission at the time

of filing the appeal. This amount alongwith interest, which accrued
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 8
thereon, if any, be remitted by the registry to respondent no.1 of this

appeal being complainant by way of crossed cheque/demand draft

after 45 days from receipt of certified copy of this order.
11. In First Appeal No.167 of 2015, the appellant had

deposited an amount of Rs.12,200/- in this Commission at the time

of filing the appeal. After calculating the interest on above amount,

the amount be remitted by the registry to respondent no.1 of this

appeal being complainant, as per his entitlement in a strict manner,

as per this order, by way of crossed cheque/demand draft after 45

days. Remaining amount, if any, be remitted by the registry to

appellant of this appeal.
12. Arguments in above referred appeals were heard on

text:
s order, by way of crossed cheque/demand draft after 45

days. Remaining amount, if any, be remitted by the registry to

appellant of this appeal.

 ORDER
Thiru. J. JAYARAM, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER.
1. The appeal is filed by the 1st opposite party against the order of the

District Forum, Thanjavur in C.C.No.106/2007, dated 25.08.2010, allowing the

complaint against the 1st opposite party.
2. The case of the complainant is that he purchased a motor cycle from

the 2nd opposite party availing loan from the 3rd opposite party and his vehicle

was insured with the 1st opposite party. The vehicle was stolen away on

21.01.2007 and the loss of motorcycle was intimated to the police; but the

vehicle could not be traced. He submitted claim form to the insurer/1st opposite

party but the claim was repudiated by the 1st opposite party without any valid

reason, which amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the 1 st opposite

party and hence the complainant praying for direction to the opposite parties to

pay jointly and severally a sum of Rs.43,224/- which is the amount paid to the

2nd opposite party and to pay compensation.
3. According to the 1st opposite party, the complainant's vehicle was not

title: Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
text:
o

pay jointly and severally a sum of Rs.43,224/- which is the amount paid to the

2nd opposite party and to pay compensation.
3. According to the 1st opposite party, the complainant's vehicle was not

registered with the Registering Authority/Regional Transport Office and further
3
the loss of motorcycle was reported only on 29.03.2007 to the 1st opposite party

and to the Police belatedly and hence the complainant is not entitled to claim

compensation under the policy and the claim was repudiated for valid reasons

and there is no deficiency in service on their part.
4. The District Forum considered the rival contentions and allowed the

complaint holding that there is deficiency in service on the part of the 1st

opposite party and passed an order directing the 1st opposite party to pay

Rs.40,775/- which is the cost of the motorcycle and to pay costs of Rs.1000/-.

Aggrieved by the impugned order the 1st opposite party/National Insurance

Company has preferred this appeal.
5. The contention of the appellant/1st opposite party would be that the

complainant's vehicle was insured with them and the vehicle was lost on

21.01.2007 and the vehicle was not registered with the Registering

Authority/Regional Transport Officer at the time of theft and the vehicle was

title: Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
text:
cle was insured with them and the vehicle was lost on

21.01.2007 and the vehicle was not registered with the Registering

Authority/Regional Transport Officer at the time of theft and the vehicle was

used by the complainant without registration in violation of the provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act
and the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and

hence the claim was repudiated and there is no deficiency in service on their

part.
6. On perusal of Ex A3, the Policy was in force from 01.12.2006 to

30.11.2007 and the vehicle was purchased on 30.11.2006 and theft of the

vehicle took pace on 21.01.2007 and therefore the policy was very much in force

on the date of theft. However, admittedly, the vehicle was purchased on
4
30.11.2006 and the vehicle was lost on 21.01.2007 and theft has been reported

to the police only on 13.02.2007 after 23 days after the incident as seen from

FIR, Ex A7 and intimation has been sent to insurer/1st opposite party only on

09.03.2007, after a delay of 47 days. Therefore, it is clear that the complainant

has been using the vehicle from 30.11.2006 to 21.01.2007 without registration

with the Registering Authority.
7. In these circumstances, the appellant has argued that the

respondent/complainant is not entitled to compensation under the policy and the

appellant relied on the decisions of the Hon'ble National Consumer Disputes

title: Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
text:
stances, the appellant has argued that the

respondent/complainant is not entitled to compensation under the policy and the

appellant relied on the decisions of the Hon'ble National Consumer Disputes

Redressal Commission reported in I (2013) CPJ 32B (NC) (CN) in the case

Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., - Vs - K.M. Thirunavukkarasu wherein

it has been held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
21(b)
-
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
-
Sections 39
,
41
, 44 - Insurance - Accidents

claim - Invalidity of registration number - Violation of conditions of policy -

Claim repudiated - Alleged deficiency in service - District Forum allowed

complaint - State Commission dismissed appeal - Hence, revision - Complainant

failed to obtain permanent registration number for the vehicle before expiry of

temporary registration number or even several days thereafter - He had taken

calculated risk in not registering vehicle with concerned registering authority -

Complainant cannot seek any benefit under
section 44
of Motor Vehicles Act,

1988 - Repudiation justified.
5
8. The appellant further relied on the decision of Hon'ble National

Commission, reported in II (2013) CPJ 20A (NC) (CN) in the case of
Narinder Singh - Vs New India Assurance Co., Ltd., & Ors
wherein it has

title: Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
text:
appellant further relied on the decision of Hon'ble National

Commission, reported in II (2013) CPJ 20A (NC) (CN) in the case of
Narinder Singh - Vs New India Assurance Co., Ltd., & Ors
wherein it has

been held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
21(b)
-
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
-
Sections 39
, 192 - Insurance - Accident of

vehicle - Surveyor appointed - Loss assessed - Invalid Registration - Claim

repudiated - Alleged deficiency in service - District Forum allowed complaint -

State Commission allowed appeal - Hence revision - Vehicle was being driven

without registration at the time of accident which is prohibited under
section 39
of Act, 1988 - This is also an offence under
Section 192
of Act, 1988 - State

Commission rightly dismissed complaint.
9. The appellant also relied on the decision of the Hon'ble National

Commission reported in IV (2012) CPJ 570 (NC) in the case of
Attar Singh

& Anr - Vs - Reliance General Insurance Co., & Anr
wherein it has been

held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
14(1)(d)
,
21(b)
- Insurance - Theft of vehicle - Delay in lodging FIR and sending

information to Insurance Company - Claim repudiated - Alleged deficiency in

service - District Forum allowed complaint - State Commission allowed appeal -

Hence revision - FIR was lodged after a delay of 27 days from commission of

title: Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
text:
- Claim repudiated - Alleged deficiency in

service - District Forum allowed complaint - State Commission allowed appeal -

Hence revision - FIR was lodged after a delay of 27 days from commission of

theft - Information was sent to Insurance Company about theft with delay of

283 days - Terms and conditions of insurance policy stipulate that petitioners
6
were required to intimate Insurance, Company immediately about theft -

Repudiation justified."
10. In the light of the above decisions of Hon'ble National Commission,

we hold that the respondent/complainant is not entitled to claim the benefits

under the policy and that there is no deficiency in service on the part of the 1 st

opposite party in repudiating the claim of the complainant.
11. The District Forum has erroneously held that there is deficiency in

service on the part of the 1st opposite party and has allowed the complaint

granting compensation. In view of our finding that there is no deficiency on the

part of the 1st opposite party, the order of the District Forum is liable to be set

aside.
12. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the order of the District

Forum is set aside and the complaint is dismissed. No order as to costs in this

appeal.
13. The Registry is directed to hand over the Fixed Deposit Receipt

made towards the mandatory deposit to the appellant/1st opposite party duly

int is dismissed. No order as to costs in this

appeal.
13. The Registry is directed to hand over the Fixed Deposit Receipt

made towards the mandatory deposit to the appellant/1st opposite party duly

discharged with accrued interest.

 Order

 This appeal has been preferred by appellant/Opposite Party No. 1

(hereinafter referred as 'OP No. 1') under
Section 15
of the Consumer

Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') against the order

dated 16.04.2014 in C.C. No. 536 of 06.12.2013 passed by the learned

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
red as 'OP No. 1') under
Section 15
of the Consumer

Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') against the order

dated 16.04.2014 in C.C. No. 536 of 06.12.2013 passed by the learned

District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Bathinda (in short the 'District

Forum') vide which the complaint filed by the respondent/complainant

(hereinafter referred as 'complainant') was allowed with the directions to
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 2
OPs No. 1-3 to make arrangement to collect the mobile hand set alongwith

accessories from the complainant and to make cash payment of Rs. 15,699/-

alongwith compensation of Rs. 10,000/-. The order was to be complied

within 45 days from the date of receipt of copy of the order, failing which it

will carry interest @ 9% per annum till realization whereas complaint

against OP No. 4 was dismissed.
2. A consumer complaint was filed by the complainant against the

OPs on the allegations that OP No. 1 was India's most popular online

shopping mall providing online purchasing of products like Cell Phone,

Mobile, Cameras, Computers etc of various companies. The complainant

was in need of mobile handset for his personal use and also allured by the

tall claims made by OP No. 1, he opted to purchase mobile phone Samsung

Galaxy S2-GT-19100 manufactured by OP No. 2 and marketed by OP No. 3

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
bile handset for his personal use and also allured by the

tall claims made by OP No. 1, he opted to purchase mobile phone Samsung

Galaxy S2-GT-19100 manufactured by OP No. 2 and marketed by OP No. 3

and delivered by Op O. 4. Accordingly he placed an online order on

04.10.2010 which was confirmed by OP No. 1 vide PaisaPay ID

34739521695 on the same day. As per the terms of the OPs, the consumer

has to pay full payment in advance at the time of placing the order and

accordingly he made the entire payment of Rs. 15,699/- if on the receipt of

the product, the consumer does not satisfied, then the consumer had the

choice to replace the mobile hand set with new one or to get 100% refund of

the amount paid in advance. OPs had assured that the ordered item shall be

received by the complainant on or before 15.10.2013. OP No. 1further

advised that if the ordered item is not received by the complainant on or

before 15.10.2013, he can request for the refund of the amount. The

complainant had not received the ordered item upto 15.10.2013. The mobile

hand set bearing serial/IMEI No. 357470045937798 was sent through OP

No. 4 to the complainant vide invoice No. 3510/1925060 dated 08.10.2013
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 3
for a sum of Rs. 15,699/- was received on 17.10.2013. It was further alleged

that when the parcel was opened, it was found that there were scratches on

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
dated 08.10.2013
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 3
for a sum of Rs. 15,699/- was received on 17.10.2013. It was further alleged

that when the parcel was opened, it was found that there were scratches on

the mobile hand set and the battery also seemed not to be new one and some

slips/stickers were put on the said mobile hand set. Accordingly, he sent a

mail to OP No. 1 on 17.10.2013 and protested for the delivery of old and

defective hand set and claimed the refund of the amount of Rs. 15,699/-. OP

No. 1 opened the claim of the complainant under claim ID 305440. Then he

received the mail from OP No. 3 to send back the aforesaid mobile hand set

to OP NO. 4. Thereafter he received another mail from OP No. 1 who

wanted proof regarding the claim of the complainant on 19.10.2013. The

complainant sent the scanned photographs of the aforesaid mobile handset to

OP NO. 1. However, to the utter surprise of the complainant, he received

another mail from OP No. 1 on 21.10.2013 whereby he was required to

confirm the receipt of ordered product. He again contacted OP NO. 1 and

protested for the receipt of aforesaid mail to which they conveyed the

complainant that they shall check their record and shall take further steps in

the matter accordingly. Thereafter, he received another e-mail on

21.10.2013 from OP No. 1 whereby they directed the complainant to re-ship

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
y shall check their record and shall take further steps in

the matter accordingly. Thereafter, he received another e-mail on

21.10.2013 from OP No. 1 whereby they directed the complainant to re-ship

the consignment to the seller and to provide the details of tracking. He

received another mail from OP No. 3 on 22.10.2013 whereby they

confirmed the approval of refund of the amount and confirmed that the

complainant will receive the refund amount very soon and said the

complainant to send the mobile hand set to OP No. 3 through OP No. 4 but

the complainant was not clear to whom the said order was required to be

sent back and on which address. Then he received another telephonic call

from the OPs on their numbers 0124-6777005 and toll free number

18002093229 to send back the aforesaid mobile hand set. He tried to get the
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 4
instructions to whom the said hand set was required to be sent back, but no

instructions were issued to the complainant by the OPs. OP No. 3 vide mail

dated 22.10.2013 confirmed the approval of the refund of the full amount to

the complainant but the complainant did not receive any refund amount. He

received another mail from OP No. 1 on 24.10.2013 whereby they

demanded proof of return shipment without confirming the name and

address of the addressee and ultimately the claim of the complainant was

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
eived another mail from OP No. 1 on 24.10.2013 whereby they

demanded proof of return shipment without confirming the name and

address of the addressee and ultimately the claim of the complainant was

closed. Then the complainant vide mail dated 28.11.2013 to confirm the

mail and address to whom the hand set was to be sent back but they again

enquired from the complainant to provide return shipment proof. The

complainant had been trying from post to pillar to get the amount back but to

no action. He was still ready to return the mobile hand set and the said

mobile hand set was still in the same condition, but conduct of the OPs in

sending the old and defective mobile hand set and not returning the amount

as per their terms amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade

practice. Hence the complaint was filed with the directions to the OPs to

refund the value of the mobile hand set of Rs. 15,699/- alongwith interest @

18% p.a., Rs. 50,000/- as compensation and Rs. 11,000/- as litigation

expenses.
3. The complaint was contested by the OPs. OP No.1 took preliminary

objections in its written reply stating that the claim was highly exaggerated.

The sale price of the mobile set was INR 15,699 whereas compensation of

Rs. 76,699/- has been demanded. The business of OP No. 1 is to provide an

online market place through its website www.ebay.in from where the

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
of the mobile set was INR 15,699 whereas compensation of

Rs. 76,699/- has been demanded. The business of OP No. 1 is to provide an

online market place through its website www.ebay.in from where the

buyers and sellers directly interact for sale-purchase of various items as

defined under the
Information Technology Act, 2000
as amended from time

to time and his role was to facilitate other person for receiving, storing or
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 5
transmitting record/information, therefore, the status of OP No. 1 is that of

that of 'Intermediary' and under
section 79
of the Information Technology

Act, 2000 no liability can be fastened upon OP No. 1. The contract of sale

of items was only between the registered seller and the winning

bidder/buyer. OP No. 1 provided the terms and conditions for registering

the claim for replacement/refund of product. The service to the

buyers/sellers is a gratuitous service. The claim redressal process of OP No.

1 follows with each of its buyer and seller is a two step process under which

firstly the claim has to be registered with OP No. 1, he was to process it and

look into the genuineness and validity of such claim. No consideration was

taken by OP No. 1 from the complainant at the time of transaction in

question, therefore, there was no relationship of consumer/service provider

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
ness and validity of such claim. No consideration was

taken by OP No. 1 from the complainant at the time of transaction in

question, therefore, there was no relationship of consumer/service provider

between the complainant and OP No. 1.
4. In the primary submission, it was submitted that the complainant

failed to return the item received within a period of 30 days as per their

procedure. Clause 6 of the User Agreement also excludes the involvement

of OP NO. 1.
5. On merits, the preliminary objections taken above were reiterated. It

was further submitted that OP No. 1 received the said product on

12.10.2013. On 16.10.2013, the complainant raised the claim on the website

of OP No. 1 complaining against the said product. The submission of the

complainant that he received the said product on 17.10.2013 was false. OP

No. 1 had contacted the complainant and asked for proof of his claim. The

complainant had failed to file any document depicting the defective product

in question. Even the phone calls and e-mails sent to the complainant were a

part of gratuitous service. During the complaint the product was not

returned, therefore, his claim was closed, therefore, there was no deficiency
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 6
in service on the part of OP No. 1. It was submitted that the complaint was

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
roduct was not

returned, therefore, his claim was closed, therefore, there was no deficiency
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 6
in service on the part of OP No. 1. It was submitted that the complaint was

without merit and it be dismissed.
6. OP No. 2 in its written reply took the preliminary objections that

District Forum did not have any territorial jurisdiction and under
section 11

(2) (b)
of CP Act as no permission was sought from the District Forum

before institution of the complaint. The complaint was false and frivolous to

the knowledge of the complainant, therefore, liable to be dismissed under
section 26
of the Act. The complainant had concealed the material and

necessary information that the obligation of this OP was to set right the

mobile hand set by repairing or replacing the defective parts only. The

performance of the mobile phone depends upon the handling of the product

and downloading of various mobile applications, games and virus threat

from internet usage. No ground was made out in favour of the complainant

for replacement of the mobile hand set because he has not alleged any

specific manufacturing defect and inferior quality of the specific part and

there was no expert evidence to prove the defect. There was no deficiency

in services on the part of this OP and that the complainant had not annexed

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
ct and inferior quality of the specific part and

there was no expert evidence to prove the defect. There was no deficiency

in services on the part of this OP and that the complainant had not annexed

the warranty card bearing stamp of seller and as per exclusion clause No. 1

printed at the back of warranty card, if the warranty card was not filled up

and mailed back/submitted to the nearest authorized service centre of the

complaint within two weeks of the purchase, the warranty condition in such

circumstances were not applicable. On merits, it was denied for want of

knowledge that the complainant had placed online order for the purchase of

mobile phone Samsung Galaxy S-2 GT-19100 and made the payment of Rs.

15699/-. They were not in the knowledge that OP No. 1 had assured the

complainant that the ordered item shall be received on or before 15.10.2013

and in case, it was not received then he had right to get the refund. It was
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 7
denied for want of knowledge that he had no knowledge whether the hand

set was received through OP No. 4 on 17.10.2013. It was also denied that

the complainant sent the email on 17.10.2013 and protested for the delivery

of old and defective product and claimed refund of Rs. 15699/-. It was also

denied that the complainant received mail from OP No. 3 to send back the

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
mail on 17.10.2013 and protested for the delivery

of old and defective product and claimed refund of Rs. 15699/-. It was also

denied that the complainant received mail from OP No. 3 to send back the

aforesaid hand set to OP NO. 4. It was also denied for want of knowledge

that OP No. 4 sought proof regarding claim of the complainant or that the

complainant had scanned photographs to OP No. 1. Other facts as stated in

the complaint were also denied for want of knowledge. It was denied that

the complainant had suffered any mental tension, agony, loss on account of

non refund of the amount of hand set as alleged by him. The complainant

against this OP was without merit and it be dismissed.
7. OPs No. 3 & 4 were proceeded ex-parte.
8. Parties adduced evidence in support of their contentions. Complainant

tendered into evidence his affidavit Ex. C-1 and documents Ex. C-2

photocopy of letter, Ex. C-3 photocopy of declaration, Ex. C-4 to Ex. C-11

photocopies of messages, Ex. C-12 photocopies of photographs, Ex. C-13 to

Ex. C-17 photocopy of messages, Ex. C-18 to Ex. C-19 photocopy of emails,

Ex. C-20 affidavit of Parvesh Garg, Ex. C-21 photocopy of account

statement, Ex. C-22 photocopy of email, Ex. C-23 photocopy of pay rules

and policies containing page No. 1 to 8, Ex. C-24 photocopy of how fees

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
fidavit of Parvesh Garg, Ex. C-21 photocopy of account

statement, Ex. C-22 photocopy of email, Ex. C-23 photocopy of pay rules

and policies containing page No. 1 to 8, Ex. C-24 photocopy of how fees

work containing page No. 1 to 4 and closed the evidence. On the other hand

OP No. 1 tendered into evidence Ex. OP-1/1 affidavit of Ashish Kumar, Ex.

OP-1/2 photocopy of User Agreement, Ex. OP-1/3 photocopy of I.D.

9. After going through the allegations as alleged in the complaint,

12. It has been contended by the counsel for the appellant/OP No. 1 that

the District Forum has failed to appreciate the contentions raised by the

complainant in the complaint. The District Forum has also failed to accept

ed by the counsel for the appellant/OP No. 1 that

delivery/condition of the products returned by the seller. Therefore, the

penalty was wrongly fixed upon OP No. 1 alongwith OPs No. 2 and 3.
13. In case, we go through the facts of the case, the complainant had

they are manufacturer and

OP No. 1 is that his role is just as an intermediary and he had not sold any

product and in case there was any defect in the product then he was not

liable for the same. However the entire correspondence on the record is

OP No. 1 and OPs No. 2 & 3 has not come up on the record. The agreement

"Intermediary" with respect to any particular electronic message

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
No. 1 has relied upon the definition of

intermediary as given in the
Information Technology Act, 2000
which is

reproduced as under:-
"Intermediary" with respect to any particular electronic message

 means any person who on behalf of another person receives stores and

 transmits that message or provides any service with respect to that

 message;
But we have to see what was the role of OP No. 1. As the role of

intermediary is just to pass the electronic message, but here the role of OP

No. 1 is more than that. It is not restricted to online shopping but he has

taken the entire case on behalf of manufacturer and seller with the purchaser.

Therefore, the role of OP No. 1 cannot be restricted only to be intermediary.

Even the warranty has been placed on the record as Ex. OP-1/3 according to

which in case if the purchaser is not satisfied with the product, then he has

an option to report his concern by using an online request form to register a

dispute within 30 days of item delivery if the item does not concern as per

the order. In the present case, the complaint was lodged within the statutory
First Appeal No.1002 of 2014 12
period as per the warranty. It cannot be said that OP No. 1 had no role to

play, therefore, the District Forum has rightly observed the deficiency in

service on the part of OPs No. 1 to 3. So, the findings so recorded by

title: Ebay India Pvt. Ltd. vs Parvesh Garg on 1 June, 2015
text:
anty. It cannot be said that OP No. 1 had no role to

play, therefore, the District Forum has rightly observed the deficiency in

service on the part of OPs No. 1 to 3. So, the findings so recorded by

District Forum are correct and we affirm the same.
14. In view of the above discussion, we are of the opinion that there

is no merit in the appeal and the same is hereby dismissed. The order of the

District Forum is correct and the same is upheld.

igence of the OP, if the Commission

 u/s 14 of the Act and/or quantum of compensation and punitive damages etc. will depend

12.4 Under the provisions of the Act, any good, like the car in the present case, can be
 ordered to be replaced or the cost can be ordered to be refunded if it suffers from any

"12.5 Whenever a manufacturer/Dealer of a vehicle offers to sell a brand new vehicle to

Consumer Protection

1986....."
12.6 How does a purchaser of a new vehicle, who is neither an expert in automobile
 Engineering, nor expected to be so, perceive a manufacturing defect or a defect in the car?
 Whenever a person purchases a new vehicle, be it a low end vehicle or a middle end
 vehicle or a high end vehicle, depending upon his economic sta

title: H.G. Jain vs Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. on 14 July, 2025
text:
ceive a manufacturing defect or a defect in the car?
 Whenever a person purchases a new vehicle, be it a low end vehicle or a middle end
 vehicle or a high end vehicle, depending upon his economic status/affording capacity, has
 great sentimental/emotional values attached to such purchase/acquisition of new vehicle.
 Even an unwanted small scratch or damage to the vehicle in the initial period of such
 purchase upsets not only the purchaser of such vehicle but his family members as well. If
 such a vehicle start giving troubles/manifesting mechanical or other technical issues right
 from the beginning, calling for its repeated visits to the workshop for servicing/repairs etc.,
 such occurrences itself disturbs the peace of mind of such purchaser and cause mental
 agony to him and his family. It is natural for such a Complainant to think that a vehicle
 giving repeated troubles, requiring repeated visits to the workshop, suffers from same kind
 of serious defects, which he tend to classify as 'manufacturing defect', although in all such
 cases, the defects though being there, may not strictly speaking be 'manufacturing defect'.
 In the context of airbags not deployed in an accident, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shailendra
 Bhatnagar (2022) SCC Online SC 483), observed "..... A consumer is not meant to be an
 expert in physics calculating the impact of a collusion of the theories bas

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shailendra

 expert in physics calculating the impact of a collusion of the theories based on velocity and
 force......"
12.7 In cases involves allegations of manufacturing defect in the vehicle, it is typical on
 the part of manufacture and/or dealer to take the plea that the vehicle suffered damage due
 to the negligent handling of the vehicle by the purchaser/complainant and the alleged issues
 are only due to operational/usage reasons, there is lack of proper maintenance etc. The
 standard defence taken by Manufacturers/Dealers in such cases where manufacturing
 defect is alleged and replacement is sought is that vehicle is sold under a warranty for a
 certain specified period from the date of purchase or until vehicle runs for a certain kms.,
 whichever is earlier and that warranty is made subject to certain terms and conditions,
 qualifications and limitations as set out in the warranty booklet and that as per warranty, the
 manufacturers/dealers obligation is limited to repair or replace the defective components at
 its sole discretion during the warranty period if the manufacturer/dealer acknowledge that
 such defect(s) is attributable to faulty material or workmanship at the time of manufacturer."

 such defect(s) is attributable to faulty material or workmanship at the time of manufacturer."
50. An issue was also raised of the liability of the principal vis-à-vis the dealer. The said issue

was also answered in paragraphs 12.8 and 12.9 as follows:-
"12.8 Further, in cases involving automobiles, it is typical on the part of manufacturer to
plead Principal to Principal relationship rather than Principal to Agent relationship with a
view to avoid its liability for any wrongful acts of their authorized dealer. The issue of
Manufacturer-Dealer relationship came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in
Tata Motors Ltd. Vs. Antonio Paulo Vaz & Anr. (Civil Appeal No.
574/2021
decided on 18.02.2021). In this case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, after taking note of
dealership agreement, held that the relationship between manufacturer-dealer was that of
Principal to Principal and not that of Principal to Agent. In the present case, the OP-1
(manufacturer) in its pleadings and/or evidence has not specifically claimed either a
Principal to Principal or Principal to Agent relationship with OP-2 (dealer), although during
the hearing the Counsel for OP-1 stated that they work on Principal to Principal basis.
Further, in their submission, OP-1 has taken the plea that there is no privity of contract
between Complainant and OP-1, as admittedly the Complainant purchased th

title: H.G. Jain vs Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. on 14 July, 2025
text:
ork on Principal to Principal basis.
Further, in their submission, OP-1 has taken the plea that there is no privity of contract
between Complainant and OP-1, as admittedly the Complainant purchased the car from
OP-2 and not from OP-1. OP-1 had not provided any services to the Complainant and
hence there is no ground to allege deficiency in services on the part of OP-1. On the
other hand, OP-2 dealer contended during the hearing that notwithstanding that the car in
question has been sold by them, they are concerned with any providing after sale
services and have nothing to do with the defects in the car, in question, if any, contending
further that they have not been deficient in providing any service/after sale service to the
complainant in this case. In a Principal to Agent relationship, the Principal is responsible
for wrong doings of his agent/acts done on behalf of the Principal. However, in a
Principal to Principal relationship, which is generally entered into by car manufacturers
with their. authorized dealers under some kind of a dealership agreement, while the
Principal (Manufacturer) may not be responsible for the wrong doings/acts of negligence
of the Principal (Dealer), it surely is responsible for the warranties it has given with
respect to removing any defects or replacement of parts or replacement of car itself in
case of manufacturing defect(s), as long as condit

text:
it surely is responsible for the warranties it has given with
respect to removing any defects or replacement of parts or replacement of car itself in
case of manufacturing defect(s), as long as conditions of warranties have been
observed/complied with. Although the correspondence between the parties show that
OP-1 and OP-2 were acting in tandem to each other, as if OP-2 was acting like an agent
of OP-1 while conveying various offers like trade in offer, extended warranty etc. on
behalf of OP-1 only, even if it is presumed that relationship between manufacturer and
dealer of a car is' that of Principal to Principal, the manufacturer can only resist/avoid his
responsibility/his liabilities for wrong doings/acts of omissions and commissions of dealer,
but for warranties offered to the customer during the warranty period, and subject
to due compliance of terms of such warranties by the customer, both the
manufacturer and dealer are liable for repairs/replacement of any parts or
replacement of car itself, if the terms of warranty so provide for. Dealer alone
cannot be made to bear the liabilities for repair/replacement of parts and/or
replacement of car on account of manufacturing defect during the warranty period
even in a Principal to Principal relationship.

dealer are independent legal entities, d
