 it from 9% to 18% per annum, while keeping the other terms intact. Respondent shall
 refund the requisite amount within a period of two months from date.
3.2. Similarly, reliance is placed on the following observations of the Supreme Court
in M/s Ashoka Investments Co. Vs. M/s United Towers India Pvt. Ltd. in C.A. No.
4913/2015 decided on 11.10.2022:
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusing the material on record, we
 enquired from the respondents, as to whether, the amount as awarded by the NCDRC in
 the impugned order dated 16.03.2015 has been paid to the appellant or not. We were
 informed that amount has not been paid so far. No pg. 5 just

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
, as to whether, the amount as awarded by the NCDRC in
 the impugned order dated 16.03.2015 has been paid to the appellant or not. We were
 informed that amount has not been paid so far. No pg. 5 justification has come forward as
 to why the awarded amount was not tendered to the appellant. The appellant has
 pressed for the entire complaint being allowed as per the relief claimed therein. On the
 other hand, the respondent has sought to justify the order of NCDRC. However, there is
 no appeal by the respondent. The appellant has also pressed vehemently that
 respondent should be called upon to produce the sale deeds of the two flats in question,
 transferred in favour of the third parties and that the said amount ought to be paid to the
 appellant along with other claims, the respondent has unjustly enriched itself by the
 aforesaid conduct. On the other hand, this request has been resisted by the respondents.
11. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, we are in
 agreement with the findings recorded by the NCDRC regarding the conduct of both the
 parties, however, we feel that in the fitness of things and in the interest of both the parties
 considering the nature of agreement made and also their conduct that the order of the
 NCDRC requires to be modified. The rate of interest awarded is only 9%. Once, we find
 that under the agreement, in t

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
idering the nature of agreement made and also their conduct that the order of the
 NCDRC requires to be modified. The rate of interest awarded is only 9%. Once, we find
 that under the agreement, in the event of default, the appellant's liability to pay
 interest on the defaulted amount could go up to 18%, it would be just and proper in
 the facts of the present case that 18% interest be awarded on the refund amount.
12. We accordingly partly allow this appeal and in partial modification of the impugned
 order of the NCDRC, we direct that respondent will refund the amount of
 Rs.4,95,000/(four lakhs and ninetyfive thousand) being the total sale consideration to the
 appellant along with interest @ 18% per annum w.e.f. 17.01.1995 till the date, it is paid.
The said amount be paid at the earliest and in any case within a period of four weeks
 from today.
3.3 Drawing our attention to para 4 onwards, and para 14 in particular, of the State
Commission's order, on facts, it is stated by Mr. Gupta that the appellant has neither
pleaded nor brought any evidence on record even to explain or justify the delay in
handing over of the possession or to state the stage of completion of the project. The
appellant has been completely and adamantly unconcerned about the agony of the
allottees or its own obligation of timely completing the project and duly handing over the
possession and even in

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
t. The
appellant has been completely and adamantly unconcerned about the agony of the
allottees or its own obligation of timely completing the project and duly handing over the
possession and even in communicating the prospect or timelines for the same. It is
therefore, urged that the rate of interest, as granted by the State Commission after
 complete appreciation of the evidence on record and all relevant facts including the
conduct of the parties as discussed in the order, in the facts and circumstances, do not
require any interference. As such, if at all, in view of the fact that for delayed payments,
the builder as per the BBA was entitled to charge the interest at the rate of 21%, the
State Commission should ideally have awarded the interest at the rate of 21%.
4. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the decisions
cited at the bar. There is no dispute that there is deficiency in service in as much as
handing over of the possession has been delayed beyond more than 3 1/2 years from
the agreed date of possession i.e. 36 months from the date of agreement. The only
grievance raised by the appellant builder in the present appeals in with regard to the
rate of interest and compensation for mental agony. The close perusal of the line of
judgments of the Supreme Court with regard to the rate of interest to be awarded in
cases of directions of refund of th

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
of interest and compensation for mental agony. The close perusal of the line of
judgments of the Supreme Court with regard to the rate of interest to be awarded in
cases of directions of refund of the consideration paid by the allottees, restricting such
interest rate to 9% relied upon by the appellant would indeed reveal that though it has
been opined therein that neither compensation under multiple heads can be granted nor
can the compensation granted can be excessive or unreasonable or disproportionate,
we are unable to find a binding mandate that under no circumstance can the interest to
be granted be more than 9% or that in all circumstances it has to be 9%. On the other
hand, in the Supreme Court recent decisions in Rajnesh Sharma and in Ashoka
Investments Co. Vs. M/s United Towers India Pvt. Ltd. in C.A. No. 4913/2015 decided
on 11.10.2022, it has been observed that there is no sacrosanct rule that interest
beyond 9% cannot be allowed in cases of directions for compensation by way of refund
due to deficient service by the developers. It has further been observed in these cases
that the overall circumstances would and should determine the compensatory rate of
interest. Following the same, we are of the considered opinion that all relevant factors
including the nature of deficiency, the length of the delay caused by the developer, the
reasons for such delay, the injury or

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
wing the same, we are of the considered opinion that all relevant factors
including the nature of deficiency, the length of the delay caused by the developer, the
reasons for such delay, the injury or loss, including the mental agony, suffered by the
complainant and even the prevalent market conditions and the current market price for
the complainant to get equivalent unit, and, the similar factors all should go into the
consideration of the fora while deciding the rate of interest to be allowed while directing
refund of the consideration paid by the complainant. Equally, the terms and condition in
the buyers agreement or in the allotment letter and the rate of interest stipulated therein
for delayed payment of instalment or for delay in handing over the possession would
also be a relevant consideration.
5. We note that in para 18, the State Commission has discussed the issue of rate of
interest with considerable detail and has duly and judiciously applied its mind to the
aspect of quantum of compensation through rate of interest. It is the categorical
observation of the State Commission that compensation cannot be uniform, which
observation resonates fully with the observations of the Supreme Court in Rajnesh
Sharma. It has been further noted by the State Commission that in cases of directions
for refund of the amounts, the allottee suffers the loss of escalation of the price

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
the Supreme Court in Rajnesh
Sharma. It has been further noted by the State Commission that in cases of directions
for refund of the amounts, the allottee suffers the loss of escalation of the price of that
unit and he would need to take out more money from his pocket for beating the
escalation in price and therefore after referring to a number of decisions of Supreme
Court and of this Commission, has come to a considered and judicious conclusion that
the award of interest at 12% per annum would serve the ends of justice. The
respondent appears right in contending that the similar unit cannot now, in the present
rising market scenario, be purchased by him even with the compensation as awarded .
by the State Commission. We also note that the builder, for delayed payment of
instalments by the allottees, has stipulated charging of interest at 18/21%, though that
factor being relevant, that alone cannot be the measure for awarding compensatory
interest. In the present appeal while heavy reliance has been placed by the appellant
on Supreme Court decisions awarding interest at 9% in cases of refund, the appellant
builder has also relied on Clause 5.3 (c) to contend that the pre-agreed rate of interest
in cases of failure of the developer to offer the plots is 9% and therefore, no more than
9% could have been awarded by the State Commission on that count also. We in this
behalf, howe

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
ate of interest
in cases of failure of the developer to offer the plots is 9% and therefore, no more than
9% could have been awarded by the State Commission on that count also. We in this
behalf, however, note that Clause 5.1 (c) provides for suo motu and proactive action of
tendering refund by the developer. The same criteria obviously cannot and should not
apply when the allottee has suffered due to deficient service and has earned the
entitlement to such rightful refund after a strenuous wait of nearly five years and after a
legal battle of nearly two years. Apart from stating the rate of interest as granted by the
State Commission to be excessive, the appellant has not been able to point out
objectively any error in the finding of the State Commission or the logic of
proportionality qua the rate of interest as adopted by the State Commission. No case
has been made out to the effect that the actual injury or financial loss suffered by the
complainants on account of the non-delivery of the units within the stipulated time is
less than the compensation granted by way of interest as granted. We are of the
considered opinion that the quantum of compensation, when challenged in the appeal,
the interference by us can be only when the same is on the ground and basis of the
 compensation being demonstrably either gross and apparently excessive or low, or
palpably disproportionate, o

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
ppeal,
the interference by us can be only when the same is on the ground and basis of the
 compensation being demonstrably either gross and apparently excessive or low, or
palpably disproportionate, or apparently arbitrary, or being wholly based on no
 s

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
e is on the ground and basis of the
 compensation being demonstrably either gross and apparently excessive or low, or
palpably disproportionate, or apparently arbitrary, or being wholly based on no
 s

evidence, and has also to be based and established to be so on facts and evidence
relating to quantum of injury or loss suffered. As such, no such effort or such ground
has been made out by the appellant for us to interfere with the judicial discretion
exercised reasonably and judiciously by the State Commission in arriving at and
granting quantum of compensation through the rate of interest of 12% as granted. We
also find no error in the direction of the State Commission with regard to the penal
interest of 3% per annum in case of default by the OP in making the payment before
the due date. Though the lumpsum award of Rs. 1.35 lacs towards "mental agony and
costs" opens a new and second head of compensation, after noting that the amount
granted is composite inclusive of the costs, and after noting the smallness of the
amount of award under this head, we, in appellate jurisdiction, decline to interfere. We,
thus finding no valid reason to interfere, fully uphold the order of the State Commission.
In the result, the appeals FA/42/2022, FA/43/2022 and FA/44/2022 filed by the OP
builder are dismissed.
6. The appeal FA/227/2023 has been filed by Asha Kumari with reported delay of
402

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
e Commission.
In the result, the appeals FA/42/2022, FA/43/2022 and FA/44/2022 filed by the OP
builder are dismissed.
6. The appeal FA/227/2023 has been filed by Asha Kumari with reported delay of
402 days. On the day of the hearing, nobody was present to press the appeal. The
delay condonation application being IA/2295/2023 has been filed wherein the reasons
for delay are stated to be financial constraints of the complainant who is a retired
school teacher, inability to pay the counsel fees and the medical expenses which
became necessary in the year 2017 and 2019. After considering the specific reasons
as detailed in the application, and the reply of the respondent received on 14.01.2025
vide diary no. 1480, we, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, deem it
proper to condone the delay. Turning to the merits, however, we note that the State
Commission has already granted refund along with interest at 12%. The appellant is
seeking enhancement in the rate of interest. The appellant has relied on the fact that
the Buyers agreement para 2.4 allowed the rate of interest of 18-21% for delayed
payment of instalments by the allottees and therefore, the interest granted by the State
Commission is erroneously on the lower side. The appellant also relied on various
decisions of this Commission and the Supreme Court wherein interest at the rate of
18% or higher has been gran

title: Altus Space Builders Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. vs Ajay Kumar Singhal & 3 Ors. on 11 December, 2025
text:
e State
Commission is erroneously on the lower side. The appellant also relied on various
decisions of this Commission and the Supreme Court wherein interest at the rate of
18% or higher has been granted. The appellant also pleaded that a loan of Rs.15 lakhs
from the HDFC bank was taken for obtaining the said property on which substantial
interest had been paid without any corresponding benefit of acquiring the property and
 e

 therefore also the rate of interest to be awarded by the State Commission needed to be
 in the range of 18 to 21%. Having considered the contentions and having perused the
 file, and for the reasons as already discussed, we are unable to find any convincing
 reason or basis to interfere with the well-reasoned order of the State Commission and
 with the well-founded basis for award of compensation as adopted by the State
 Commission. We, therefore, find no merit in the appeal and the same is dismissed.
7. In the result, all the four appeals are dismissed.

1. The third opposite party
in O.P.213/2005 is the appellant in F.A.591/2006 and first and second opposite
parties are the appellants in F.A.626/2006.
2. The first respondent, in
both the appeals, as complainant, approached the District Forum, Chennai
(South), complaining deficiency, against the opposite parties/appellants
seeking direction to replace the goods with new goods of similar description,
which shall be free from any defect, as well, for a recovery of total sum of
Rs.19,20,472/- on various heads on the following grounds (in brief).
3. The complainant purchased
Ford Ikon Rally Sport Car (Registration No.TN-01-D-0006) on 6.6.2000 for a sum
of Rs.6,16,286/- with one year warranty period, trusting the promise and
commitment made by the opposite parties.
Right from the date of purchase, the engine of the car in question
developed frequent problems, by abnormal jerking with heavy noise thereby
causing the complainant,, and others in the car, to feel scared and afraid of
traveling in the car, within the warranty period itself, necessitating
immediate repair and shelling out money from the pocket of the complainant in
view of the urgency an

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
to feel scared and afraid of
traveling in the car, within the warranty period itself, necessitating
immediate repair and shelling out money from the pocket of the complainant in
view of the urgency and want of time.
4. The opposite parties did
not rectify the mistakes which resulted unnecessary expenses for the
complainant to travel elsewhere. With in
a few months of purchase, the manufacturing defect of the engine had manifested
itself by way of jerking of engine and engine noise, not rectified by the
second opposite party, who is an authorized service centre, though charged
excessively, collected a sum of Rs.60,472/-.
In view of the deficiency caused, legal notice was issued, for which, a
reply was given, wherein, the mistake was admitted by the opposite parties.
5. The opposite parties, in
order to repair the manufacturing defects, opened engine head and the said act,
instead of solving the problem, created leading to various other problems, such
as emitting black smoke, causing further noise.
Because of the repeated defects and the same was not rectified properly
by the second and third opposite parties, though the complainant had taken the
vehicle to them on various dates, they have committed deficiency in service to
the consumer, namely the complainant.
The first opposite party being the manufacturer is liable to replace the
vehicle and all the opposite parties are jointl

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
y have committed deficiency in service to
the consumer, namely the complainant.
The first opposite party being the manufacturer is liable to replace the
vehicle and all the opposite parties are jointly and severally liable to pay
the above said sum also. Hence, the
complaint.
6. The first and second
opposite parties, denying all the allegations in the complaint, would contend
that the vehicle has run for around 36,646 kms from 6.6.2000 to 26.12.2004 and
the fact being so, the accusation of the complainant that there was
manufacturing defect in the engine is frivolous and untenable, that whenever
the vehicle was delivered for service/repairs, they were attended to the
satisfaction of the complainant, not challenged and therefore, there is no
deficiency of service, that when the complainant reported, engine vibrating at
idling, the same was rectified to the complainants satisfaction, that engine
noise and jerking cannot be due to manufacturing defect and it may be due to enormous
reasons including continuous use of the vehicle and wear and tear, for which, the
opposite parties cannot be held responsible, that the opposite parties never
admitted any manufacturing defect, at any point of time, that right from the
date of purchase, till 27.2.2003, no complaint was raised about the performance
of the engine which would be seen from the Job Cards from 27.2.2003 to
24.09.2004, wherein,

of time, that right from the
date of purchase, till 27.2.2003, no complaint was raised about the performance
of the engine which would be seen from the Job Cards from 27.2.2003 to
24.09.2004, wherein, the complainant also took the vehicle after satisfying
himself, that the complainant has been enjoying the comfort of the vehicle,
except some technical problem, that the complainant who delivered the vehicle
for repair, refused to take delivery of the vehicle despite being issued a
letter dated 27.01.2005 and even till this date, the complainant has not taken
delivery of the vehicle and that the complainant is taking unfair advantage of
a welfare legislation, claiming exorbitant amount and that since there is no
negligence or deficiency in service, no question of any damage could be granted
by these opposite parties, including punitive damages, thereby, prayed for the
dismissal of the case.
7. The third opposite party
in its separate Version, would contend that after 23.01.2003, the vehicle was
not serviced at their Station, that they have not committed any deficiency in
service or practiced any unfair trade practice, that all the averments are
frivolous, false and untenable, that the complainant is not entitled to any

8. Based upon the pleadings,
the District Forum exhibiting 18 documents on the side of the complainant

e complainant is not entitled to any
relief, thereby, prayed for the dismissal of the complaint.
8. Based upon the pleadings,
the District Forum exhibiting 18 documents on the side of the complainant and 5
documents on the side of the opposite parties, evaluated the materials, framing
points for consideration also. After
evaluation and assessment of the evidence, the District Forum came to the
conclusion, that the defect in the engine was persisting continuously, the
second opposite party had not delivered the same, after making necessary
repairs, which should be construed as deficiency in service. It was further held that since the engine
head was opened to rectify the defects of jerking, the complainant is entitled to
replacement of the engine. In this view,
a direction came to be issued, directing all the opposite parties, to fix new
engine from any defect apart from repairing the vehicle, further directing the
opposite parties to pay a sum of Rs.25,000/- as compensation jointly and
severally, as per the order dated 31.07.2006, which is under challenge in both
the appeals.
9. The third opposite party
who is a Dealer/Service Station, not a manufacturer of the engine or the car,
as the case, may be, he cannot comply the direction. In this view, the third opposite party
aggrieved not only by the first direction, but also by the direction to pay the
compensation, questioning the

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009

s the case, may be, he cannot comply the direction. In this view, the third opposite party
aggrieved not only by the first direction, but also by the direction to pay the
compensation, questioning the findings, on various grounds filed separate
appeal in F.A.591/2006.
10. The first and second
opposite parties, one being the manufacturer, have also questioned the
reasonings given by the District Forum, not satisfied on various grounds, in
F.A.626/2005.
11. Heard the learned counsel
for the appellant, perusal of Written Arguments documents as well as the order
of the lower Forum.
12. The learned counsel,
appearing for the appellants in both the cases, would submit that in the
absence of proof regarding the manufacturing defect, the directions issued by
the lower forum, that too not following the procedure contemplated under
Section13 (b)
of Consumer Protection Act, is erroneous, liable to be set
aside. Further submission was made, on
behalf of the appellants, that after the warranty period was over, there is no
question of replacing the goods/engine, and in this case, the District Forum
without understanding the scope of the warranty, and the contract between the
parties, issued directions which are not within its jurisdiction and in this
view also, the order of the District Forum is to be eclipsed. Elaborating the above submissions, our
attention was also drawn to certain ruling

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
ctions which are not within its jurisdiction and in this
view also, the order of the District Forum is to be eclipsed. Elaborating the above submissions, our
attention was also drawn to certain rulings, of the National Commission, where
it is held, the procedure contemplated under
Section 13 (b)
should be followed,
in this kind of cases.
13. Per contra, it is the
submission of the learned senior counsel representing the
complainant/respondent, that the defect, whether it is manufacturing or
otherwise, since Act does not contemplate manufacturing defect alone, existed
and persisted from the date of purchase of the vehicle and therefore, when that
was not rectified, the opposite parties are not entitled to escape from their
liability as if warranty period was over, whereas it should construed since the
defect occurred, even during the warranty period, still the same continuous, it
should further follow, as per the terms and conditions, the goods should be
replaced, in this case engine of the
car. Further submission of the learned
senior counsel was that because of the defects not repaired by the opposite parties, the complainant was put to hardship, mental agony, monetary
loss etc. and to redress the same, only a nominal amount was ordered as
compensation which cannot be faulted.
Supporting the above submission and to enlighten how the warranty should
be construed, our attention

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
nd to redress the same, only a nominal amount was ordered as
compensation which cannot be faulted.
Supporting the above submission and to enlighten how the warranty should
be construed, our attention was also drawn to certain decisions of the Apex Court, as well as National Commission.
14. Hearing the submissions of
the learned counsel for the parties, perusing the records, then giving our
anxious thought, as well considering the date of purchase and the vehicle left
with the second opposite party for repair, we are of the considered opinion,
that the trial forum has not properly analyzed the case, applied the law
correctly, consequentially, delivered an erroneous order, which requires
setting aside, since in our further opinion, the complainant has not made out a
case, though in the lengthy complaint, he has described many things, which are
not germane to decide the point in issue.
15.
Section 2 (1) (f)
defines defect means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity,
potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any
law for the time being in force or [under any contract, express or implied, or]
as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods
and (g) defines deficiency means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming or inadequacy in the
quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
nner whatsoever in relation to any goods
and (g) defines deficiency means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming or inadequacy in the
quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by
or under any law for the time being in force has been undertaken to be
performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to
any service. While giving
meaning for goods, Act says, as defined in the
Sale of Goods Act, 1930
. Therefore, the warranty or condition defined
under the
Sale of Goods Act
, has to be taken into consideration, in this case,
in order to find out the defect or the deficiency as well the warranty.
16. As rightly submitted by
the learned senior counsel for the complainant/respondent, the Act nowhere says,
the defect should be manufacturing defect.
The defect contemplated under the
definition must be the manufacturing defect, inherent in nature or the defect
should have occurred, within the period of warranty because of the expression
used in (f) and (g) under any contract
, express or implied, undertaken to be
performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to
any service. Therefore, if the defect or the service
complained, had occurred or happened or not attended, was beyond the period of
warranty, which should be taken a contract or condition then, that kind of
activity cannot be brought in under th

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
service
complained, had occurred or happened or not attended, was beyond the period of
warranty, which should be taken a contract or condition then, that kind of
activity cannot be brought in under the above said definition. True, if the defect was noticed, within the
period of warranty or if the deficiency had occurred within the period of
warranty, then continued, continuously or perpetually not corrected, then that can
be taken as covered under the contract or in pursuant of the contract, if there
is a failure to rectify the defect or if there is a deficiency in service.
17.
Section 13 (1)(c)
of the
Consumer Protection Act contemplates where the complainant alleges a defect in
the goods which cannot be determined, without proper analysis or test of the
goods, the District Forum shall obtain a sample of the goods from the
complainant, seal it and authenticate it in the manner prescribed and refer the
sample so sealed to the appropriate laboratory along with a direction that such
laboratory make analysis or test, whichever may be necessary, with a view to
finding out whether such goods suffer from any defect alleged in the complaint
or suffer from any other defect and to report its findings thereon to the
District Forum within a period of forty five days of the receipt of the
reference or within such extended period as may be granted by the District
Forum, which is mandatory i

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
s findings thereon to the
District Forum within a period of forty five days of the receipt of the
reference or within such extended period as may be granted by the District
Forum, which is mandatory in
nature, and this is also the dictum of National Commission, in several
decisions. In this case, admittedly, the
District Forum has not followed the procedure, in order to obtain a report,
about the defect alleged in the complaint regarding the car. In the absence of the expert opinion, based
upon the allegations in the complaint of the complainant alone, that too, after
4 years, deciding the case, car manufactured by the first opposite party was
defective, must be a defective decision, which is available here.
18. In the case decided in The Manager, Tata Engineering and
Locomotive Co. Ltd., Proprietor Commercial Motor, Dehradun and Proprietor
Commercial Motor, Rishikesh {II (2009) CPJ 190 (NC)}, a complaint came to
be lodged before the District Forum, that the manufacturer was guilty of supplying
a truck, with manufacturing defects to the purchaser, which was opposed and
despite on the strength of the warranty, a direction came to be issued, which
was finally under challenge before the National Commission, where the National
Commission has held, that when there is no reliable expert evidence to hold
that the truck suffered from any manufacturing defect, question of directing
the

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
he National Commission, where the National
Commission has held, that when there is no reliable expert evidence to hold
that the truck suffered from any manufacturing defect, question of directing
the opposite party therein to refund the value of the vehicle is unjustified,
though the case was within the period of warranty. In the case on hand also, we do not have any
reliable expert evidence, since the District Forum has not obtained any report,
either on its own, on the basis of the allegation of the complainant or on the
petition filed by the complainant.
19. The National Commission in
LML Limited Vs.
Arun Kumar and Ors, in Para 7 of the order has noted that
both the lower Fora erred in not following the procedure laid down under
Section 13
of the CPA, which had to be done by us. The report of expert has been reproduced
earlier. Having perused the material on
record, and hearing the parties, we are quite clear that vehicle having run for
more than four years, it was not possible at this stage to arrive at a
conclusion about any manufacturing defect and repair cost of these defects
having placed at Rs.10,000. It is not in
dispute that the motorcycle was taken to O.Ps. 1 and 2 for repairs many times,
but only when nothing was done, a complaint was filed before the District
Forum, which decision is applicable to the present case.
Once again the National Commission in
Ajitha Chit

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
repairs many times,
but only when nothing was done, a complaint was filed before the District
Forum, which decision is applicable to the present case.
Once again the National Commission in
Ajitha Chit Funds (P) Ltd., Vs.
Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co. Ltd., and Ors
, has held In the absence of evidence of expert to
that effect and car having diesel engine, it cannot be concludes as rightly
held by Fora below the car was having manufacturing defect. On the above basis, since there is no expert
opinion, except the bills and Job Cards, which we will discus hereunder, which
also not supportive of the complainants case, we conclude, that the
respondent/complainant has not made out a case of manufacturing defect or the
defect, as the case may be, from the day of purchase and therefore, at this
distance of time, direction to replace the engine may not be proper.
20. Admittedly, the
complainant purchased Ford Ikon Rally Sport Car from the opposite parties on
6.6.2000 for a sum of Rs.6,16,286/-. It
is also an admitted fact that the warranty period was one year and the case
came to be filed before the District Forum on 31.03.2005, that is 5 years after,
short of 3 months. The vehicle also run
36,646 kms as on 26.12.2004. Without
considering these things, after the warranty period was over, a direction came
to be issued, which appears to be not correct, that too, in view of the fact

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
so run
36,646 kms as on 26.12.2004. Without
considering these things, after the warranty period was over, a direction came
to be issued, which appears to be not correct, that too, in view of the fact
that the complainant has not made out a case of manufacturing defect in the
engine within the period of warranty except small problem, which will arise ordinarily
in any mechanical device. If that
problem had not been set it right, within the period of warranty freely or
thereafter on payment basis, then only question of accusing the manufacturing
company or the service provider would arise which are also not available in
this case, which would be seen from the documents. Before going into documents, in order to find
out whether the complainant had established the defects, from the day one of
the purchase as claimed or atleast within the period of warranty as claimed, we
have to see certain decisions relied on by the learned senior counsel for the
respondent/complainant, to fit in with the case.
21. The Apex Court of India in
Jose Philip Mampillil Vs.
M/s.Premier Automobiles Ltd., & Another, reported in CDJ 2004 SC 281, though the condemned act and conduct of the
manufacturer or the dealer
in that case
, has not restored the order of the
District Forum, which directed replacement of the engine free of costs which
was upset by the State Commission, whereas gave direction to repair t

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
aler
in that case
, has not restored the order of the
District Forum, which directed replacement of the engine free of costs which
was upset by the State Commission, whereas gave direction to repair the
vehicle, pay damages etc., adding some more conditions, thereby, informing that
replacement of engine, alone was not the remedy. From
the facts available therein, it is clear even at the time of taking delivery,
the car was defective, since there were defects in the paints, and that the
piston rings of the engine had gone. In
spite of that, only compensation and repair alone was contemplated, and
question of replacement of the engine as directed by the District Forum not
restored.
22. The Apex Court in
Indochem Electronic and
another Vs. Addl
. Collector of Customs, A.P., reported
in 2006 (3) CTC 74, has observed that If such breaches of conditions
of warranty admittedly had taken place during the period of warranty, no
exception can be taken to the judgement and order passed by the Statement Commission
as also the National Commission. Further
observing that From the aforementioned conduct of the Appellant itself, it may be
inferred that it voluntarily undertook to meet the requirements of the
Respondent relating to mal-functioning, etc. of the said system despite expiry
of the period of warranty. For all
intent and purport, the period of warranty, thus, stood extended. As the d

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
ents of the
Respondent relating to mal-functioning, etc. of the said system despite expiry
of the period of warranty. For all
intent and purport, the period of warranty, thus, stood extended. As the defects in the system including
manufacturing defects, if any, were found not only during the period of
warranty but also during the extended period and as the Appellant itself
undertook to attend to the complaints received in that behalf, in our opinion,
it is too late, for it now to contend that in view of the fact that the period
of contract or warranty expired, it had not liability therefore. Thus, it is seen, if the mal-functioning of
the car or defect in the engine, had occurred during the warranty period, then
continued, not attended effectively, by the manufacturer or the service
provider undertaking to rectify the mistake, then it could be held that the
warranty period stood extended, not otherwise.
In this decision also,
Section 12
of Sale of Goods of Act was
considered, where, Condition and Warranty are available. Considering 12 (3) of that Section, in Para 28
of the judgement, it is stated Although
in terms of sub-section (3) of
Section 12
, no right accrues to a purchaser to
reject the goods on breach of stipulation of warranty, the same would not mean
that the extent of damages cannot be equivalent to the price of the goods in as
much as such a power has specifically b

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
o
reject the goods on breach of stipulation of warranty, the same would not mean
that the extent of damages cannot be equivalent to the price of the goods in as
much as such a power has specifically been conferred upon the Commission, further
observing it is true, where a stipulation in a contract of sale is a warranty,
its breach may give rise to a claim for damages but not to a right to reject
the goods and treat the contract as repudiated; but, where a stipulation in a
contract of sale is a condition, its breach may give rise not only to a claim
for damages but also generally to a right to treat the contract as repudiated.
23. In M/s. Hyundai Motors India Ltd., Vs.
M/s.Hyundai Motors India Ltd., & Another, the National Commission had an occasion to consider the manufacturing
defect, and the conduct of Multi-National Company, manufacturing a car having
defects. As seen from the facts of the
case, within the period of one year, from the date of purchase of the vehicle,
fuel leaking occurred, white smoke reported, followed by running repair,
wherein, within the period of warranty, engine was dismantled, head assembly
repaired, and in this view, a direction came to be issued, to repay the entire
cost, in addition to, compensation and this decision will not come to the aid
of the complainant which period has run from the date of purchase exceeding the
warranty period also. Based

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
ay the entire
cost, in addition to, compensation and this decision will not come to the aid
of the complainant which period has run from the date of purchase exceeding the
warranty period also. Based upon
the
above decision
, the facts of the case should be seen.
24. The warranty period in
this case come to an end on 5.6.2001.
Therefore, we have to see within the period of warranty, whether the
complainant had complained any defect in the engine, in order to say, that
existed even during the period of warranty, so as to apply the dictum of the
Supreme Court ruling extending the period of warranty. As rightly submitted by the appellants,
during the period of warranty, for one year, there was no complaint of any
problem in the engine, whether it is jerking or abnormal noise as the case may
be and as seen from the repair order dated 6.7.2001 alone, the
Customer/Complainant complained about the vehicle jerking, and abnormal noise,
which was repaired as seen from the document dated 7.7.2001 (Ex.A4). Further,
as seen from the vehicle repair history, engine and other problems reported,
only after the period of warranty.
25. The learned senior counsel
submitted that the defect was admitted by the opposite parties, also not acceptable
to us, since the letter dated 17.1.2005, is not clear, regarding the defect
therein as if that had occurred during the period of warranty, as seen from
Pa

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
by the opposite parties, also not acceptable
to us, since the letter dated 17.1.2005, is not clear, regarding the defect
therein as if that had occurred during the period of warranty, as seen from
Para 2 of the letter dated 17.1.2005. Only after the vehicle run more than 20,000
kms, the complainant had raised the engine vibration, at idling and this defect
alone is stated in the notice, however.
Since the engine head was opened for repairing the defect, your client demanded
that 70% of the cost of repair be borne by the dealer that does not mean, that the defect was
admitted from the day one of the purchase, or within the period of
warranty. Therefore, on the basis of the
so called admission, it is not possible, for us to conclude that the defect was
admitted, that too, within the period of warranty, which should be construed as
extended, thereby, compelling the manufacturer, to replace the vehicle.
26. The perusal of the records
filed on behalf of the complainant, would disclose that jerking or vibration was
reported only after the period of warranty and therefore, the Forum cannot
compel the opposite parties, to replace the engine since the problem might have
occurred for some other reasons, certainly not because of manufacturing defect
or defect which had occurred within the period of warranty. As per the condition and warranty, if at all,
the complainant can claim damages,

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
ther reasons, certainly not because of manufacturing defect
or defect which had occurred within the period of warranty. As per the condition and warranty, if at all,
the complainant can claim damages, if deficiency in service is proved and he
cannot reject the goods asking for new one, which is prohibited. Here also, as and when reported, repairs were
rectified, and the complainant not satisfied, finally left the vehicle with the
second opposite party, for which, they cannot be held responsible, since they
have reported, that the vehicle is ready after repair, asking the complainant
to take delivery. Probably, to avoid the
expenses, and when there was dispute in sharing the cost of the repair, it
seems, the complainant left the vehicle, and approached the Forum, after 4
years and in this view, we find no deficiency in service, which was not properly,
considered by the District Forum. For
the foregoing reasons, we conclude, that the complainant is neither entitled to
replacement nor compensation, and the appeal deserves acceptance.
27. In
the result, both the appeals are allowed, setting aside the order of the
District Forum in O.P.213/2005, dated 31.07.2006 and the complaint is
dismissed.
28. However,
taking into consideration, that even after the warranty period, first and
second opposite parties have undertaken to repair the vehicle in question, they
are directed to repair th

title: Chennai Ford, vs . R.Rathnavelu, on 31 December, 2009
text:
missed.
28. However,
taking into consideration, that even after the warranty period, first and
second opposite parties have undertaken to repair the vehicle in question, they
are directed to repair the vehicle at free of cost as special case and hand
over the same to the complainant, issuing notice within two months, from this
date. There will be no order as to cost, in both the appeals.

                   This appeal is directed against the order dated 26.10.2022, rendered by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, U.T. Chandigarh    (hereinafter to be referred as "the Ld. Lower Commission"), vide which, it dismissed the complaint bearing No.CC/463/2020,being without any merit.
2.             Before the Ld. Lower Commission, it was case of the complainants/appellants that   they in order to visit the Holy City of Shirdi for religious purpose, booked   air-tickets of Opposite Party No.1 Airlines, through Opposite Party.2,for journey   from Delhi to Shirdi for 27.12.2019 and  for return journey  from Shirdi to Delhi on 28.12.2019, by making payment of Rs.16,600/- and Rs.14,649/- respectively and the same were confirmed by Opposite Party No.1 (Annexure C-2 & C-6). It is stated that the complainants had also made booking of Shatabdi Train from Chandigarh to Delhi for 27.12.2019, Hotel Stay in Shirdi for one night at Hotel Temple Tree for 27/28.12.2019 and booking for return journey from Delhi to Chandigarh via Volvo Bus for 28.12.2019. However, on reaching Delhi Airport well in time, after getting check-in when they were   standing in the queue with

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023
text: d booking for return journey from Delhi to Chandigarh via Volvo Bus for 28.12.2019. However, on reaching Delhi Airport well in time, after getting check-in when they were   standing in the queue with boarding passes in hand to board the plane, suddenly the officials of Opposite Party No.1 Airlines closed the boarding gates and informed the complainants that their flight from Delhi to Shirdi has been cancelled.  However, no reason was given   for cancellation of the flight.  Opposite Party No.1 neither made any alternative arrangement/flight to reach Shirdi, nor offered any hotel/accommodation for stay in Delhi nor made any arrangement for return journey of complainants to Chandigarh.  Having no option, the complainants were forced to return to Chandigarh and as such, they had to purchase on the  spot fresh air tickets in emergency of Air Asia by paying an amount of Rs.17,682/- (Annexure C-4) for Delhi to Chandigarh flight.   When  complainants agitated the matter with the Opposite parties, they raised a false ground that the flight was cancelled due to bad weather.  The complainants then sent notice through email to the OP airline on 21.1.2020  to look into their grievance and harassment suffered by them but Opposite Party NO.1 instead of apologizing   replied that they do not have any provision to alternative flight or hotel accommodation and compensation to the passengers in

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023
text:
ssment suffered by them but Opposite Party NO.1 instead of apologizing   replied that they do not have any provision to alternative flight or hotel accommodation and compensation to the passengers in this regard. It is further stated that even the Opposite party No.1 failed to provide the full refund of the air tickets  which is stated to be violative against the policy of the Government of India. Hence, alleging deficiency in service  and unfair trade practice on the part of the Opposite parties due to which  the complainants have to suffer financial loss, mental agony and physical harassment, a consumer complaint was filed before the Ld. Lower Commission.
3.                    Pursuant to issuance of notice of the complaint, both the opposite parties contested the complaint before the Ld. Lower Commission.  Opposite Party No.1 in its reply admitted the  factual matrix of the case but  stated that due to "Bad Weather" at Shirdi, the Opposite Party  was constrained to cancel the flight No.SG-946 from Delhi to Shirdi and accordingly  as per the directions of Air Traffic Control(ATC), the  flight in question was  cancelled and intimation about the said cancellation was sent to the complainants by way of e-mail and SMS on their email id and mobile number on 27.12.2019 at 12.38 hours. According to the Opposite Party,  the complainants were given an option to seek full refund or get

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023
text: mplainants by way of e-mail and SMS on their email id and mobile number on 27.12.2019 at 12.38 hours. According to the Opposite Party,  the complainants were given an option to seek full refund or get an alternate flight by contacting the reservation helpline, but the complainants did not seek the assistance of Opposite Party  for availing alternate flight and as such, full refund of Rs.16,660/- was made on 9.1.2020 and Rs.399/-  were remitted to the complainants on 16.1.2020  through travel agent i.e. OP No.2.  It is also submitted that the complainants were 'No Show' for the next day's flight from Shirdi to Delhi and though Opposite Party No.1 has an unequivocal  right to forfeit the said amount towards return ticket, yet as a goodwill gesture,  the entire return ticket amount of Rs.14,649/- was refunded to the complainants through Opposite Party  No.2 i.e. their travel agent on 28.12.2019 itself.  It is further stated that no damages, whatsoever, were suffered by the complainant and even otherwise as 'Terms of Carriage' which is a contract binding upon the parties, the Opposite Party had an unequivocal and unconditional authority to delay/cancel/pre-pone or divert the flight due to bad weather or other technical defects or for the other reasons beyond its control, for which it could not be made liable.  It is further stated that all airlines are governed by the Rules and Reg

4.                   Opposite Party No.2 in its reply   while admitting the factual matrix of the case  stated that the sole grievance of the complainants is against Opposite Party No.1.  It  was stated  that the  answering OP had duly issued the desired confirmed flight bookings on the desired date to the complainants and after the issuance of the confirmed flight bookings, the answering OP was discharged of its obligations qua th

issued the desired confirmed flight bookings on the desired date to the complainants and after the issuance of the confirmed flight bookings, the answering OP was discharged of its obligations qua the bookings and service provider. It was further stated   that the complainants did not disclose that the answering OP has duly processed the complete refund amounting to Rs.31,589/- on 3.1.2020 for both the onwards and return sector flight bookings.  It is stated that answering OP has duly performed all its duties by issuing the concerned flight bookings and by further processing the refund at the instance of cancellation by Opposite Pary No.1,  as the refunds are processed as per the airline fare rules and cancellation policy.  It was further stated that no cause of action arose qua the answering Opposite Party and  the complainants have failed to make out any case against the answering Opposite Party for the alleged deficiency in service and unfair trade practice and a prayer was made for dismissal of the complaint.
5.                  On appraisal of the complaint,  evidence adduced on record and after  hearing Counsel for the parties,  Ld. Lower Commission dismissed the  complaint of the appellants/ Complainants, being without any merit.
6.                 Dissatisfied with  the aforesaid order passed by the Ld. Lower Commission, the instant Appeal  has been filed by the Appell

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023

of the appellants/ Complainants, being without any merit.
6.                 Dissatisfied with  the aforesaid order passed by the Ld. Lower Commission, the instant Appeal  has been filed by the Appellants/Complainants for quashing and setting aside the impugned order dated 26.10.202 and further to allow the consumer complaint with costs.
7.                     We have heard Counsel for the parties,  and have gone through the evidence and record of the case with utmost care and circumspection.
8.                 The main ground, in the appeal, urged by the appellants is that  there is not a single document produced  on record by the airline that the flight was cancelled due to bad weather in Delhi but the Ld. Lower Commission without even considering the documents on record passed the impugned order.  It is contended that the staff of the airline neither   informed  in advance about the cancellation of the flight, nor, gave any reason nor explained that why the flight was cancelled when the appellants family was almost about to enter the plane. The respondent No.1 did not make any alternative arrangement to reach Shirdi, nor any hotel/accommodation for stay in Delhi was provided. Thus, respondent No.1 airline had not taken any concrete steps to take care of the passengers of their cancelled flight and as such the appellants have to suffer immense mental agony, physical harassmen

us, respondent No.1 airline had not taken any concrete steps to take care of the passengers of their cancelled flight and as such the appellants have to suffer immense mental agony, physical harassment and monetary loss.
9.                  At the time of arguments, the learned Counsel for the appellants submitted that as the respondents have not placed on record any document with regard to bad weather due to which the flight in question was cancelled on 27.12.2019, he may be given time to produce some documents/certificate from the concerned authorities/ATC with regard to weather on 27.12.2019 for rebutting the contention of the respondents. On request, sufficient time was granted to obtain the information.  Ultimately, Counsel for the appellants placed on record  information sought through RTI, which is as under ;

It is not very clear, whether the applicant asked the number of arrivals and departures for which date.  However, on 27.12.2019, total number of arrivals is 8 and total number of departure is 8, total movement 16.
The above information placed on record by the appellants does not speak about the status of weather forecast on 27.12.2019. Arrival and departures of flights from Delhi or Shirdi Airport on 27.12.2019 does not support the case of the appellants that there was no bad weather on that date. In reply to the contention of Counsel for the appellants, it was submitted by Counsel for the respondents that bad weather does not happen in advance and as such no advance intimation of the same could have been given to the appellants and other passengers.  It is further submitted that as soon as the respondents came to know about bad weather at Shirdi and consequent cancellation of the flight by the ATC, the passengers including the appellants were informed and they were offered the next available flight, which was on the next day, but the appellants did not avail the said facility. It was further submitted that respon

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023
text:
luding the appellants were informed and they were offered the next available flight, which was on the next day, but the appellants did not avail the said facility. It was further submitted that respondent NO.1 is a low cost airline and does not provide any arrangement for boarding and lodging. As the appellants did not avail the offer of next flight, the entire ticket charges were refunded to them.
10.                The Ld. Lower Commission rightly observed that the  claim of the appellants/ complainants that their flight from Delhi to Shirdi scheduled for 27.12.2019 through OP Airlines was cancelled without any reason is not justified.  It further observed that the respondent No.1/Opposite Party No.1 has rightly cancelled the flight in question due to "Bad Weather" at Shirdi as well as on  the  directions of ATC in this regard.  It was further observed that   as the reason for cancellation of the flight in question was beyond the power and control of the Airline, no deficiency in service is made out against OP Airline.
11.              On the aspect of grant of compensation, the Ld. Lower Commission rightly observed that  as per Clause 1.4 and 1.5 of Civil Aviation Requirements issued by DGCA, the airline is not liable to pay compensation in respect of cancellations and delays which are attributable to ATC (Air Traffic Control), meteorological conditions, unexpected flight sa

title: Vipan Sharma vs Spice Jet Ltd on 26 June, 2023
text:
ssued by DGCA, the airline is not liable to pay compensation in respect of cancellations and delays which are attributable to ATC (Air Traffic Control), meteorological conditions, unexpected flight safety shortcomings, operational and technical reasons etc. or any other causes that are beyond the control of the airline but which effect their ability to operate flights on schedule. Similar is the position in the present case, therefore, the complainants/appellants  are not entitled to any compensation.
12.                  Counsel for the appellants could not show anything to the contrary which may persuade us to interfere in the order.   We find  that no case is  made out to interfere in the order, under challenge.
13.                  For the reasons recorded above, the appeal, being devoid of merit, must fail, and the same is dismissed,   with no order as to costs. The order of the Ld. Lower Commission is upheld.

 M. THANIKACHALAM .J, PRESIDENT
1. The
complainants are the appellants.
2. Brief
facts:
The
complainants / appellants, being the family members, have booked air tickets,
in the 2nd opposite party airlines, through the 1st
opposite party, their recognized agent, for travel on 17.9.2004, from Belgaum,
via Bangalore to Chennai, by flight No.DN 205, and Bangalore to Chennai by
flight No.DN 121, in order to celebrate Vinayagar Chathurthi pooja on
18.9.2004, in the house at Chennai. As scheduled, when they reached Belgaum
airport at 6.30 a.m., on 17.9.2004, to their surprise and shock, they were
informed, that Belgaum flight has been cancelled, advising to get the refund
value of air ticket, from their agent, i.e., the 1st opposite party
at Chennai.
3. The
request of the complainants to make arrangements by accommodating in any one of
the flights, operated by the 2nd opposite party to Chennai, not
conceded, and they have also previously not informed to the passengers,
regarding the cancellation. The sudden
cancellation, without advance information, and not-making alternative
arrangement for the confirmed tickets,
should be construed as not only as negligent act, but also as deficiency

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
ation. The sudden
cancellation, without advance information, and not-making alternative
arrangement for the confirmed tickets,
should be construed as not only as negligent act, but also as deficiency in
service. Because of the deficiency in
service, committed by the opposite parties, the complainants were compelled to
go to railway station, constrained to purchase tickets, incurring expenses,
thereby they have put to mental agony, depression etc., incurring additional
expenses also, for which the opposite parties are liable.
4. The 1st
opposite party arbitrarily deducted a sum of Rs.452/- towards transaction fee,
which they are entitled, and for the delay of refund also, the complainants are
entitled to interest. Claiming
compensation, notice was issued dt.21.11.2004, for which neither there was
reply, nor compliance, thereby the complainants are constrained to file the
case to recover a sum of Rs.1,31,649/- in all.
5. The
opposite party, admitting the booking of tickets, by the complainant, from
Belgaum to Chennai, via Bangalore, opposed the claim contending that due to
technical reasons, the flight was cancelled, which was informed to all the
passengers viz. 18, booked their
ticket for flight on 17th September, through their call centre, and
therefore it is incorrect to say that the 2nd opposite party,
announced the cancellation of the flight, surprisingly on the arrival of t

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
et for flight on 17th September, through their call centre, and
therefore it is incorrect to say that the 2nd opposite party,
announced the cancellation of the flight, surprisingly on the arrival of the
complainant at Belgaum airport, that the 2nd opposite party,
refunded the amount to the 1st opposite party, who in turn refunded
the amount to the complainant, which was received without any protest, and as
such the opposite parties have not committed any deficiency, that too in not
providing alternative accommodation, since their air service was the low cost
operation in India, committed to provide service to all, thereby praying for
the dismissal of the complaint, denying
other averments also.
6. The
District Forum, by its order dt.21.7.2008, recorded a finding that the
cancellation of flight was informed through the call centre, even on16.9.2004,
that as per the terms and conditions available in the air ticket itself, refund
was given, and in the conduct of the opposite parties, there was no deficiency
of service, thus concluding, the complaint was dismissed, which is impugned
once again, seeking redressal before us.
7. It is the
common case of the parties, that the complainants have booked their travel
ticket, in the 2nd opposite party airlines on 17.9.2004, through the
1st opposite party, even on 6.8.2004 itself, confirming the schedule. On 17.9.2004, when the complainants

text:
have booked their travel
ticket, in the 2nd opposite party airlines on 17.9.2004, through the
1st opposite party, even on 6.8.2004 itself, confirming the schedule. On 17.9.2004, when the complainants came to
Belgaum airport, according to the complainants, they were informed at the
airport alone, regarding the cancellation of the flight, thereby delaying their
journey, not only that, but also compelling them to travel by train, taking
tickets at 11th hour, thus creating tension, torture, travel
expenses etc., It is also an admitted
fact, after 10 days or so, the 1st opposite party refunded the
amount, less transaction fee, which was acknowledged by one of the complainants,
without any protest, as seen from Ex.A7.
After receiving the amount, the complainants expressing their
experience, hardship suffered, claimed compensation, including the refund of
the deducted portion, alongwith other travel expenses, declined or not complied
with, resulting consumer complaint, ending in failure. In this context, we have to see, what are the
conditions available in the air ticket, which should be taken as the binding
terms and conditions of the contract, between the parties.
8. The
airlines may be compelled to cancel their flight, due to technical reasons,
beyond their control, and therefore mere cancellation of a flight, that too low
cost operation of flight, like the 2nd opposite party, cann

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
compelled to cancel their flight, due to technical reasons,
beyond their control, and therefore mere cancellation of a flight, that too low
cost operation of flight, like the 2nd opposite party, cannot be
perse faulted. In this case, the flight
which was to commence its journey on 17.9.2004,
cancelled due to technical defense, as urged before us, which is not
very much under challenge. Therefore,
for the cancellation of the flight by the 2nd opposite party, we
cannot find fault, but it is the duty of the airlines to inform in advance to
the passengers, to have their alternative accommodation thereby not causing
inconvenience, and if possible, providing alternative travel arrangement
also. In this case, the opposite parties
have not undertaken, to provide alternative flight, since the scheduled flight
itself was not able to be operated, because of some technicalities. Therefore, the non-providing of alternative
flight, or accommodation in anyother flight, since it is not made out by the
complainant, that they have operated the same on the same day, may not be
faulted or considered as deficiency in service.
If at all, the non-information if any can be faulted. That is., also one
of the deficiency in service, alleged in the complaint.
9. At the
time of the booking the travelers are required to furnish their contact
numbers, and the purpose is to contact them, incase of emergency

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
the deficiency in service, alleged in the complaint.
9. At the
time of the booking the travelers are required to furnish their contact
numbers, and the purpose is to contact them, incase of emergency like cancellation
of flight etc. In this case, the
complainants have given their land line number at Chennai, though they have
planned to travel from Belgaum to Chennai, via Bangalore. It is not the case of the complainants, that
they have given Belgaum number, or any mobile number, to have easy access by
the call centre. Therefore, when the 2nd
opposite party had decided to cancel the flight, even on 16th
September 2004, due to technical reasons, they have informed their call centre,
requesting them to inturn inform to all the passengers, who have given their
contact number. Accordingly, as seen
from Ex.B1, the call centre had informed the cancellation of the flight on
16.9.2004 itself, though it was Madras number, since they had no other number,
to contact the complainants. If at all
the Madras
number, who received the information, ought to have informed the complainant,
and that for failure, the opposite parties cannot be made responsible. The information find in Ex.B1 communication,
is not proved to be false, in our view, it must be correct. The complainants have not given their mobile
number, or Belgaum number, thus we conclude, it is not a case of sudden
cancellation of the f

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
,
is not proved to be false, in our view, it must be correct. The complainants have not given their mobile
number, or Belgaum number, thus we conclude, it is not a case of sudden
cancellation of the flight on 17.9.2004, and even prior to that, i.e., on 16.9.2004,
itself information was given to the passengers, including the complainants,
which could not be reached, because they have not provided the alternative
phone number.
10. The
complainants, unfortunately, probably not informed, by Madras member landed at
Belgaum airport, and they came to know about the cancellation only there, for
which we cannot affix the label of deficiency of service. At the airport they were informed about the
cancellation, endorsement also made in the tickets, to refund the amount,
requesting the passengers to approach their booking agent, for getting
refund. In this way, as we have already adverted
to above under Ex.A7, payments were made, received without protest, and
therefore, it is not open to the complainant to say now, they are entitled to
more amount, or the opposite party had deducted arbitrarily the amount due to
them, especially the 2nd opposite party is concerned, since the 2nd
opposite party had advised the 1st opposite party, to refund the
entire amount. In this context, we have
to seen the conditions available in the ticket also.
11. In the
ticket, under the heading delays/ cancellatio

title: Arvind V. Joshi 2. Tmt. Survana A. Joshi ... vs M/S. Ram Mohan & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 224, ... on 27 June, 2011
text:
had advised the 1st opposite party, to refund the
entire amount. In this context, we have
to seen the conditions available in the ticket also.
11. In the
ticket, under the heading delays/ cancellation, and changes in schedule it is specifically stated that the carrier may
without notice, cancel or delay a flight, due to various reasons, as enumerated
therein and one of the reasons is mechanical failure, which will come within
the meaning of technical reasons.
Therefore, as per the terms and conditions also, the carrier is entitled
to cancel the flight, since they cannot take the risk of the passenger, when
the aircraft, is not fit for flying as per the standard. The District Forum, considering the above
said terms and conditions, available in the ticket, as well as relying upon
certain rulings of the State Commissions, has come to an unerring conclusion,
that the cancellation was due to technical reasons, and as such there was no
deficiency of service, and since the complainant had already got refund of the
amount, is not entitled to any relief, which finding we endorse,
unhesitatingly, thereby concluding the appeal is devoid of merits.
12. In the result, the appeal is dismissed,
confirming the order of the District Forum n O.P.No.73/2005 dt.21.7.2008. There will be no order as to cost
throughout.

 SHRI.M.K.ABDULLA SONA,MEMBER
Both appeal prefers from the order passed by the CDRF, Thrissur in CC.No.124/06 dated 15.12.01.  The Appeal No.223/12,  the appellant is the opposite party prefers this appeal from the order passed by the forum below that the appellant/opposite party is directed to pay Rs.50,000/- as compensation with cost of Rs.1,000/- within 2 months from the date of receipt of copy of the order.  If the amount is not paid within the prescribed time,   the complainant would be entitled to get 12% interest for compensation amount from the day of order till the realization.
2.  The Appeal No.264/12 filed  by the appellant/complainant who prefers this order from the above order on the ground that he is not satisfied with the amount ordered by the forum below.  Hence he prays to enhance the amount of compensation and costs ordered by the forum below.

 HARNAM SINGH THAKUR,  JUDICIAL MEMBER:
Revision Petition is preferred against the order dated  16.10.2019 in execution Case No.88 of 2019 filed in Consumer complaint No. 225 of 2018 passed by the learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Karnal (In short 'the forum) vide which  bailable warrants has been issued against O.P.No.1-petitioner.
2.      The brief facts of the case are that the complainant is practicing lawyer, at Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, District Court Karnal since 2001. During the summer vacation, the complainant planned to spend their vacation in Dalhousie, Himachal Pradesh. The complainant had booked the Royal Residency, Dalhousie from 20th June 2018 to 23rd June 2018 and paid Rs.10,620/- through credit card, which was duly credited in the account of OP No.2 through OP No.1, but, on 19th June 2018 no message of confirmation was received by him from OP.   On 20th June 2018 at 01.45 a.m. he received one SMS from OP No.1, which  shows that confirmation of the hotel booking in Royal Residency, but, the place was not mentioned.  He with their two children started journey by their own car from Karnal to Dalhousie and reached Dalhousie at about

title: Make My Trip India vs Gagan Sehgal And Another on 22 January, 2020
text:
irmation of the hotel booking in Royal Residency, but, the place was not mentioned.  He with their two children started journey by their own car from Karnal to Dalhousie and reached Dalhousie at about 7.00 p.m. on 20.06.2018. When he contacted the hotel, the manager of the hotel told him that  the booking of the room was not with it. The manager also told that the hotel booked by complainant namely Royal Residency is located at Ooty, Tamil Nadu.   At that time, the complainant booked room and paid Rs.20,000/- for two nights. The manager of the said hotel had given one mobile number of one Shri Amit who is state head of Make My Trip of Himachal Pradesh.  He requested Mr. Amit to refund the paid amount of Rs.10,620/- to him, but, to no avail.  Thus there was deficiency in service on the part of the O.Ps.
3.      Notice was issued to the opposite parties.  O.P.No.1 filed written version stating that the OP confirmed the booking of complainant for Royal Residency, Ooty instead of Royal Residency, Dalhousie are false and same are denied.   On 19.06.2018, the complainant got booked one room at Hotel Royal Residency, Ooty from 20.06.2018 to 23.06.2018 by paying an amount of Rs.10,620/- and accordingly, the OP No.1 confirmed the booking.  The complainant also inserted wrong email IDs at the time of confirming the bookings, as a result thereof, the complainant could not receive the hote

title: Make My Trip India vs Gagan Sehgal And Another on 22 January, 2020
text:
d accordingly, the OP No.1 confirmed the booking.  The complainant also inserted wrong email IDs at the time of confirming the bookings, as a result thereof, the complainant could not receive the hotel voucher on e.mail.  The complainant himself made the booking for wrong city i.e. Ooty instead of Dalhousie.  Thus there was no deficiency in service on the part of the O.P. No.1.
4.      O.P.No.2 was proceeded against ex parte vide order dated 28.11.2018.
5.      The argument has been advanced by Sh.Nitin  Bhasin, the learned counsel for the petitioner. With his kind assistance the original file including whatever the evidence has been led on behalf of  revisionist had also been properly perused and examined.
6.      After hearing learned counsel for the revisionist (JD No.1) we of the considered view that revision petition is without merits.  Revisionist company has challenged the order dated 16.10.2019 passed by the learned District Forum, Karnal vide which bailable warrants have been issued against petitioner(JD NJo.1) for not making the remaining payment.
7.      It is argued by learned counsel for the revisionist-JD No.1 that           share of  JD No.1-revisionist Rs.15,864/- has already been paid to the complainant-Gagan Sehgal and remaining payment is to be made by opposite party No.2. However, this contention of learned counsel for revisionist- J.D. No.1 is not much conv

title: Make My Trip India vs Gagan Sehgal And Another on 22 January, 2020
text:
as already been paid to the complainant-Gagan Sehgal and remaining payment is to be made by opposite party No.2. However, this contention of learned counsel for revisionist- J.D. No.1 is not much convincing because as per original order dated 21.05.2019 passed by the learned District Forum complaint has been allowed and O.Ps. have been directed to refund Rs.10,620/- to the complainant with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of deposit till its realization. Moreover, the O.Ps were also directed to pay Rs.20,000/-  on account of mental agony and harassment suffered by him and for the litigation expenses. The said order reveals that the liability of the O.Ps. including present revisionist is joint and it cannot be segregated to say that revisionist-JD No.1 has already paid its share to the complainant, therefore, it should be exonerated from the further liability and bailable warrants be recalled.
In support of his arguments, learned counsel for the revisionist has placed reliance upon the authorities of High Court of Madras and High court of Punjab and Haryana titled as
Avidayappan Chettiar Vs. Kanthimathi Ammal
decided on 28.07.1965,
Dharampal and Ors. Vs. Ram, Jawari and Ors. Decided
on 22.03.2010 respectively  and opinion of Hon'ble Supreme Court in civil Appeal No.188 of 1955 titled as
Topanmal Chhotamal Vs. Kundomal Gangaram and Ors. Decided
on 08.09.1959.
8.      In the

title: Make My Trip India vs Gagan Sehgal And Another on 22 January, 2020
text:
cided
on 22.03.2010 respectively  and opinion of Hon'ble Supreme Court in civil Appeal No.188 of 1955 titled as
Topanmal Chhotamal Vs. Kundomal Gangaram and Ors. Decided
on 08.09.1959.
8.      In the last mentioned authority (supra), it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the  question is whether in such circumstances an executing Court can go behind the decree & give the relief to the appellant which was expressly denied to him in the suit. The question so posed can only have one answer.  It is well-settled principle  that a Court executing a decree cannot go behind the decree: it  must take the decree as it stands, for the decree is binding and conclusive between the parties to the suit.  If the contention of the appellant were to be accepted, it would contravene the said principle; for, while the decree as construed by us, has directed that it should not be executed against the personal properties of the partners, the executing Court would be directing execution against the said partners.  While the decree excluded personal liability, the executing court would be imposing the same. This cannot obviously be done.
9.      A careful perusal of the above mentioned authorities relied upon by the learned counsel for the revisionist- J.D. No.1 reveals that these are not applicable and distinguishable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand as no recovery bein

title: Make My Trip India vs Gagan Sehgal And Another on 22 January, 2020
text:
ities relied upon by the learned counsel for the revisionist- J.D. No.1 reveals that these are not applicable and distinguishable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand as no recovery being made from the personal property of the opposite parties and if at all revisionist is having any grievance against the order dated 21.05.2019 order under execution regarding 50% liability of the revisionist-JD. No.1 then this issue can be raised  and clarified before the learned District Forum. More-so, no prejudice is going to be caused to the revisionist/O.P.No.1  if bailable warrants have been issued, for presence and payment.
10.    In the light of above discussion, foregoing revision petition is dismissed  being without merits.

DR. INDER JIT SINGH, PRESIDING MEMBER
1. These two First Appeals (FAs) have been filed by the under
section 19
of
Consumer Protection Act 2019, against the order dated 09.11.2016 of the State
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, (hereinafter referred to as the 'State
Commission'), in Consumer Complaint (CC) No. 47/2012.
2. First Appeal No. 573/2017 has been filed by the Appellant (hereinafter
referred to as Axis Bank), who was Opposite Party Nos.l&2 before the State
Commission and FA/1950/2017 has been filed by Appellant (hereinafter referred to
as Vodafone Mobile), who were Opposite Party Nos. 3 8i 4 before the State
Commission, inter alia praying for setting aside the impugned order passed by the
State Commission in CC/47/2017.
3. As both the Appeals have been filed against the same order of the State
Commission vide which State Commission has allowed the Complaint filed by the
Complainants against all the OPs-1 to 4, jointly & severally, these are taken up
together.
4. Notice was issued to the Respondent(s) in both the FAs on 18.04.2017 and
26.10.2017 respectively.
5. Brief facts of the cases, as presented by the Complainant a
