shes.
34. In the present case, the complainants have been waiting for

 possession for several years beyond the promised period. Even

 during the pendency of the present complaint, the Opposite Party

 has failed to establish that the project had been completed or that

 lawful possession could have been offered. The prolonged delay

 has deprived the complainants of the benefit of the property as

 well as the use of the money deposited by them. In such

 circumstances, requiring the complainants to continue waiting for

 possession would be wholly unfair and unjust.
35. We are, therefore, of the considered opinion that the Opposite

 Party has failed to perform its contractual obligations and has

 committed deficiency in service. Its conduct in collecting

 substantial amounts from the complainants without completing

 the project and delivering possession within the promised period

 also amounts to an unfair trade practice. The complainants are,

 therefore, entitled to seek refund of the amount deposited by them

36. Therefore, the complainants have prayed for a refund of

to

of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, relating to admissions.

 It is well settled that admissions constitute substantive evidence

 against the party making them.
In

, AIR 1960 SC 100,

37.
In view of the foregoing discussion and the law
laid down by
the

 Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgments referred to hereinabove,

 we are of the considered opinion that the Opposite Party has failed

 to deliver possession of the allotted plot within a reasonable period

1. Raka T.V. & Furniture Traders, Bhusawal, original opponent

challenges in this appeal order passed by District Consumer Forum,
2 F.A. No..: 1697-06
Jalgaon on 29.07.2006 while deciding the complaint case No.

195/2006.
2. Facts of the case are as under:
Complainant Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid, resident of Bhusawal

purchased colour Television (T.V.) of Samsung Company by Model

No. 21" 58 on 25.11.2004 for Rs. 15,500/-. Accordingly, bill No. 968

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
under:
Complainant Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid, resident of Bhusawal

purchased colour Television (T.V.) of Samsung Company by Model

No. 21" 58 on 25.11.2004 for Rs. 15,500/-. Accordingly, bill No. 968

was issued by the appellant to the complainant. It is found

immediately after purchase of said T.V. that, TV is not running

properly. Picture on the screen were disturbing, voice of the

television set fluctuates automatically etc. It is also doubted by the

complainant that television is locally assembled, but sold by

appellant with label of Samsung Company. Therefore, complainant

approached to appellant and demanded refund of the amount or

replacement of television. Appellant sent one mechanic to the house

of complainant. Said mechanic inspected the TV and informed the

complainant that, there is picture fault and it can be rectified in the

workshop only. Therefore, complainant approached to appellant and

requested to repair the said television, but appellant did not pay

heed. Therefore, complainant issued legal notice dated 01.02.2005.

Appellant did not issue the warranty card with the bill of TV

therefore, the doubt of complainant that TV given by appellant is not

of Samsung Company, but it was locally assembled, was strengthen

then complainant approached to Forum.
3 F.A. No..: 1697-06
3. Appellant appeared before Forum and denied the claim. It is

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
lant is not

of Samsung Company, but it was locally assembled, was strengthen

then complainant approached to Forum.
3 F.A. No..: 1697-06
3. Appellant appeared before Forum and denied the claim. It is

submitted by appellant that, the allegation of the complainant that,

locally assembled TV was sold by appellant with label of Samsung

company is not true. No any complaint received from the

complainant about non-functioning of TV. Mechanic from the shop

visited the house of complainant and tried to rectify the problem. It is

further submitted that, for the manufacturing defects in the goods not

the dealer but manufacturer is liable. As manufacturer is not made

party to the complaint, complaint is not maintainable.
4. After hearing both the parties District Forum directed appellant

to replace the TV or refund the amount of Rs. 15,300/- with interest @

6 % p.a. from the date of purchase.
5. Dissatisfied with the said judgment and order original

opponent came in appeal.
6. Notices of final hearing were served on both the parties. Adv.
Hemant Bhangale appeared for appellant and respondent appeared

in person. Adv. Bhangale vehemently argued the case. He submitted

that, as the complaint about no-functioning of TV was received,

immediately mechanic was sent to the house of complainant to

rectify the defect. Therefore, there is no deficiency in service on the

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
that, as the complaint about no-functioning of TV was received,

immediately mechanic was sent to the house of complainant to

rectify the defect. Therefore, there is no deficiency in service on the

part of appellant. Appellant is a dealer of goods and not
4 F.A. No..: 1697-06
manufacturer. For the complaint of manufacturing defect

manufacturer is liable. As the complainant did not make manufacture

as a party to the complaint, complaint is not sustainable for non-

joinder of party. Adv. Bhangale further submitted that, the District

Forum failed to consider the fact that dealer is only intermediater

between the manufacturer and consumer and he is wrongly ordered

to refund the amount or replace the TV set. In support of his

argument he produced the citation of National Commission-
7. i) In Classic Automobiles Vs. Lila Nand Mishra & Anr.,

 reported in I- (2010) CPJ 235 (NC). It is held by Hon'ble

 National Commission that, Manufacturing defects - Joint and

 several liability imposed on manufacturer absolved in appeal - Entire

 liability fixed on dealer - Hence revision - Onus to prove

 manufacturing defect lies on complainant - No expert evidence

 produced to prove defects cannot be termed as manufacturing defect -

 No expert evidence produced to prove manufacturing defect in

 vehicle.
It is also held by Hon'ble National Commission that, dealer not liable

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
rove defects cannot be termed as manufacturing defect -

 No expert evidence produced to prove manufacturing defect in

 vehicle.
It is also held by Hon'ble National Commission that, dealer not liable

unless show that, vehicle sold by manufacturer on principal to

principal basis. Dealer being a intermediator between consumer and

manufacturer, liability for manufacturing defect to be fixed on

manufacturer.
5 F.A. No..: 1697-06
ii) In
Abhinandan Vs. Ajit Kumar Verma & Ors.
, reported in I

(2008) CPJ 336 (NC). It is held by Hon'ble National Commission that,

Dealer can not be held liable for manufacturing defects in VCP- Orders of

Fora below not legally sustainable.
Both these authorities are not applicable to the instant case as in both

the cases manufacturer was party to the complaint, but he was

exempted from the liability by the Forum. Therefore, it is held that,

only dealer can not be held liable.
8. In the instant case, manufacturer is not party to the complaint.

In our view, dealer can get reimbursed the price from manufacturer

which he has to pay to the consumer for manufacturing defect of the

goods. In the case on hand dealer is made party to the complaint,

manufacturer is not party. As dealer was directed to replace the TV

set or to refund the price, he can recover the said amount from the

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
ds. In the case on hand dealer is made party to the complaint,

manufacturer is not party. As dealer was directed to replace the TV

set or to refund the price, he can recover the said amount from the

company, as he is authorized dealer of the company.
9. Respondent in person submitted that, immediately after

purchase of TV it is found that, there are manufacturing defects in the

TV set, therefore they approached to appellant. The mechanic from

appellant inspected the TV set and informed the complainant that,

there is picture problem which can be rectified at the workshop, but

appellant avoided to rectify the said TV set. On the contrary,

appellant behaved arrogantly with the complainant. It is submitted
6 F.A. No..: 1697-06
by complainant that, manufacturing defects are found in the

warranty period therefore, complainant is entitled to the replacement

of the TV set. It is also submitted by respondent that, as the appellant

supplied locally assembled TV with label of Samsung he did not

issue the warranty card of the company and thereby committed

unfair trade practice. As appellant is guilty of unfair trade practice he

avoided to give the proper service. Manufacturing defects were

found in the warranty period therefore, TV set can be replaced and

dealer can get it compensated by the company. But, appellant

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
ice he

avoided to give the proper service. Manufacturing defects were

found in the warranty period therefore, TV set can be replaced and

dealer can get it compensated by the company. But, appellant

avoided to redress the grievance of complainant, therefore District

Forum has rightly granted the relief.
10. We heard both the parties at sufficient length and perused the

record. Appellant is a dealer of Samsung Company. The TV set

started giving problems of manufacturing defects in warranty period

therefore; complainant is entitled for replacement of the TV set or

refund of amount. A person purchasing new goods for his

satisfaction, was constrained to approach the dealer or service center

again and again for repair of the new article is really causing mental

torture. As the manufacturing defects are found in warranty period,

appellant is liable to replace the TV set or refund the amount. We
relied on the citations of Hon'ble National Commission.
a. In
Maruti Suzuki (India) Ltd., Vs. Adulapuram Buchiraju

& Ors., III
(2008) CPJ 119 (NC). It is held by National Commission
7 F.A. No..: 1697-06
that, various defects noticed within warranty - Replacement of engine and

gear box advised by dealer - Consumer entitled to replacement of vehicle.
b. In
Kinetic Engineering (P) Ltd. & Anr. Vs. Santosh Kumar

Prasad, III
(2008) CPJ 266. It is held by Delhi State Commission -

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
text:
ear box advised by dealer - Consumer entitled to replacement of vehicle.
b. In
Kinetic Engineering (P) Ltd. & Anr. Vs. Santosh Kumar

Prasad, III
(2008) CPJ 266. It is held by Delhi State Commission -

False representation made regarding high average of vehicle - Unfair trade

practice - Brand new vehicle/goods if start giving trouble, time and again

person is forced to take it to workshop, still defect continues, vehicle/goods to

be declared defective.
District Forum rightly considered all the facts and record while

allowing the complaint. We are not inclined to interfere the judgment

and order of District Forum. We pass following order.
O R D ER
1. Appeal is dismissed.
2. Appellant to pay Rs.1,000/- as cost to the respondent.
3. Copy of the order be furnished to the parties.

Evidence Affidavit and got marked Ex.A1 to A3. The Opposite Party
No.4 filed evidence affidavit. Ex.B1 & B2 are marked on their
behalf.
11. The District Commission after hearing and considering the
material on record, allowed the complaint directing the Opposite
Party No.1 to 3 to pay each Rs.50,000/- in all with interest @ 12%
p.a. from the date of cancellation of flight ticket till realization. The
Opposite Party No.4 is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- with interest @
18% p.a. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposit

. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 preferred this appeal with the
following grounds:
 The District Forum grossly erred in holding that alternative
 arrangements were not done by the Opposite Parties. The
 alternative arrangements had to be done by Opposite Party
 No.3/Airlines but not by Appellant.
 The District Forum failed to consider that the Appellant is
 only facilitator and neither it had control nor operation of
 flight and cancellation.
5
 The District Forum failed to consider that the ticket amounts
 were refunded to Respondent No.1/Complainant.
  The District Forum failed to appreciate that the hotel rooms
 were booked through cleartrip.com and as per terms, if the
 person does not arrive on the first night of accommodation
 booked, the property will be released and they will be
 charged full. Hence, there is no role of Appellant in refund of
 hotel charges.
 The District Forum ought not to have held that there is a
 deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of
 the Appellant without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt.Chukka Shakuntala on 7 December, 2023
text:
t without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or whether it is liable to be set aside, modified
or interfered with, in any manner? To what relief?
14. We have perused the material available on record and heard
the counsel for the parties. On perusal of the record, we find that
Opposite Party No.3-Airlines was set exparte in the
CC.No.190/2018 on the file of District Commission, Adilabad,
however vide IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 they filed their
written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey

y the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey and rights of the
passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and
these conditions constitute a valid binding contract between
parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
16. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

ent
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

Tickets were booked on 17.05.2016 through travel agent Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 in the main complaint.
17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the
General Insurance Company engaged in the business of general
insurance including Air Travel Insurance in collaboration with
Respondent No.3/Opposite Party No.3.
18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant requested the Opposite Parties to arrange
alternate arrangements as they were on their way to Hyderabad
and the schedule was booked in advance for Darshan at Tirupathi
and accommodation at hotels in various places of pilgrimage. Due
to the sudden cancellation of the flight, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant incurred a heavy loss and suffered great
7
hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight ticke

text:
light is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably

oking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy

pposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for

iled are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.

thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.

impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the

there is delay in handing over the possession, it amounts to

has also been made to I (2017) CPJ 513 (NC) "Neha Suri versus

Unitech Reliable Project Pvt. Ltd." In that case, the possession

of the flat was not given as agreed. It amounts to deficiency in

service. Amount deposited alongwith interest was ordered to be

refunded. Similar order was passed in I (2017) CPJ 113 "Vishal

Issar v. Park Wood Developers Pvt. Ltd.". This Commission has

already held in Consumer Complaint No. 164 of 2016 "Harmit

Singh Arora versus M/s Country Colonisers Private Limited",

decided on 2.2.2017 against the same opposite party that in case

possession of the apartment has not been given as agreed then it

amounts to deficiency in service and that the complainants are not
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 10
bound to pay further payments when the project is not coming at

the site and refund alongwith interest order was ordered. Counsel

for Op No. 1 was unable to rebut it.
11. The main plea taken by Op No. 1 is that this agreement

is between the complainant, Op No. 1 and Alice Developers (Op

No.2) and the project was to be developed by Op No. 2 and that

Op No. 1 was just a confirming party but the payment receipts Exs.

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
ement

is between the complainant, Op No. 1 and Alice Developers (Op

No.2) and the project was to be developed by Op No. 2 and that

Op No. 1 was just a confirming party but the payment receipts Exs.

C-4 to C-8 show that the payments were received by Op No. 1.

Therefore, once the Op No. 1 has received the payment, then Op

No. 1 cannot take a plea that there is no liability even if the project

was to be developed by Op No. 2 as per authorization given by Op

No. 1. When payments were received by Op No. 1, then both the

Ops are vicariously liable to deliver the flat within the agreed time

and in case possession has not been delivered then the

complainant is entitled to the refund. Therefore, both Ops are jointly

and severally liable to pay the amount.
12. It has been further argued by the counsel for Op No.1

that according to Clause No. 4.c, in case there is delay in delivery

of the possession then the Ops are liable to pay the penalty as per

Clause 4.c(ii) i.e. @ Rs. 5/- per sq. ft. per month of super area for

the period of delay in offering the possession of the said apartment.

Whereas it has been contended by the counsel for the complainant

that in case of late payment, the Ops are claiming interest @ 18%

then similar treatment be given to the complainant. It is one sided

agreement and in case of default on the part of complainant, he

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
that in case of late payment, the Ops are claiming interest @ 18%

then similar treatment be given to the complainant. It is one sided

agreement and in case of default on the part of complainant, he

has to pay 18% interest whereas Ops are to pay just 3%. This
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 11
question has been dealt in detail by the Hon'ble National

Commission in CC No. 427 of 2014 "Satish Kumar Pandey &

Anr. Vs. M/s Unitech Ltd." decided on 8.6.2015 wherein the

Hon'ble National Commission observed as under:-
"However, a term of a contract, in my view will not be final and

 binding if it is shown that the consent to the said term was not

 really voluntary but was given under a sort of compulsion on

 account of the person giving consent being left with no other

 choice or if the said term amounts to an unfair trade practice. It

 was submitted by the learned counsel for the complainants that

 the term providing for payment of a nominal compensation such

 as Rs.5/- per square foot of the super area having become the

 order of the day in the contracts designed by big builders, a

 person seeking to buy an apartment is left with no option but to

 sign on the dotted lines since the rejection of such term by him

 would mean cancellation of the allotment. He further submitted

 that a person seeking to acquire a built up flat instead of

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
but to

 sign on the dotted lines since the rejection of such term by him

 would mean cancellation of the allotment. He further submitted

 that a person seeking to acquire a built up flat instead of

 purchasing a plot and then raising construction on it, therefore, is

 not in a position to protest resist the inclusion of such a term in the

 Buyer's Agreement, and has to rely upon the reputation of the

 builder, particularly if he is a big builder such as Unitech Ltd. He

 also submitted that the format of the Buyer's Agreement is never

 shown to the purchasers at the time of booking the apartment and

 if he refuses to sign the Buyer's Agreement on the format provided

 by the builder, not only will he lose the booking, even the booking

 amount/earnest money paid by him will be forfeited by the builder.

 I find merit in the above referred submissions of the learned
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 12
counsel. A person who, for one reason or the other, either cannot

 or does not want to buy a plot and raise construction of his own,

 has to necessarily go in for purchase of the built up flat. It is only

 natural and logical for him to look for an apartment in a project

 being developed by a big builder such as the opposite party in

 these complaints. Since the contracts of all the big builders

 contain a term for payment of a specified sum as compensation in

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
ject

 being developed by a big builder such as the opposite party in

 these complaints. Since the contracts of all the big builders

 contain a term for payment of a specified sum as compensation in

 the event of default on the part of the builder in handing over

 possession of the flat to the buyer and the flat compensation

 offered by all big builders is almost a nominal compensation being

 less than 25% of the estimated cost of construction per month, the

 flat buyer is left with no option but to sign the Buyer's Agreement

 in the format provided by the builder. No sensible person will

 volunteer to accept compensation constituting about 2-3% of his

 investment in case of delay on the part of the contractor, when he

 is made to pay 18% compound interest if there is delay on his part

 in making payment.
It can hardly be disputed that a term of this nature is wholly one

 sided, unfair and unreasonable. The builder charges compound

 interest @ 18% per annum in the event of the delay on the part of

 the buyer in making payment to him but seeks to pay less than 3%

 per annum of the capital investment, in case he does not honour

 his part of the contract by defaulting in giving timely possession of

 the flat to the buyer. Such a term in the Buyer's Agreement also

 encourages the builder to divert the funds collected by him for one

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
rt of the contract by defaulting in giving timely possession of

 the flat to the buyer. Such a term in the Buyer's Agreement also

 encourages the builder to divert the funds collected by him for one

 project, to another project being undertaken by him. He thus, is

 able to finance a new project at the cost of the buyers of the
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 13
existing project and that too at a very low cost of finance. If the

 builder is to take loan from Banks or Financial Institutions, it will

 have to pay the interest which the Banks and Financial Institutions

 charge on term loan or cash credit facilities etc. The interest

 being charged by the Banks and Financial Institutions for financing

 projects of the builders is many times more than the nominal

 compensation which the builder would pay to the flat buyers in the

 form of flat compensation. In fact, the opposite party has not even

 claimed that the entire amount recovered by it from the flat buyers

 was spent on this very project. This gives credence to the

 allegation of the complainants that their money has been used

 elsewhere. Such a practice, in my view, constitutes unfair trade

 practice within the meaning of
Section 2(r)
of the Consumer

 Protection Act, 1986 since it adopts unfair methods or practice for

 the purpose of selling the product of the builder. Though, such a

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
practice within the meaning of
Section 2(r)
of the Consumer

 Protection Act, 1986 since it adopts unfair methods or practice for

 the purpose of selling the product of the builder. Though, such a

 practice does not specifically fall under any of the Clauses of
Section 2(r) (1)
of the Act that would be immaterial considering

 that the unfair trades, methods and practices enumerated in
Section 2(r) (1)
of the Act are inclusive and not exhaustive, as

 would be evident from the use of word "including" before the

 words "any of the following practices".
The same view was upheld by the Hon'ble National Commission in
CC No. 347 of 2014, "Swarn Talwar & Ors. Vs. Unitech Ltd.
"

decided on 14.8.2015.
A reference has also been made to the

judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in "K.A. Nagmani Vs.

Housing Commissioner, Karnataka Housing Board", C.A. No.

6730-6731, decided on 19.9.2012.
In that case, the District Forum
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 14
has allowed interest @ 12% p.a. and its appeal was dismissed by

the State Commission as well as the Hon'ble National Commission

and after relying upon the judgment of "
Ghaziabad Development

Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
", (2004) 5 SCC 65, the interest @

18% per annum on the deposited amount was allowed alongwith

Rs. 50,000/- as compensation.
Against the judgment of the Hon'ble

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
velopment

Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
", (2004) 5 SCC 65, the interest @

18% per annum on the deposited amount was allowed alongwith

Rs. 50,000/- as compensation.
Against the judgment of the Hon'ble

National Commission in "
Swarn Talwar & Ors. Vs. Unitech Ltd.",

C.C. No.
347 of 2014 (supra), Op preferred the appeal before the

Hon'ble Supreme Court i.e. Civil Appeal No. 35562 of 2015,

decided on 11.12.2015 and passed the order as under:-
"We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and

 perused the record. We do not see any cogent reason to

 entertain the appeal. The judgment does not warrant any

 interference.
The Civil Appeal is dismissed."
13. It was further observed by the Hon'ble National

Commission in another judgment 2017(3) CLT 520 (NC) "Ankur

Goswami versus Supertech and another" that this clause in the

allotment letter would be applied to the case where allottee is

seeking possession of the flat and where allottee is not seeking

refund of the amount. However, in the present case, the allottee is

seeking the refund, therefore, the penalty @ Rs. 5/- per sq. ft. will

not be applicable. Further under Rule 17 i.e. Rate of Interest on

refund of advance money upon cancellation of agreement of
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 15
Punjab Apartment and Property Regulation Rules, 1995, it has

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
her under Rule 17 i.e. Rate of Interest on

refund of advance money upon cancellation of agreement of
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 15
Punjab Apartment and Property Regulation Rules, 1995, it has

been provided as under:-
"17. Rate of Interest on refund of advance money upon

 cancellation of agreement. - The promoter shall refund full

 amount collected from the prospective buyers under sub-

 section (1) of
section 6
together with interest thereon at the

 rate of twelve per cent per annum payable from the date of

 receipt of amount so collected till the date of re-payment."
In the above rule it has been observed to refund the amount

alongwith interest @ 12% p.a. In number of similar complaints, we

have allowed the interest @ 12% p.a. i.e.
Consumer Complaint No.

386 of 2016 "Meenakshi Puri versus Country Colonizers Pvt. Ltd. &

Ors.
", decided on 28.11.2017 and 'Consumer Complaint No. 3 of

2017 "Lt. Gurnur Singh Mahiwal & Anr. Versus M/s Country

Colonisers Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.", decided on 4.1.2018. Therefore, to be

just and reasonable, the complainant will be entitled to interest @

12% on the deposited amount.
14. No other point was argued.
15. Sequel to the above, we allow the complaint and direct

Ops to pay the amounts jointly and severally as under:-
(i) to refund a sum of Rs. 12,96,000/- to the

 complainant alongwith interest @ 12% p.a. from the

title: Harminder Singh Pannu vs Unitech Ltd. on 4 April, 2018
text:
the above, we allow the complaint and direct

Ops to pay the amounts jointly and severally as under:-
(i) to refund a sum of Rs. 12,96,000/- to the

 complainant alongwith interest @ 12% p.a. from the

 various dates of deposit till actual payment;
Consumer Complaint No. 429 of 2017 16
(ii) Ops are directed to pay a sum of Rs. 50,000/- as

 compensation on account of mental and physical

 harassment suffered by the complainant.
(iii) Ops pay Rs. 21,000/- towards litigation expenses.

 The above directions be complied by the Ops within a

period of 45 days from the date of receiving of the copy of the

order, failing which the complainant shall be at liberty to execute

the order by filing application under
Sections 25
&
27
of the CP Act

against the Ops.
16. The consumer complaint could not be decided within

the statutory period due to heavy pendency of Court cases.
17. The counsel for the parties / concerned parties are

directed to collect free certified copy of the order from the office of

the Commission within a period of 15 days from the date of

pronouncement.
(GURCHARAN SINGH SARAN)

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
RTIES :

 

                Shri Pankaj Waghmode, learned counsel for the appellants.

 

           Shri Ajay Dubey, learned counsel for the respondent.

 

 

 

 O R D E R
(Passed On 30.04.2024)

 

                        The following order of the Commission was delivered by A. K. Tiwari, Acting President:
This appeal by the opposite parties/appellants-National Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'insurance
-2-
company') is directed against the order dated 26.05.2016 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Rewa (for short the 'District Commission') in C. C. No. 193/2015 whereby the complaint filed by the complainant/respondent has been allowed.
2.                Briefly put, facts of the case as narrated by the complainant are that after taking finance from the Tata Motors Finance had purchased a Tata vehicle registration no. MP-17 HH-3771 which was insured with the opposite party no.3-insurance company for the period w.e.f. 08.02.2014 to 07.02.2015 for IDV of Rs.19,20,000/-.  On 09.12.2014 during currency of the policy period, his vehicle after colliding with a tree overturned and got damaged of which intimation was given to the insurance company on 09.02.2014. The insurance company appointed surveyor in the matter. The agent of the insurance company assured him to get the claim settled within a month. The complainant incurred Rs.3

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
nce company on 09.02.2014. The insurance company appointed surveyor in the matter. The agent of the insurance company assured him to get the claim settled within a month. The complainant incurred Rs.3,69,690/- in repairs of the subject vehicle. It is submitted that the complainant's vehicle was being driven by the driver having valid and effective driving licence.   The claim filed with the insurance company was repudiated by the insurance company on 18.06.2015. The complainant therefore, alleging deficiency in service on part of opposite parties, filed complaint before the District Commission, seeking compensation of Rs.3,69,690/- with costs of Rs.15,000/-
-3-
3.                The opposite parties-insurance company admitting receiving of intimation, survey of the subject vehicle and denial of claim denied the other allegations made in the complaint. It is submitted that as per documents made available by the complainant, the subject vehicle was having permit authorization for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the subject vehicle met with an accident on 09.12.2014 and therefore at the time of accident was running without having any valid permit authorization and therefore, the complainant's claim is not payable.
4.                The District Commission holding that there is no such condition in the policy document that vehicle cannot run without permit, the repud

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
fore, the complainant's claim is not payable.
4.                The District Commission holding that there is no such condition in the policy document that vehicle cannot run without permit, the repudiation of claim by the insurance company amounts to deficiency in service and therefore allowed the complaint directing the insurance company to pay Rs.1,57,475/- with interest @8% p.a. from the date of filing of complaint till payment. Costs of Rs.1,000/- is also awarded.
5.                Heard. Perused the record.
6.                Learned counsel for the opposite parties/appellants-insurance company argued that if the complainant was having valid permit authorization, he could have filed the same. He argued that the District Commission has committed grave error in not considering the fact that the complainant's vehicle being a transport vehicle cannot run on road without having valid permit authorization. He argued that as per provisions of
-4-
Motor Vehicles Act
, the period of validity of an authorization shall not exceed one year at a time. The subject vehicle was having valid permit authorization for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the subject vehicle met with an accident on 09.12.2014 and therefore at the time of accident was running without having any valid permit authorization. The insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim as the complainant's cla

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
accident on 09.12.2014 and therefore at the time of accident was running without having any valid permit authorization. The insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim as the complainant's claim was not payable. There has been no deficiency in service on part of the insurance company. He placed reliance on the decisions of this Commission in Appeal No.542/2007 (
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Smt. Sonia Lalchandani
) decided on 19.12.2007 and in First Appeal No.142/2017 (
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Sandeep Khemka
) decided on 11.01.2023.
7.                Learned counsel for the complainant/appellant argued that the District Commission rightly considering the fact that no such condition is mentioned in the policy that a transport vehicle cannot run without valid permit authorization, the insurance company has committed deficiency in service in repudiating the claim. He argued that the District Commission has rightly allowing the complaint directed the insurance company to pay compensation and costs.
-5-
8.                Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on going through the impugned order, the record of the District Commission and the provisions of the
Motor Vehicles Act
, we find that it has been categorically submitted by the opposite parties/appellants-insurance company that the subject vehicle at the time of accident was being driven without vali

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
otor Vehicles Act
, we find that it has been categorically submitted by the opposite parties/appellants-insurance company that the subject vehicle at the time of accident was being driven without valid permit authorization and this was the ground for repudiation taken by the insurance company in their repudiation letter.
9.
Section 66
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which deals with 'Necessity for permits' is relevant for deciding the issue involved in the matter which reads thus:
Section 66
. Necessity for permits:
(1).....
(2) .....
(3) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall not apply--
(i) to any goods vehicle, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 3,000 kilograms;
(p) to any transport vehicle while proceeding empty to any place for purpose of repair;
10.
Section 66(3)(p)
provides that the provision of permit do not apply to any transport vehicle, while proceeding empty to any place for purpose of repair. This sub-section is not applicable in the instant matter since it pertains to the empty transport vehicle and relying on this sub-section makes it amply clear that the empty transport vehicle as that of the complainant/appellant, can be run without permit only when it is taken to any place for purpose of repair.
-6-
11.              In the instant matter, the subject vehicle was insured with the opposite party insurance company for the period 08.02.2014 to 07.0

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
it is taken to any place for purpose of repair.
-6-
11.              In the instant matter, the subject vehicle was insured with the opposite party insurance company for the period 08.02.2014 to 07.02.2015 for IDV of Rs.19,20,000/- under the policy (C-1). The complainant has filed National Permit (C-24) valid for the period w.e.f.07.03.2013 to 06.03.2018. On the other hand, the insurance company has also filed the aforesaid document as D-5. The insurance company has filed authorization for National Permit in Form 45 (Under Rule 83(2) and Rule 87(2) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989) for All India (D-6) but that authorization is valid for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the accident took place on 09.12.2014.  The insurance company has filed D-7 investigation report dated 09.12.2014 wherein investigator Suresh Kumar Singh also opined that the authorization for All India Permit was valid for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014. D-9 is the certificate dated 23.03.2015 provided by the RTO Rewa wherein it has been specifically stated that the subject vehicle MP-17 HH-3771 was not having valid authorization of permit for MP on the date of accident i.e. 09.12.2014.
12.              It is also pertinent to mention here that Rule 87(3) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 specifically provided that the period of validity of an authorization shall not exceed on

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
4.
12.              It is also pertinent to mention here that Rule 87(3) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 specifically provided that the period of validity of an authorization shall not exceed one year at a time. From the above it is clearly established that on the date of accident i.e. 09.12.2014 the
-7-
subject vehicle was not having valid authorization of permit. The subject vehicle being used without valid authorization of permit which is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy as also the provisions of
Section 66(1)
of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
13.              Hon'ble National Commission in
Sudershan Giri Vs United India Insurance Company Limited & Anr
IV (2020) CPJ 3 (NC)Sudershan Giri
(supra) has clearly held that vehicle being used without valid permit is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy as also provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
.
14.              From the evidence on record, we find that admittedly, the complainant was using the subject vehicle without having a valid permit authorisation, which amounts to clear violation of
Section 66(1)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as also a fundamental breach of policy terms and conditions. Thus, we find that the insurance company has not committed any deficiency in service while repudiating the claim on account of violation of fundamental breach of policy

title: National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Surendra Singh on 30 April, 2024
text:
f policy terms and conditions. Thus, we find that the insurance company has not committed any deficiency in service while repudiating the claim on account of violation of fundamental breach of policy terms and conditions as also the provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
.
15.              Therefore, in view of the aforesaid and on the basis of provisions of law, we find that the District Commission has gravely erred in holding the insurance company deficient in service for repudiation of claim
-8-
on the ground that the subject vehicle was not having valid authorization of All India Permit at the time of accident and the complainant's vehicle could

 

run without permit since there is no such condition in the policy document. We do not find any deficiency in service on part of the insurance company in repudiating the claim.
16.              In view of the aforesaid, the impugned order cannot be sustained. Accordingly, it is hereby set-aside. Consequently, the complaint is dismissed.
17.              In the result, this appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed with no order as to costs.
(A. K. Tiwari)                          (Dr. Srikant Pandey)

of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against the impugned order dated 23.08.2016, passed by the Assam State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (hereinafter referred to as 'the State Commission') in First Appeal No. 33/2015, "State Bank of India & Ors. vs. Dr. J.C.S. Kataky", vide which, while dismissing the appeal, the order dated 13.08.2015, passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum Jorhat, allowing the consumer complaint No. 7/2014, filed by the complainant/respondent, was upheld.
2.       The facts of the case are that the complainant/respondent is the holder of a savings bank account No. 10354169732 with ATM facility in the RRL Jorhat Branch of the State Bank of India.  As stated in the consumer complaint, somebody claiming to be calling from the Mumbai office of the State Bank of India, telephoned the complainant at 08:00 PM on 08.08.2012, stating that his ATM card had been upgraded and its new number was 5196200003281481, valid from August 2012 to August 2016 and that the PIN will be sent through email and that his old ATM card had been blocked.  The said caller informed the complainant a

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
w number was 5196200003281481, valid from August 2012 to August 2016 and that the PIN will be sent through email and that his old ATM card had been blocked.  The said caller informed the complainant about the new PIN as well.  The said person also stated that the new ATM card had been delivered to the concerned branch office.  After some time on the same day, the complainant received a message on his mobile phone that his ATM card had been used for purchase worth ₹976/- on POS000000000015131.  A similar message of purchase worth ₹769/- on another POS was also received thereafter.  The complainant transferred the remaining amount in his account to his another account in the State Bank of India through internet banking.  On making online verification, he found that his savings bank account No. 10354169732 had been debited with another amount of ₹28,949/- but no message had been received pertaining to the said amount.
3.       On the next morning, the complainant contacted the SBI branch at Jorhat and on their advice, lodged an FIR with Pulibar Police Station.  A case was registered vide C/No. 151/12 under
section 420
IPC.  After investigation, the Police gave report that they could not trace the culprit and they submitted the same to the court.  The complainant approached the banking ombudsman as well, but they informed him vide order dated 11.03.2014 that the complaint had been

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
ot trace the culprit and they submitted the same to the court.  The complainant approached the banking ombudsman as well, but they informed him vide order dated 11.03.2014 that the complaint had been closed.  However, they stated that the complainant was free to approach any other forum of competent jurisdiction.  The complainant filed the consumer complaint in question, claiming refund of the amount of ₹28,949/- alongwith interest @11.5% p.a. and also litigation cost of ₹3,000/-
4.       In their written statement filed before the District Forum, the OP Bank stated that there was no record or evidence of any call made or SMS sent to the complainant by them.  The OP stated that the complainant could verify and inspect his account at the concerned branch of SBI.  The District Forum after considering the averments of the parties, concluded that a sum of ₹30,694/- (₹976/- + ₹769/- + ₹28,949) had been debited from the account of the complainant in the State Bank of India on 08.08.2012 at 8:00 PM by unknown miscreants, without the knowledge of the complainant.  The District Forum found deficiency in service on the part of the Bank in not trying to trace-out the transactions at the concerned point of sale.  The District Forum ordered that a sum of ₹30,694/- with interest @10% p.a. from 08.08.2012 should be paid to the complainant alongwith a compensation of ₹20,000/- and litigation c

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
rned point of sale.  The District Forum ordered that a sum of ₹30,694/- with interest @10% p.a. from 08.08.2012 should be paid to the complainant alongwith a compensation of ₹20,000/- and litigation cost of ₹3,000/-.  Being aggrieved against the said order of the District Forum, the OP challenged the same by way of an appeal before the State Commission.  The said appeal having been dismissed vide impugned order, the OP Bank is before this Commission by way of the present revision petition.
5.       Notice of the revision petition was sent to the complainant/respondent who appeared in person and was heard.  The arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner were also heard.
6.       The learned counsel for the petitioner Bank submitted that there was no question of any call being made at 8 PM to the complainant by any official of their Bank, because their working hours were upto 5 PM only.  The learned counsel stated that the transaction in question, could be done only, if the person making the transaction was aware of the debit card number, the expiry date, the PIN as well as the CVV number.  This whole information must have been given by the complainant himself to some other person, who could be instrumental in making the transactions in question.
7.       The learned counsel has drawn attention to the evidence affidavit filed by the Bank before the District Forum, in whi

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
person, who could be instrumental in making the transactions in question.
7.       The learned counsel has drawn attention to the evidence affidavit filed by the Bank before the District Forum, in which the whole process of obtaining the ATM card has been explained.  It is stated that a customer has to come physically to the Bank to take the secret PIN.  The cards etc. are sent by registered post, but the PIN is delivered in person.  There was no question of PIN having been delivered by any bank official on phone.  The learned counsel has also drawn attention to the manual delivered to the customers by the Bank, in which the whole process of issuing the card/PIN etc. had been explained and the necessary precautions to be observed by the complainants had also been listed.  It had been stated clearly in the said manual that the Bank had no liability for the unauthorised use of the card and the responsibility was fully upon the card holder.  In the same manual, the customers had been advised to change the PIN immediately on receipt of the same from the Bank.
8.       The complainant/respondent stated on the other hand that both the consumer fora below had passed orders in his favour and there was no sufficient ground to make any change in the said orders in exercise of the revisional jurisdiction.  The complainant stated that he had not divulged information about his card or PIN t

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
nd there was no sufficient ground to make any change in the said orders in exercise of the revisional jurisdiction.  The complainant stated that he had not divulged information about his card or PIN to anybody.  On the very next day of the incident, he had personally gone to his bank branch, and on their advice, had lodged an FIR with the Police.  The Bank was clearly deficient in service as they made no efforts to check the fraud inflicted upon him.  Moreover, it was the duty of the Bank to take up the matter with the local police and then ensure follow-up with them.  The complainant also stated that he had received SMS on his mobile phone in respect of two minor amounts only and not for the main amount of ₹28,949/-.
9.       We have examined the entire material on record and given a thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced before us.
10.     The main issue that requires consideration in the matter is whether it was the duty of the Bank to play any meaningful role in the matter when their own customer/complainant had reported to them about the alleged fraudulent transaction from his account on three different occasions on the same day.  The Bank has simply taken the plea that once the ATM card was issued to the complainant and a PIN was provided, it was the duty of the card holder to change the PIN immediately, and the Bank was not liable in any manner, if any fraudu

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
that once the ATM card was issued to the complainant and a PIN was provided, it was the duty of the card holder to change the PIN immediately, and the Bank was not liable in any manner, if any fraudulent transaction had taken place from that account.  In the written statement filed by the OP Bank before the District Forum, the Bank simply stated that there was no record or evidence of any call, SMS etc. having been made by any official of the Bank to the complainant.  They have further stated that an FIR was lodged by the complainant with the local police and as per the Police report, the accused persons were untraceable.  The Bank has stated in their reply as follows:-
"that to great regret the complainant lodged this complaint where the OP can do nothing but request the complainant to verify and inspect his account in the branch of the Bank where it is open for him."
11.     On the other hand, a perusal of the complaint indicates that specific numbers of point of sale (POS) terminals at merchant establishments (MEs) have been given, saying that there were purchases worth ₹976/- and ₹769/- on 2 occasions and these amounts were debited to the account of the complainant.  The complainant received messages also in respect of these two transactions from the Bank.  However, there was a third transaction of ₹28,949/- also and the said amount was debited from the account of the comp

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
ainant received messages also in respect of these two transactions from the Bank.  However, there was a third transaction of ₹28,949/- also and the said amount was debited from the account of the complainant, but no SMS etc. was received in respect of the said amount.  It is clear from the facts on record that the Bank flatly refused to even look into the matter, what to speak of making any investigation into the same.  Once the specific POS number had been given in the message received from the Bank itself to the complainant, the Bank could have very well verified the genuineness of these transactions, after establishing contact with the person or merchant establishment in possession of the said POS, but nothing of that sort was done.
12.     The OP Bank has consistently taken stand in their written reply as well as in the oral arguments before us that unless the particulars of the card number, PIN, expiry date and the Card Verification Value (CVV) are divulged to a third person, the card cannot be misused.  It is a matter of common experience that when some payment is made from a credit/debit card on some website, the details like the card number, the expiry date, the CVV number etc. are required.  In addition, a one time password (OTP) is generated and is sent to the mobile number of the consumer and such OTP is entered before the said transaction is complete.  However, for

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
etc. are required.  In addition, a one time password (OTP) is generated and is sent to the mobile number of the consumer and such OTP is entered before the said transaction is complete.  However, for making transaction in a merchant establishment (ME), the card is handed over to the staff of such establishment and the same is put into POS and a transaction takes place after simply recording the PIN, which is valid for the ATM machine as well.  It is worthwhile to mention here that the practice of entering the PIN on the POS terminal has been started only a couple of years back or so and before that, there was no requirement of entering the PIN as well.  It is very clear, therefore, that the transaction on a POS terminal could be made by simply providing the card to the personnel of the merchant establishment and there was no need of sharing the other details etc. with that establishment.  It was, therefore, necessary for the Bank to have carried out suitable investigation into the alleged transactions.
13.     The learned counsel for the petitioner Bank has drawn attention to the orders passed by this Commission from time to time in support of his arguments.
In the case "
Raghabendra Nath Sen & Anr. vs. Punjab National Bank" [I
(2015) CPJ 254], the issue involved was that a sum of ₹5,000/- was alleged to have been fraudulently taken out from the ATM machine. The Bank took the s

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
ra Nath Sen & Anr. vs. Punjab National Bank" [I
(2015) CPJ 254], the issue involved was that a sum of ₹5,000/- was alleged to have been fraudulently taken out from the ATM machine. The Bank took the stand that as per their record, two transactions of ₹5,000/- and ₹1,000/- on the ATM card had been made on the same date and the presumption was that both these transactions were made by the card holder himself.  This Commission also observed that the complainant did not lodge the complaint immediately with the Bank.  This Commission also noted that withdrawal from the ATM could not have taken place unless the PIN was shared with some other party.
It is obvious, therefore, that the facts of the case in "
Raghabendra Nath Sen & Anr. vs. Punjab National Bank
" (supra) are not applicable in the present case, as the present complaint relates to use of the card at POS terminal of a merchant establishment.
14.     Further in "
State Bank of India vs. K.K. Bhalla" [II
(2011) CPJ 106 (NC)], it was observed that the ATM card was very much in possession of the complainant and only he was aware of the four digit PIN number.  The matter related to the withdrawal of money from the ATM machine.  This Commission held that the withdrawal could not take place unless the ATM card or PIN fell in wrong hands.
In "
State Bank of India vs. Sansar Chand Kapoor & Anr." [II
(2015) CPJ 135], the issue was th

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
Commission held that the withdrawal could not take place unless the ATM card or PIN fell in wrong hands.
In "
State Bank of India vs. Sansar Chand Kapoor & Anr." [II
(2015) CPJ 135], the issue was the withdrawal of money from the ATM machine.  This Commission found that no cash from the account of the complainant could have been withdrawn without use of the ATM card and the complainant himself was aware of the PIN number.
15.     In another case cited by the complainant/respondent and relied upon by the State Commission, "Vidyawati vs. State Bank of India & Ors." [RP No. 4868/2012 decided on 18.02.2015], the allegation was that there had been unauthorised withdrawal from the savings accounts of the complainant as well as some other person.  This Commission held that since the money had been wrongly withdrawn by foul play from the account of the complainant as well as some other person, the bank was liable to make good the loss.
16.     Given the overall set of facts and circumstances of the case, it becomes abundantly clear that the citations given by the petitioner Bank as well as by the respondent relate only to the withdrawal of money from the ATM machine by the use of the PIN.  The present complaint has, however, different fact because the transactions were made at POS terminals at different merchant establishments.  Moreover, there was a third debit from the account of th

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
The present complaint has, however, different fact because the transactions were made at POS terminals at different merchant establishments.  Moreover, there was a third debit from the account of the complainant amounting to ₹28,949/- for which no message was received by the complainant from the Bank.  It was, therefore, the duty of the Bank to have looked into the matter to arrive at the truth of the same.
17.     A perusal of the literature explaining the features of the debit card in question and relied upon by the counsel for the Bank does say that the Bank bears no liability for the unauthorised use of the card and the responsibility for the same is fully that of the card holder.  However, in the said literature, it has been stated under the head terms and conditions as follows:-
"(d) Transactions : The transactions record generated by the ATM or POS will be binding on the Cardholder and it will be conclusive unless verified otherwise and corrected by the Bank.  The verified and corrected amount will be binding on the Cardholder."
18.     A perusal of the above provision indicates that the transaction record generated by the ATM or POS will be binding on the card holder and will be conclusive unless verified otherwise and corrected by the Bank.
19.     A plain reading of this provision is sufficient to establish that once the complaint was made citing specific incidents

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
will be conclusive unless verified otherwise and corrected by the Bank.
19.     A plain reading of this provision is sufficient to establish that once the complaint was made citing specific incidents of unauthorised withdrawal, it was the duty of the Bank to have carried out the necessary verification in the matter, rather than washing their hands off from the whole episode.  Evidently, there has been deficiency in service on the part of the Bank, vis-à-vis, the consumer/complainant.  It is held, therefore, that the consumer fora below have made a correct appreciation of the facts and circumstances on record which deciding the complaint in favour of the complainant.  Moreover, it is a settled legal proposition that the powers in the exercise of the revisional jurisdiction are used only if there is a jurisdictional error or material defect in the orders passed by the consumer fora below.  We are supported in this assertion by an order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in "
Rubi (Chandra) Dutta Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
[(2011) 11 SCC 269]".
20.     From the foregoing discussion, it is held that there is no merit in this revision petition and the same is ordered to be dismissed and the orders passed by the consumer fora below are affirmed.  The OP Bank is directed to make payment of the amount in question to the complainant within 4 weeks from today.  There shall be n

title: State Bank Of India vs Dr. J.C.S. Kataky on 3 May, 2017
text:
missed and the orders passed by the consumer fora below are affirmed.  The OP Bank is directed to make payment of the amount in question to the complainant within 4 weeks from today.  There shall be no order as to costs.

 Brief facts:
On 04.09.2023, the complainant, while returning from the Hon'ble High Court had to meet his Clerk Raj Kumar who at that time was in Sector 10, Chandigarh. The said Clerk requested the complainant to meet him in the market opposite Hotel Mountview. Accordingly, the complainant reached the area and while waiting to meet the Clerk, went to opposite party No.1 Coffee Shop to have Coffee. It is the grievance of the complainant that while placing the order at the counter of the said shop, the cashier asked him to give his mobile number in order to place the order. When enquired by the complainant, the cashier told that it was their policy to take the mobile number of consumers for marketing purposes and messaging and without giving the mobile number, he would not be able to issue the bill or take the order. Perforce, the complainant disclosed his name and mobile number and thereafter, the said cashier of opposite party No.1 took the order and issued bill and handed the complainant ordered cold coffee.
2]                It has been stated that immediately upon issue of the bill by the opposite parties, the complainant received another message on his mobile stating that the

title: Pankaj Chandgothia vs The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf on 28 December, 2023
text:
inant ordered cold coffee.
2]                It has been stated that immediately upon issue of the bill by the opposite parties, the complainant received another message on his mobile stating that the S Loyalty Wallet of the complainant has been successfully loaded with 19.15 loyalty points, which would expire on 03.11.2023 and the loyalty wallet balance was 19.15 - Petpooja. It has further been stated that such messages violate the consumer rights as they amount to "Dark Patterns" which are looked down upon by the Government of India and the government says that no person including any platform shall engage in any dark pattern.
3]                It is the case of the complainant that on the pretext of taking the order and issuing bill, the opposite parties obtain the personal details of consumers and retain it in their database for marketing and other purposes and the said data is prone to leakage or hacking which results in further harassment of the complainant by way of unwanted calls and unwanted solicitation. It has further been stated that many such companies even sell their data to desirous parties and therefore, profit at the expense of the consumers.
4]                It has further been stated that Government of India, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Department of Consumer Affairs has issued a notification dated 26.05.2023 to all the retail

as further been stated that Government of India, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Department of Consumer Affairs has issued a notification dated 26.05.2023 to all the retailers and  sellers association, which also include the opposite parties, to the effect that insisting on mobile number during the sale of a product as a pre-requisite mandatory condition, even when a consumer opts not to provide the same, is a violation of their rights and constitutes unfair trade practice under the Act. It has further been stated that under
Section 72-A

It has further been stated that by imposing a mandatory requirement to provide mobile number, consumers are often forced to share their personal information against their will, after which consumers are often flooded with marketing and promotional messages from retailers, which they did not even opt for at the time of purchasing the product. It has further been stated that restricting consumers to buy products or to return, exchange, and refund or resolving consumer grievance solely on the ground that the consumer has not shared her/his mobile number, constitutes unfair trade p

ing consumers to buy products or to return, exchange, and refund or resolving consumer grievance solely on the ground that the consumer has not shared her/his mobile number, constitutes unfair trade practice under the Act. It has further been stated that in the absence of breach of any other terms and conditions of sale, mere non-sharing of phone number cannot be a ground to deprive consumers from exercising their rights under the Act.

5]                Alleging above act of the opposite parties as wrongful sale of goods, deficiency in rendering service, unfair trade practice and unfair contract, which do not stand the scrutiny of law, legal validity or any sanctity, the complainant has filed the present complaint seeking directions to the opposite parties to cancel the bill, Annexure C-1 and refund the amount of ₹383/- charged therein; delete the data including his name and mobile number from its electronic data and not to use it any further for promotional or marketing purpose; pay ₹20,000/- as compensation for mental and physical harassment; pay ₹1,00,000/- as deterrent and punitive damages to be dedicated to the welfare of consumers and citizens; discontinue the unfair trade practice of taking personal details including mobile numbers of its customers on the pretext of issuing bills; pay ₹10,000/- as legal costs.

ns; discontinue the unfair trade practice of taking personal details including mobile numbers of its customers on the pretext of issuing bills; pay ₹10,000/- as legal costs.

It has further been stated that the opposite parties do not misuse the data provided by the customers and use the same only for the benefit of the customers. The opposite parties also placed on record voluminous dates i.e. list of mobile numbers against which the Loyalty Points are credited and redeemed from 1st September 2023 onwards.
