 immediately after the theft of the vehicle. However, this
 10 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

 condition should not bar settlement of genuine claims
 particularly when the delay in intimation or submission of
 documents is due to unavoidable circumstances. The decision
 of the insurer to reject the claim has to be based on valid
 grounds. Rejection of the claims on purely technical grounds in
 a mechanical manner will result in loss of confidence of policy-
 holders in the insurance industry. If the reason for delay in
 making a claim is satisfactorily explained, such a claim cannot
 be rejected on the ground of delay. It is also necessary to state
 here that it would not be fair and reasonable to reject genuine
 claims which had already been verified and found to be correct
 by the Investigator. The condition regarding the delay shall not
 be a shelter to repudiate the Insurance claims which have been
 otherwise proved to be genuine. It needs not emphasis that
 the
Consumer Protection Act
aims at providing better
 protection of the interest of consumers. It is a beneficial
 legislation that deserves liberal construction. This laudable
 object should not be forgotten while considering the claims
 made under the Act.
18. Reliance is also placed on
Amalendu Sahoo Vs. Orient

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
legislation that deserves liberal construction. This laudable
 object should not be forgotten while considering the claims
 made under the Act.
18. Reliance is also placed on
Amalendu Sahoo Vs. Oriental
Insurance Company
ltd,. (A.No.2703/2010 decided on 25.3.2010,
wherein the Hon'ble N.C. relied upon the judgment of S.C. & gave
guideline about setting of claim on non standard basis in following
cases.
Sr.No. Description. Percentage
 settlement.
 (i) Under declaration of licensed carrying Deduct 3 years'
 capacity. difference in premium
 11 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
non standard basis in following
cases.
Sr.No. Description. Percentage
 settlement.
 (i) Under declaration of licensed carrying Deduct 3 years'
 capacity. difference in premium
 11 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

 from the amount of
 claim or deduct 25 %
 of claim amount,
 whichever is higher.
 (ii) Overloading of vehicles beyond licensed Pay claims not
 carrying capacity. exceeding 75 % of
 admissible claim.
(iii) Any other breach of warranty/condition Pay upto 75% of
 of policy including limitation as to used. admissible claim.
19. With aforesaid submissions the complainant supported the
judgment of District Consumer Forum to the extent of deficiency in
service on the part of opponent in allowing the claim. But he has
come with appeal challenging the quantum awarded which is not in
accordance with estimation and compensation is not in the
proportionate with loss and mental agony.
20. On the other hand, the learned Adv. for appellant
Shri.Chapalgaonkar has submitted that, accident took place on
15.11.2015. The intimation is given on 2.1.2016 after 48 days of the
incident, with which there is breach of general condition No.1
mentioned in the policy which at page No. 67 of compilation in
appeal No. 206/2019. The policy is produced at page No. 62 to 69
along with terms and condition. Secondly, it is Private Car Package
Policy, the complainant has used the vehicle for hire and reward, in
vio

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
l No. 206/2019. The policy is produced at page No. 62 to 69
along with terms and condition. Secondly, it is Private Car Package
Policy, the complainant has used the vehicle for hire and reward, in
violation of the terms and condition pertaining to limitation to use
the vehicle. Therefore, the opponent gave letter to the complainant
dated. 14.4.2017 by giving opportunity to complainant to explain on
aforesaid counts. And the complainant failed to give any explanation
to the letter dated 14.4.2017. Therefore, the opponent Insurance
Company has issued another letter on 15.5.2017 and gave another
 12 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
the complainant failed to give any explanation
to the letter dated 14.4.2017. Therefore, the opponent Insurance
Company has issued another letter on 15.5.2017 and gave another
 12 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

opportunity to the complainant. Then the opponent Insurance
Company for breach of policy conditions and for non explanation to
the letters above issued by opponent to complainant, the opponent
Insurance Company rightly repudiated the claim.
21. The learned Adv. for opponent Insurance Company
placed
reliance upon
the judgment of State Consumer Dispute Redressal
Commission, Maharashtra State, in New India Assurance Company
Vs. Raghunath Dnyanu Khambe reported in 2019 STPL 3592MH (I
(2019) CPJ 139) wherein the Hon'ble State Commission relied upon
the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance
Company Ltd,. Vs. Mena Agrawal reported in III (2009) SLT 158/2009
(2) SCC 523) and held that, when the vehicle insured was used on hire
basis as taxi, against the terms and condition of policy, the Insurance
Company is not liable to pay compensation.
22. The Adv. for opponent placed Reliance upon another judgment
and Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Oriental Insurance Company Vs.
Parvesh Chander Chadha
in C.A.No. 6739 of 2010 decided on
17.8.2010 (S.C) wherein the Hon'ble Lordship of Apex Court observed
that-
"6. Admittedly, the Respondent had not informed the Appellant about
the alleged

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
der Chadha
in C.A.No. 6739 of 2010 decided on
17.8.2010 (S.C) wherein the Hon'ble Lordship of Apex Court observed
that-
"6. Admittedly, the Respondent had not informed the Appellant about
the alleged theft of the insured vehicle till he sent letter dated
22.5.1995 to the Branch Manager. In the complaint filed by him, the
Respondent did not give any explanation for this unusual delay in
informing the Appellant about the incident which gave rise to cause
for claiming compensation. Before the District Forum, the Respondent
did state that he had given copy of the first information report to
 13 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

text:
the incident which gave rise to cause
for claiming compensation. Before the District Forum, the Respondent
did state that he had given copy of the first information report to
 13 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

Rajender Singh Pawar through whom he had insured the car and
untraced report prepared by police on 19.9.1995 was given to the
said Shri Rajender Singh Pawar, but his explanation was worthless
because in terms of the policy, the Respondent was required to inform
the Appellant about the theft of the insured vehicle. It is difficult, if
not impossible, to fathom any reason why the Respondent, who is
said to have lodged First Information Report on 20.1.1995 about the
theft of car did not inform the insurance company about the incident.
In terms of the policy issued by the Appellant, the Respondent was
duty bound to inform it about the theft of the vehicle immediately
after the incident. On account of delayed intimation, the Appellant
was deprived of its legitimate right to get an inquiry conducted into
the alleged theft of vehicle and make an endeavour to recover the
same. Unfortunately, all the consumer foras omitted to consider this
grave lapse on the part of the Respondent and directed the Appellant
to settle his claim on non-standard basis. In our view, the Appellant
cannot be saddled with the liability to pay compensation to the
Respondent despite the fact that he had not compli

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
d the Appellant
to settle his claim on non-standard basis. In our view, the Appellant
cannot be saddled with the liability to pay compensation to the
Respondent despite the fact that he had not complied with the terms
of the policy."
23. The third reported case relied upon by the opponent Insurance
Company is
Puneet Kumar Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd
,. &
Anr. of National Commission in Revision Petition No. 308/2016 - of
Hon'ble National Commission wherein it is observed that, plying a
transport vehicle on a public place without the requisite permit
cannot be said merely to be breach of the warranty/condition of the
policy including limitation as to its use. Plying the vehicle on a public
place being prohibited and being punishable as an offence under the
 14 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
of the warranty/condition of the
policy including limitation as to its use. Plying the vehicle on a public
place being prohibited and being punishable as an offence under the
 14 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

provision of the M.V.Act, such a breach in our view would be of a
fundamental nature and therefore will not fall within the purview of
the breach which in terms of the above referred guidelines can be
settled on non-standard basis.
In
Amalendu Sahoo
(Supra), the
private vehicle was found to be used for hire and such a breach was
not considered to be a fundamental breach of the terms and
conditions of the policy. The vehicle if registered for private use can
be brought on the road though it cannot be used for hire, whereas a
transport vehicle cannot at all be brought on the road without
obtaining the requisite permit in terms of the
section 66
of the
M.V.Act.
Therefore, the breach committed in this case cannot be
treated at par with the breach in
Amalendu Sahoo
(Supra).
24 We agree with the ratio of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble
National Commission in respect of use of vehicle by committing the
breach of condition as to limitation, wherein the claim may be
considered on non standard basis.
25. In the case in hand, it is important to note that, policy is
admittedly private car policy wherein it is one of the condition that,
the policy covers use of vehicle for any purpose other th

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
basis.
25. In the case in hand, it is important to note that, policy is
admittedly private car policy wherein it is one of the condition that,
the policy covers use of vehicle for any purpose other than hire or
reward or carrage of goods and in the schedule of policy it is made
clear that in case of use of private vehicle for hire and reward the
company shall not be liable to pay compensation. Here the vehicle is
used for hire and reward. In the statement of the injured Maya
Yogesh Bhalerao it is specifically mentioned that the driver was
collecting the passenger on hire and reward basis. She herself along
with her son Sanvidhan were travelling by paying fair with another
 15 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
cifically mentioned that the driver was
collecting the passenger on hire and reward basis. She herself along
with her son Sanvidhan were travelling by paying fair with another
 15 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

passenger was Vinod Pardeshi who was injured and she learned that
he was expired. Said statement of witness is at page No. 73 of
appeal compilation. Copy of FIR is at page No. 29to30 which is
lodged by ASI Suresh Premchandu Jeere on next day on 10.5.2015 at
about 7.00 p.m. as the driver of vehicle ran away without giving
intimation to police station. In the said FIR also the name of
deceased Vinod Pardeshi and injured Maya Yogesh Bhalerao and her
son Sanvidhan is mentioned, who were travelling in the vehicle.
There is not a single statement given by complainant or his driver to
police that the friend of complainant were occupants. On the
contrary , the complainant for the first time is coming with the case
that the deceased was his friend and Maya Yogesh Bhalerao is the
wife and Sanvidhan is a son of his friend. These conducts of owner
and driver clearly shows that persons travelling were simply
passengers as submitted by passenger Maya Bhalerao, in her
statement before the police.
26. There is not a single document showing that the owner or
driver either came forward to give intimation to police or to
Insurance Company. Even before repudiating the claim the
opportunity was given

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
6. There is not a single document showing that the owner or
driver either came forward to give intimation to police or to
Insurance Company. Even before repudiating the claim the
opportunity was given to owner to submit explanation as to breach
of condition, i.e. carrying vehicle beyond limitation or breach of
policy condition and in causing delay of 48 days in submitting
intimation to Insurance company. When the opponent has
repudiated the claim on aforesaid grounds, then at least at the time
of filing the consumer complaint the complainant had opportunity to
explain these two conditions. The complainant remained silent to
state that as to why there is such a huge delay. On the bare
 16 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
umer complaint the complainant had opportunity to
explain these two conditions. The complainant remained silent to
state that as to why there is such a huge delay. On the bare
 16 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

statement of complaint that he gave intimation to police and the
intimation to service centre, it cannot be inferred that there was
intimation to Insurance Company. There is also no such document
showing that immediate instruction was given to police by the
complainant. Thus, there is no explanation for causing 48 days delay
in giving intimation to opponent Insurance Company. The
complainant has also not filed affidavit of insured Maya or her son
Sanvidhan if all they were wife and son of his friend.
27. If we go through the policy condition which is at page No.67,
states that, policy and its schedule, shall read together. The condition
No.1 at page No.67 as to condition, states that,-
"Notice shall be given in writing to the company immediately
upon the occurrence of any accidental loss or damage in the event of
any claim and thereafter the insured shall give all such information
and assistance as the company shall require."
28. It reveals from repudiation letter dated 29.05.20217 that,
besides the submission of claim there was no prior intimation of
incident to opponent Insurance Company. The repair estimation
issued by Diwekar garage to opponent in the month of January 2016,
(

hat,
besides the submission of claim there was no prior intimation of
incident to opponent Insurance Company. The repair estimation
issued by Diwekar garage to opponent in the month of January 2016,
(at page No.36to41) bears the claim number issued by opponent.
The said number is also mentioned in surveyor's report at page No.76
to 81 which show that, there was no prior intimation. The
complainant has also filed same documents, with his appeal
compilation of FA. No.290/2019, at page No. 28 to 80. Thus, even
on giving reasonable opportunity to explain the breach of policy
 17 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

text:
as also filed same documents, with his appeal
compilation of FA. No.290/2019, at page No. 28 to 80. Thus, even
on giving reasonable opportunity to explain the breach of policy
 17 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

conditions, the complainant failed to explain the same. There is also
no whisper that at any point of time the complainant made any
correspondence besides submission of claim to opponent.
On the
contrary the complainant or his driver did not visit police station
after accident or issued intimation to opponent Insurance company
as required immediately after the incident, as to loss or damage
sustained to vehicle, in writing. This delay of 48 days is inordinate
and not at all explained satisfactorily as expected as per conditions
and also observed by the judgment of Apex Court in Oriental
Insurance Com. Ltd,. Vs. Parvesh Chandar Chadda, Stated Supra and
even as observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Omprakash Vs.
Reliance General Insurance, Stated Supra
. It is expected to explain
the delay satisfactorily. In the case in hand it is not at all explained.
29. Secondly, the another breach as to driving the vehicle for hire
or reward beyond the condition as to use of vehicle beyond
limitation is not only breach but using the vehicle without permit in
contravention of the provision of
Motor Vehicle Act
. Perhaps even if
it is accepted in view of
Amlendu
's case that the claim for breach o

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
n is not only breach but using the vehicle without permit in
contravention of the provision of
Motor Vehicle Act
. Perhaps even if
it is accepted in view of
Amlendu
's case that the claim for breach of
such condition can be settled on non standard basis, still in the case
in hand there is breach of condition as to intimation of accident
immediately to the Insurance Company in writing, and it is inordinate
delay of 48 days it is not explained as mentioned above.
30. The Hon'ble District Consumer Forum though observed that
there is breach of policy condition and further pleased to allow the
complaint partly on non standard basis, by ignoring fact that the case
is relied upon by the opponent states that delay in lodging report if
 18 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

title: Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
text:
n and further pleased to allow the
complaint partly on non standard basis, by ignoring fact that the case
is relied upon by the opponent states that delay in lodging report if
 18 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

not explained properly or satisfactorily the Insurance Company
cannot be held liable to pay compensation to the insured. At the cost
of repetition we would like to mention that, in this case the District
Consumer Forum has totally ignored that in spite of giving
opportunity by opponent Insurance Company to the complainant to
explain the delay & breach of policy condition, there is no
explanation and also no whisper about the same. Therefore, in
aforesaid distinguishing circumstances, it cannot be said that the
claim is repudiated only on technical ground.
31. Moreover, immediate conduct on the part of driver, fleeing
away from the spot without intimation of accident and further on the
part of owner not giving information immediately in writing to the
insurance company as expected in policy condition, not make
entitled the complainant the compensation. Hence, the judgment
of District Consumer Forum requires interference and needs to be set
aside. There is also no merits in appeal filed by complainant for
enhanced compensation as claimed in the complaint. We therefore,
answer the points accordingly and pass following order.

          This is an appeal filed by the opposite parties  aggrieved by the orders   of District Consumer Forum-III, Hyderabad   dated 13.09.2013 made in CC No.39 of 2011   wherein it  allowed the complaint directing the opposite parties no.1 and 2 to refund a sum of Rs.1,91,000/- with interest 9% p.a. from 17.06.2010 till realization together with compensation of Rs.20,000/- and costs of Rs.2,000/-.
2.                 For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as arrayed in the complaint.
3.                 The case of the complainant, in brief,  is that  complainant is an Account holder of the Opposite Party No.2 having a savings Account No.004801522315 since 2004.    On 17.06.2010 an amount of Rs.1,91,000/- was debited from the Complainant savings account without his authorization and therefore, he lodged a complaint on 18.06.2010  with the opposite partyno.2.   On   verification, the Complainant came to know that series of transactions were done in a fraudulent manner and had learnt that in those series of transactions, two transactions in particular were withheld on the premise that transactions were dealt with fake accounts. The Complainant was informed by the

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text: er and had learnt that in those series of transactions, two transactions in particular were withheld on the premise that transactions were dealt with fake accounts. The Complainant was informed by the Opposite Party No.2 that the said transactions were done fraudulently by hacking his savings account by unknown persons. However, the opposite party No.2 assured the complainant that it had started verification/investigation in the matter  and further information can be provided after the completion of the verification. When the Complainant visited the Opposite Party No.2 Bank to enquire about the progress of his complaint, the Branch Manager of Opposite Party No.2 informed the Complainant that since it was an internal investigation, the details will not reflect in the customer care system.   The opposite parties have entangled the Complainant into procedural trap in order to absolve the opposite parties from its negligent actions and deficient conduct.   Thereafter, the complainant came to know that   the cybercrime cell upon investigation has unearthed a massive fraud whereat 3 fraudsters have been traced and after locating and identifying them,  the police at Delhi arrested the suspects and brought them to Hyderabad. During the interrogation the suspects have confessed that they got the information from the Bank employees Mumbai and Delhi of ICICI Banks. On 12.07.2010, the oppo

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
pects and brought them to Hyderabad. During the interrogation the suspects have confessed that they got the information from the Bank employees Mumbai and Delhi of ICICI Banks. On 12.07.2010, the opposite parties addressed an email requesting the Complainant to furnish the details and accordingly   on 15.07.2010, the required information was sent to them but despite that the case was closed for want of information. Thereafter, on 07.09.2010, the opposite parties approached the Complainant after a gap of 2 months, offered the Complainant to execute a draft deed of release   However, the Complainant refused to accept the said proposal. The opposite parties were deficienct in not protecting the interest of the complainant and that some of the employees of opposite parties are in active collusion with the fraudsters caused wrongful loss to the complainant.  Hence, the complaint praying to direct the opposite parties to pay Rs.1,91,000/- with interest @ 15% p.a. together with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- and costs of Rs.40,000/-.
4.                 The opposite parties resisted the case contending that the complainant is not a consumer within the meaning of
CP Act
.  The complainant having knowledge that the opposite parties are not liable for the negligent acts of the complainant in sharing the personal information of his credit/debit card with third parties which resulted for the

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
ving knowledge that the opposite parties are not liable for the negligent acts of the complainant in sharing the personal information of his credit/debit card with third parties which resulted for the alleged transactions and now trying to blame and extract money from the opposite parties.     The complainant having availed the internet banking facility from the opposite parties by agreeing to the terms and conditions as per the account opening form as such the complaint filed is bad in law and is liable to be rejected as the dispute against opposite parties does not fall within the purview of
C.P. Act
.    The opposite party bank upon hearing from the complainant of the alleged fraudulent transactions, began a prompt internal verification of the transactions and trace the transactions to different internet account and also marked a freeze on the said accounts.  It is observed that all these amount transfers were made on 17.06.2010.  As per the Bank's process, since no FIR was lodged at that time with regard to the sums claimed and the opposite party bank had no way of ascertaining the fraud.  The opposite party bank sought a letter of indemnity from the complainant as is part of its regular procedure but the complainant refused to sign the indemnity letter for the opposite party bank to release the said sum.  The complainant had initially complained to the call center of the o

ts regular procedure but the complainant refused to sign the indemnity letter for the opposite party bank to release the said sum.  The complainant had initially complained to the call center of the opposite party bank and basing on such complaint of the complainant immediately all the five accounts were got freeze.  However, by the time the complaint was made and due action taken, certain amounts were already withdrawn from the said accounts with the exception of two amounts.
5.                The opposite party Bank wanted to release Rs.21,000/- first to the customer since it was an unencumbered account and the funds were readily available to be refunded and for the same the opposite party had asked the complainant to sign the deed of release, however, he refused to sign the deed of release even when it was repeatedly explained to him that as per the Bank's mandate the said deed of release was required to be signed by a customer before any action  could be taken.     It is the prime responsibility of any account holder to protect confidentiality of their PIN Numbers and Pass words, so that it is not misused by third parties. There is absolutely no deficiency of service by the opposite parties and as such the complaint is liable to be dismissed.

osite parties and as such the complaint is liable to be dismissed.
6.                In proof of his case, he  filed his evidence affidavit and got marked Ex.A1 to A7. The Manager (Legal)   of the opposite parties  filed his Evidence Affidavit and got marked   Exs.B1 to B4.
7.                The District Forum after considering the material available on record, allowed  the complaint bearing CC No.39 of 2011 by orders dated 13.09.2013  as stated in paragraph No.1, supra.
8.                 Aggrieved by the said decision, the opposite party no.1  preferred the appeal contending that the Dist. Forum did not appreciate the facts in correct perspective.   The District Forum failed to appreciate that the disputed transactions were done online using the confidential details of the customer and that the transactions could not have been possible unless the customer has divulged/compromised the confidential details of its accounts like user ID and password.   The customer who has failed in its duty to secure the confidential details of its account and customer alone can be held responsible for any loss suffered due to his negligence and his failure to protect the confidential details of its account.  The District Forum erred in not appreciating the multiple steps and safety measures taken by the Bank to facilitate an online transaction such as the User ID and password, registration of b

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
account.  The District Forum erred in not appreciating the multiple steps and safety measures taken by the Bank to facilitate an online transaction such as the User ID and password, registration of beneficiary and a Unique Registration Number sent to the customer's mobile number by SMS but instead erroneously ascribed liability on the Bank for not sending an SMS for each transaction and failed to appreciate that the SMS alerts were always sent as a value added service free of cost, post completion banking transactions, when neither the bank nor the customer can stop such transactions especially since such transactions were done through internet banking mode.    Hence, the opposite parties prayed to allow the appeal by setting aside the order of the District Forum and dismiss the complaint.
9.                  Ms Usha Rani, Advocate represents counsel on record for appellant.  Counsel for respondent present.  Heard.  Written arguments of both parties are filed.
10.                         The point that arises for consideration is whether the impugned orders as passed by the District Forum suffer from any error or irregularity or whether they are liable to be set aside, modified or interfered with, in any manner?  To what relief?
11.                         It is not in dispute that the complainant was having savings account with the opposite party no.2 bank and that on his com

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
interfered with, in any manner?  To what relief?
11.                         It is not in dispute that the complainant was having savings account with the opposite party no.2 bank and that on his complaint with regard to misuse of the said account by some unknown persons in making online transactions, the Cyber Crime Cell arrested a gang which allegedly defrauded lakhs of rupees having stolen data of number of customers of the ICICI Bank including the complainant.            It is the contention of the opposite parties that the  complainant himself was negligent in protecting confidential information of his PIN number and Password and   as such they were not responsible for his monetary loss.      The opposite parties also contended that the complainant not a consumer and that the dispute against opposite parties does not fall within the purview of the C.P.Act.
12.               We do not agree with the contention of the opposite parties for the reasons that the jurisdiction of the Consumer Fora exists to impart speedy and expeditious cheaper justice to protect the Consumers.
Section 3
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 does provide efficacious, additional and supplementary remedy. Complaint cannot be thrown away merely because some complicated questions may arise. Consumer Fora do have ample powers to deal with the consumer disputes to solve them and protect the consumers.

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
dy. Complaint cannot be thrown away merely because some complicated questions may arise. Consumer Fora do have ample powers to deal with the consumer disputes to solve them and protect the consumers.
13.                        There is increase in the grievances of the customers in relation to unauthorized banking transactions in respect of electronic online remote payment and cashless transactions e.g. internet banking, mobile banking, card not present (CNP) transactions, pre-paid payment instruments resulting in debits from their Bank accounts and customers   need to be protected in unauthorized electronic banking transactions. Banks need to assure safety to the customers making them feel safe and secure in respect of the electronic banking transactions. Banks are duty bound to take appropriate steps to assess the risk and provide for robust mechanism to prevent and detect fraud and to provide for liability arising out of misappropriation or fraud. Banks must ask their customers to compulsorily register for the E-mail alerts, SMS alerts, system must be such so that customers can immediately inform by reply to the Bank about any illegal or unauthorized remote or internet transaction soon after occurrence thereof. Customer's liability must be zero when he informs the Bank at the earliest possible opportunity. Burden of proof to prove customer's liability is upon the Bank in all

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
on soon after occurrence thereof. Customer's liability must be zero when he informs the Bank at the earliest possible opportunity. Burden of proof to prove customer's liability is upon the Bank in all cases of the online internet transactions.  Bank must show that it had taken immediate steps to prevent and/or detect fraud. Banks transacting inter se do have means to trace the culprits on the basis of Know Your Customer (KYC) details in the Bank accounts and recover the sums wrongly transferred by electronic transfers. The basic principle is one must be made to pay for negligence when it has caused deficiency in service and loss to consumer actionable under the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
.   It is argued that respondent/complainant himself is negligent but this submissions by the respondents is not acceptable because in cases of internet transfers unless alerted prior to or at the time of internet transfers we cannot impute any blame to the consumer, who was in darkness as to withdrawals by unknown persons by mode of internet transfers.
14.              In view of this, we hold in the facts and circumstances of the case that the forum was   justified in not holding that Bank is liable to refund the amount which was  wrongly transferred to other accounts.    Internet Banking is a facility made available from the Bank on payment of service charges. The Bank concerned is duty b

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
liable to refund the amount which was  wrongly transferred to other accounts.    Internet Banking is a facility made available from the Bank on payment of service charges. The Bank concerned is duty bound to protect its consumer's interest by alerting the consumer of services by E-mails and SMS communications when electronic transactions exceeding Rs.50,000/- or beyond are done on behalf of the consumer account holder. We refer Circular of Reserve Bank of India bearing DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18 dated 06/07/2017 regarding limiting liability of customers in unauthorised electronic banking transaction. The shift in the policy of the Reserve Bank of India fixing zero liability upon the Bank customer in case of sending funds by internet transfers through other Banks, that too without alerting the Customer by E-mails or SMS alerts must be adhered to by the nationalized and recognized Banks doing banking business in India. The burden to disown liability is heavy on the opposite party Bank and it had not discharged satisfactorily in the facts and circumstances of the case. The Bank sending money by internet transfers when informed promptly by the consumer in such case is expected to lodge the complaint immediately with the police and follow the money went in to wrong hands by appropriate criminal proceedings by resorting to
Section 357
of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
to lodge the complaint immediately with the police and follow the money went in to wrong hands by appropriate criminal proceedings by resorting to
Section 357
of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the meantime the Bank concerned shall make good the loss caused to the Consumer by negligence on the part of the Bank or its officials. The Non-deposit and non-restoration of the money misused and/or misappropriated or wrongly sent by internet transfers, at the foot of the Savings Bank account of the Complainant   amounted to deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties Bank, actionable by the consumer under the
Consumer Protection Act,1986
.
15.               The Honble Supreme Court in State of Gujarath vs Shantilal Mangaldas AIR 1969 SC 634. Held the compensation to mean..  "In ordinary parlance the expression compensation means anything given to make things equivalent; a thing given to or to make amends for loss recompense, remuneration or pay, it need not therefore necessarily in terms of money. The phraseology of the Constitutional provision also indicates that compensation need not necessarily be in terms of money because it expressly provides that the law may specify the principles on which, and the manner in which , compensation is to be determined and given . If it were to be in terms of money along, the expression paid would have been more appropriate".
16.

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
the principles on which, and the manner in which , compensation is to be determined and given . If it were to be in terms of money along, the expression paid would have been more appropriate".
16.                        The Supreme Court held that the compensation to be awarded is to be fair and reasonable.
In
Charan Singh vs Healing Touch Hospital and others
2000SAR(Civil) 935 the Apex Court stressed the need of balancing between the compensation awarded recompensing the consumer  and the change it brings in the attitude of the service provider. The Court held While quantifying damages , consumer forums are required to make an attempt to serve ends of justice so that compensation is awarded, in an established case, which not only serves the purpose of recompensing the individual, but which also at the same time aims to bring about a qualitative change in the attitude of the service provider. Indeed calculation of damages depends on the facts and circumstances of each case. No hard and fast rule can be laid down for universal application. While awarding compensation, a Consumer Forum has to take into account all relevant factors and assess compensation on the basis of accepted legal principles, on moderation. It is for the Consumer Forum to grant compensation to the extent it finds it reasonable, fair and proper in the facts and circumstances of a given case according to establ

title: 1. Icici Bank Limited, Rep. By Its ... vs Mr. Kateka Sudhakar, S/O. K.J. Lazarus, ... on 5 March, 2018
text:
l principles, on moderation. It is for the Consumer Forum to grant compensation to the extent it finds it reasonable, fair and proper in the facts and circumstances of a given case according to established judicial standards where the claimant is able to establish his charge.
17.                         For the foregoing reasons we are inclined to modify the order of the District Forum by setting aside the interest part  and maintain the rest of the order.
In the result the appeal is allowed modifying the order of the District Forum. The opposite parties are directed to pay Rs.1,91,000/- to the respondent/complainant. Rest of the order is confirmed. There shall be no order as to costs.

In case of non-compliance then Clause No. 5.5 is relevant, which

"5.5 Subject to Clause 5.1 and 5.2 above and further the

However, as per the agreement, within the stipulated period, the

delivered within the time then the complainants have a right to ask

for the refund. A reference can be made to the judgment of the

Hon'ble National Commission reported as II (2014) CPJ 131

"PUDA versus Kanwalpreet Singh" that in case there is delay in

handing over the possession, it amounts to deficiency in service

and refund order can be passed. A reference has also been made

to I (2017) CPJ 513 (NC) "Neha Suri versus Unitech Reliable

Project Pvt. Ltd." In that case, the possession of the flat was not

given as agreed. It amounts to deficiency in service. Amount

deposited alongwith interest was ordered to be refunded. Similar
Consumer Complaint No. 373 of 2017 12

Developers Pvt. Ltd.". This Commission has already held in

Consumer Complaint No. 164 of 2016 "Harmit Singh Arora versus

against the same opposite party that in case possession of the

apartment has not been given as agreed then it amounts to

deficiency in service and that the complainants are not bound to

on 2.2.2017

against the same opposite party that in case possession of the

apartment has not been given as agreed then it amounts to

deficiency in service and that the complainants are not bound to

pay further payments when the project is not coming at the site and

refund alongwith interest order was ordered.
7. After taking the approximate full amount, Ops failed to

construct and deliver the possession of the apartment to the

complainants, therefore, Ops are deficient in service. Therefore,

the complaint is liable to be allowed.
8. It has been further argued by the counsel for the Ops

that according to Clause No. 5.5, in case there is delay in delivery

of the possession then the Ops are liable to pay the penalty as per

Clause 5.5 i.e. @ Rs. 5/- per sq. ft. per month of super area from

the date, the possession was to be delivered upto the date of

payment. Whereas it has been contended by the counsel for the

complainants that in case of late payment, the Ops are claiming

interest @ 18% then similar treatment be given to the

complainants. It is one sided agreement and in case of default on

the part of complainants, they paid 18% interest whereas Ops are

to pay just 3%. This question has been dealt in detail by the

Hon'ble National Commission in CC No. 427 of 2014 "Satish

title: Rajeshwari Sarin vs M/S Country Colonisers Pvt. Ltd. on 20 March, 2018

to pay just 3%. This question has been dealt in detail by the

Hon'ble National Commission in CC No. 427 of 2014 "Satish

Consumer Complaint No. 373 of 2017 13
8.6.2015 wherein the Hon'ble National Commission observed as

under:-
"However, a term of a contract, in my view will not be final and

 binding if it is shown that the consent to the said term was not

 account of the person giving consent being left with no other

 choice or if the said term amounts to an unfair trade practice. It

 was submitted by the learned counsel for the complainants that

 the term providing for payment of a nominal compensation such

 as Rs.5/- per square foot of the super area having become the

 order of the day in the contracts designed by big builders, a

 person seeking to buy an apartment is left with no option but to

 sign on the dotted lines since the rejection of such term by him

 would mean cancellation of the allotment. He further submitted

 that a person seeking to acquire a built up flat instead of

 purchasing a plot and then raising construction on it, therefore, is

 not in a position to protest resist the inclusion of such a term in the

a person seeking to acquire a built up flat instead of

 builder, particularly if he is a big builder such as Unitech Ltd. He

 also submitted that the format of the Buyer's Agreement is never

 shown to the purchasers at the time of booking the apartment and

 if he refuses to sign the Buyer's Agreement on the format provided

 by the builder, not only will he lose the booking, even the booking

 or does not want to buy a plot and raise construction of his own,
Consumer Complaint No. 373 of 2017 14
has to necessarily go in for purchase of the built up flat. It is only

 natural and logical for him to look for an apartment in a project

 being developed by a big builder such as the opposite party in

 these complaints. Since the contracts of all the big builders

 contain a term for payment of a specified sum as compensation in

 the event of default on the part of the builder in handing over

 possession of the flat to the buyer and the flat compensation

text:
ers

 contain a term for payment of a specified sum as compensation in

 offered by all big builders is almost a nominal compensation being

 less than 25% of the estimated cost of construction per month, the

 flat buyer is left with no option but to sign the Buyer's Agreement

 in the format provided by the builder. No sensible person will

 volunteer to accept compensation constituting about 2-3% of his

 investment in case of delay on the part of the contractor, when he

 is made to pay 18% compound interest if there is delay on his part

 in making payment.
It can hardly be disputed that a term of this nature is wholly one

 sided, unfair and unreasonable. The builder charges compound

 interest @ 18% per annum in the event of the delay on the part of

 the buyer in making payment to him but seeks to pay less than 3%

 per annum of the capital investment, in case he does not honour

 his part of the contract by defaulting in giving timely possession of

 the flat to the buyer. Such a term in the Buyer's Agreement also

 encourages the builder to divert the funds collected by him for one

 project, to another project being undertaken by him. He thus, is

 able to finance a new project at the cost of the buyers of the

title: Rajeshwari Sarin vs M/S Country Colonisers Pvt. Ltd. on 20 March, 2018
text:
encourages the builder to divert the funds collected by him for one

 project, to another project being undertaken by him. He thus, is

 able to finance a new project at the cost of the buyers of the

 existing project and that too at a very low cost of finance. If the

 builder is to take loan from Banks or Financial Institutions, it will
Consumer Complaint No. 373 of 2017 15
have to pay the interest which the Banks and Financial Institutions

 charge on term loan or cash credit facilities etc. The interest

 being charged by the Banks and Financial Institutions for financing

 projects of the builders is many times more than the nominal

 compensation which the builder would pay to the flat buyers in the

 form of flat compensation. In fact, the opposite party has not even

 claimed that the entire amount recovered by it from the flat buyers

Section 2(r)
of the Consumer

 Protection Act, 1986 since it adopts unfair methods or practice for

Section 2(r) (1)
of the Act that would be immaterial considering

r

 the purpose of selling the product of the builder. Though, such a

of the Act that would be immaterial considering

 that the unfair trades, methods and practices enumerated in

written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
y the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey and rights of the
passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and
these conditions constitute a valid binding contract between
parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
16. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
ent
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

Tickets were booked on 17.05.2016 through travel agent Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 in the main complaint.
17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the
General Insurance Company engaged in the business of general
insurance including Air Travel Insurance in collaboration with
Respondent No.3/Opposite Party No.3.
18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant requested the Opposite Parties to arrange
alternate arrangements as they were on their way to Hyderabad
and the schedule was booked in advance for Darshan at Tirupathi
and accommodation at hotels in various places of pilgrimage. Due
to the sudden cancellation of the flight, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant incurred a heavy loss and suffered great
7
hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight ticke

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
light is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
b

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
oking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
pposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
iled are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.
26. For the reasons stated herein above and after giving
thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
R

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Smt Gopu Rajamani on 7 December, 2023
text:
ugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
Respondent No.1/Complainant a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards
compensation. Time for compliance is six weeks, failing which the
amount of Rs.10,000/- shall carry interest @ 8% p.a. till
realization. The parties to bear their own costs.
Sd/- Sd/-
 I/C PRESIDENT MEMBER-J

 This appeal, filed under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act

 1986 (hereinafter called "the Act" for short) is directed against order dated

 13/12/2019 passed by District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,

 Janjgir-Champa (C.G.) (hereinafter referred to as "District Forum" for

 short), in Complaint Case No.CC/11/2019, whereby the complaint filed

 by the respondent herein alleging deficiency in service against the

 appellants herein in repudiating her insurance claim was partly allowed

 and the appellants were directed to pay within a month the sum assured

 of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lacs) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of
Dismissed Page 1 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
compliant i.e. 30.01.2019, compensation for mental agony Rs.10,000/- (Ten

 Thousand) and cost of litigation Rs.2,000/- (Two Thousand). Feeling

 aggrieved, the opposite party insurance company has preferred this

 appeal.
2. In nutshell the facts of the case are that indisputably the husband of

 the complainant Late Rajababu obtained a life insurance policy from the

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
party insurance company has preferred this

 appeal.
2. In nutshell the facts of the case are that indisputably the husband of

 the complainant Late Rajababu obtained a life insurance policy from the

 appellant/ opposite party on 14.03.2015 for sum assured of Rs.5,00,000/-

 (Five Lacs). During subsistence of the policy on 07.01.2017 the insured

 husband of the respondent / complainant died. As per case of the

 respondent/ complainant she preferred claim before the appellant /

 insurance company in the month of April 2017, which was repudiated.

 Legal notice was also sent but the same was not replied nor the amount of

 insurance claim was paid hence alleging deficiency in service on the part

 of the appellant/ opposite party insurance company, complaint was filed

 seeking direction for payment of sum assured of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lacs),

 compensation for mental agony Rs.1,00,000/- (One Lac) along with cost of

 litigation and any other relief.
3. The appellant / opposite party insurance company filed its written

 version before the District Forum mainly to the effect that the life assured

 was chronic alcoholic and suffering from ascites with cirrhosis of liver

 disease, he was taking treatment for the same. He was first diagnosed for

 ascites and positive cirrhosis of liver on 03.10.2011, which was prior to the

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
ffering from ascites with cirrhosis of liver

 disease, he was taking treatment for the same. He was first diagnosed for

 ascites and positive cirrhosis of liver on 03.10.2011, which was prior to the

 issuance of insurance policy but this material information was suppressed

 at the time of filling proposal form for insurance which amounts to breach

 of principle of uberrima fides hence the insurance claim was repudiated, in

 which the insurance company has not committed any deficiency in

 service.
Dismissed Page 2 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
4. Learned District Forum on consideration of rival contentions of

 both parties partly allowed the complaint and directed the appellant/

 opposite party to pay the sum assured, compensation for mental agony

 and cost of litigation as aforesaid in paragraph No.1.
5. We have heard final arguments of both parties, perused the record

 and the written arguments submitted by learned counsel for the

 respondent / complainant.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party has filed certain

 document as per list along with an application under order 41 rule 27
of

 CPC
, marked as I.A. No.01/2023, which has already been allowed and

 documents are taken on record. Along with the application the documents

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
list along with an application under order 41 rule 27
of

 CPC
, marked as I.A. No.01/2023, which has already been allowed and

 documents are taken on record. Along with the application the documents

 filed are photocopy of Liver Function Test of the deceased dated

 31.10.2011, his treatment records of 2016 and 2017, letter of repudiation

 and investigation report, death certificate etc. whereas most of them were

 already filed before the District Forum and were considered.
7. Before us the appellant/ opposite party has reiterated the facts

 stated and grounds taken in the written version and argued that the

 learned District Forum has erred in appreciating the terms of the policy,

 information filled in the proposal form by the deceased life assured and

 his treatment records in the light of
Section 45
of the Insurance Act, 1938

 and has passed an erroneous order, hence this appeal needs to be allowed

 setting aside the impugned order. Whereas the learned counsel for the

 respondent/ complainant has supported the impugned order and argued

 that learned District Commission has rightly held the appellant/ opposite

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
he impugned order. Whereas the learned counsel for the

 respondent/ complainant has supported the impugned order and argued

 that learned District Commission has rightly held the appellant/ opposite

 party deficient in service in repudiating the genuine claim of the
Dismissed Page 3 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
respondent/ complainant and passed the impugned order which is just

 and proper and is not required to be interfered with.
8. We have considered the arguments advanced by both parties and

 gone through the record as well as the impugned order. In the impugned

 order we find that learned District Commission has arrived at the

 conclusion that the appellant/ opposite party has failed to establish that

 the insured had fraudulently concealed any information of his previous

 disease. It is true that in the proposal form the deceased Rajababu gave all

 the answers in negative but at the same time it is also true that he was not

 having knowledge of any pre-existing disease as appears from the

 available documents in the record of the District Forum as well as the

 documents filed before us. Only two documents i.e. Abdominal Ultra

 Sonography Report dated 03.10.2011, filed before the District Forum as

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
cuments in the record of the District Forum as well as the

 documents filed before us. Only two documents i.e. Abdominal Ultra

 Sonography Report dated 03.10.2011, filed before the District Forum as

 Exhibit OP-3 and photocopy of Liver Function Test of the deceased dated

 31.10.2011 are the documents of some diagnostic tests only which were

 done about four and half years prior the date of proposal for insurance.

 But what were the final findings, what treatment was given, which

 medicines were prescribed and for which period, to clarify these facts no

 document is brought on record. Whether the deceased Rajababu had to

 stay admitted in any hospital for treatment, nothing of that sort is proved

 by the appellant / opposite party by way of filing any cogent evidence.
9. The appellant / opposite party has also brought on record the

 Death Claim Investigation Report of Eagle Eye Consultant Private

 Limited, which is marked as Exhibit OP-4. In the said investigation report

 except mere description and opinion of the investigator nothing was

 discussed on the basis of which such opinion was given nor any evidence

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
marked as Exhibit OP-4. In the said investigation report

 except mere description and opinion of the investigator nothing was

 discussed on the basis of which such opinion was given nor any evidence

 was filed along with the said investigation report. In the said report
Dismissed Page 4 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
nowhere it is specifically stated that the deceased underwent any

 treatment and remained admitted in any hospital for a period more than a

 week or even for a single day. It is also not specifically mentioned that

 any medicine was continuously being taken by the life assured since 2011

 till the date of proposal, instead it is mentioned that local doctors failed to

 indentify the life assured by name. At the conclusion, only it is mentioned

 that as per information given life assured visited Mission Hospital

 Bilaspur few years back, where the doctors suggested him to stop

 alcoholism, but such document was not brought on record. At the

 appellate stage the insurance company itself has brought on record a

 document titled as „Physician‟s Statement - Death‟ as Annexure-5 in

 which in second page under „Prior Medical History‟ in reply to the

 question „Have you advised the deceased during the past 5 years, prior to

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
led as „Physician‟s Statement - Death‟ as Annexure-5 in

 which in second page under „Prior Medical History‟ in reply to the

 question „Have you advised the deceased during the past 5 years, prior to

 the final illness? the check box given against „No‟ was ticked, meaning

 thereby the Medical Officer of District Hospital Janjgir has certified that

 the life assured was never advised by him in the past 5 years. This

 document also goes against the case of the appellant/ insurance company.

 Thus, from the documents available on record of the District Forum as

 well as filed before us we are not convinced that the deceased was having

 any pre-existing disease or he was taking any medicine. In fact the

 insurance company has also failed to prove that the life assured was

 having knowledge of any pre-existing disease, which he suppressed in the

 proposal form for obtaining his life insurance.
10. So far as the another ground of repudiation of claim that the life

 assured was alcoholic is concerned, in the Discharge Ticket, Annexure-6,

 dated 27.12.2016 the name of illness is mentioned as chronic alcoholic liver

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
r ground of repudiation of claim that the life

 assured was alcoholic is concerned, in the Discharge Ticket, Annexure-6,

 dated 27.12.2016 the name of illness is mentioned as chronic alcoholic liver

 disease with ascites with severe anaemia. The policy in question was
Dismissed Page 5 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
obtained on 14.03.2015 and on 27.12.2016 i.e. after about one year and

 more than nine months, it was diagnosed that the life assured was chronic

 alcoholic. The approximate period reported by the life assured or any

 other source is not mentioned to determine as to for how long the life

 assured was alcoholic and this ambiguous situation is not sufficient to

 hold that the life assured was alcoholic prior to the date of proposal, hence

 this ground of repudiation of claim also has no leg to stand. Hence, with

 the foregoing discussion we are of the considered view that the appellant

 / opposite party insurance company has committed deficiency in service

 in repudiating the insurance claim of the life assured deceased husband of

 the complainant, as has rightly been held by the learned District Forum.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party insurance

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
the insurance claim of the life assured deceased husband of

 the complainant, as has rightly been held by the learned District Forum.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party insurance

 company has placed reliance upon judgements of Hon‟ble Apex Court in
P.C. Chacko & Anr. Vs. Chairman Life Insurance Corporation of India

 & Anr.
, (2008) 1 SCC 231;
Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors. Vs.

 Asha Goel (Smt.) & Anr.
, (2001) 2 SCC 160; United India Insurance Co.

 Ltd. Vs. MKJ Corporation in Appeal (Civil) No.6075-6076 of 1995 dated

 21.08.1996 and that of Hon‟ble National Commission in
Life Insurance

 Corporation of India Vs. Smt. Kusum Patro, II
(2012) CPJ 272 (NC) in

 support of his arguments that principle of utmost good faith was breached

 by the life assured hence the insurance company has right to repudiate the

 insurance claim, whereas learned counsel for the respondent /

 complainant has
placed reliance upon
judgement of Hon‟ble Apex Court

 in
Santwant Kaur Sandhu Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Civil

 Appeal No.2776
of 2002 dated 10.07.2009. But the case laws relied by

 learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party as well as the

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
Santwant Kaur Sandhu Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Civil

 Appeal No.2776
of 2002 dated 10.07.2009. But the case laws relied by

 learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party as well as the

 respondent / complainant are not relevant in the facts of the instant case
Dismissed Page 6 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
as the appellant insurance company has failed to prove its contention, as

 discussed hereinabove, that any material information regarding previous

 treatment, pre-existing disease or consumption of alcohol prior to the date

 of making proposal for life insurance was concealed deliberately by the

 life assured. Hence, we are of the considered view that the appellant /

 opposite party has committed deficiency in service in repudiating the

 insurance claim as has rightly been held by learned District Forum.
12. So far as the quantum of award is concerned learned District

 Forum has justifiably awarded the sum assured under the insurance

 policy in question and the amount of compensation for mental agony also

 appears justified in the facts and circumstances of the case and calls for no

 interference.
13. Therefore, in view of the above discussion, we do not find any error

 in the impugned order passed by learned District Forum, hence we affirm

title: B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
text:
mstances of the case and calls for no

 interference.
13. Therefore, in view of the above discussion, we do not find any error

 in the impugned order passed by learned District Forum, hence we affirm

 the same and dismiss this appeal being devoid of any merit. No order as

 to cost.
(Justice Gautam Chourdiya) (Pramod Kumar Varma)
 President Member
 /11/2023 /11/2023

 Pronounced On: 14th November 2023

The present appeal is directed
against the Order dated 03.08.2011 passed by the Ld. District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit II in Case No. CDF/Unit-II/CC No. 1385 OF 2009
in the matter of Sri Samar Roychoudhury
-vs- Hotel New Sea Hawk, Marine Drive, Swargadwar, Puri 752001 and others.
The
facts relating to the case are as follows:
The Appellant / Complainant, a senior
citizen of 69 years and a legal practitioner at Honble Calcutta High Court,
decided to go to Puri on a pleasure trip in October 2009 and accordingly booked
an accommodation in the Respondent /OP 1s Hotel at Puri for 7 days from 1st to 7th October 2009 with the help of OP No. 2
located at 48/A, Dr. Sundari Mohan Avenue, Kolkata 700014 on payment of Rs.
15,750/-. The accommodation being Room
No. 201 or Room No. 301 of the OPs hotel at Puri was offered by the Respondent
No. 2 and recommended to be suitable for four heads at the enquiry of the

The Appellant / Complainant visited

nd talked to the

udgment of the Ld. District Forum and case references as in IV (2010) CPJ

8.           We have heard the Counsel for the parties, and, have gone through the evidence and record of the cases, carefully.
9.           It is evident, on record, that vide provisional allotment letter dated 07.06.2011 (Annexure C-2), the complainant was allotted a Plot bearing no.111, in the residential project "IREO Hamlet" admeasuring 250.59 sq. yard, Sector 98, SAS Nagar, Mohali, the basic sale price whereof was Rs.25,000/- per sq. yard besides External Development Charges (EDC) @Rs.1,275.10 per sq. yardand IFMS charges @Rs.350/- per sq. yard. Admittedly, Plot Buyer's Agreement was executed
