4. Vide order dated 04.08.2026, Counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent
 submitted that the Respondent does not wish to file a reply or written arguments
 and would make oral submissions before this Commission.
5. We have perused the material available on record and heard the counsel appeared
 on behalf of the Appellant and the Respondent.
6. The main question for consideration before us is whether the District
 Commission erred in holding the Appellant deficient in service and in directing
 the Appellant to reimburse a sum of Rs.42,92

title: State Bank Of India vs Shakuntala Mehtani on 8 October, 2026
text:
6. The main question for consideration before us is whether the District
 Commission erred in holding the Appellant deficient in service and in directing
 the Appellant to reimburse a sum of Rs.42,92,450/- along with interest and
 compensation to the Respondent.
7. On perusal of the record, we find that the Respondent had specifically alleged
 that the registered mobile number linked with the bank accounts was changed
 without her knowledge or consent and that the internet banking facility, which
 was stated to be limited to "View Only", was subsequently utilized for carrying
 out the disputed transactions. The Appellant, on the other hand, has contended
 that the change in the registered mobile number and the activation of the
 transaction facility could not have been affected without the mandate of the
 account holder. However, despite taking such a specific stand, the Appellant has
 failed to place on record any document evidencing the mandate or written consent

the Appellant has

 of the Respondent for change of the registered mobile number or for alteration of
 the internet banking facility.
8. It is further evident from the record that the Status Report dated 08.05.2023
 submitted by the Investigating Officer before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi
 records that the registered mobile number of the Respondent was changed with
 the assistance of an official of the Appellant Bank. The said report further
 indicates that written consent of the customer was mandatory for such change,
 whereas no such request was available with the Bank. Thus, the material available
 on record raises a serious question regarding compliance with the prescribed
 banking procedure by the Appellant.
9. Furthermore, the submission of the Appellant that transaction alerts were duly
 received on the registered mobile number also does not satisfactorily explain the
 circumstances in which the registered mobile number itself came to be changed.
 Once the Appellant admitted that change of the registered mobile number
 required a mandate from the account holder, it was incumbent upon the Appellant
 to produce the relevant mandate or other contemporaneous record to establish
 that the cha

title: State Bank Of India vs Shakuntala Mehtani on 8 October, 2026
text:
he registered mobile number
 required a mandate from the account holder, it was incumbent upon the Appellant
 to produce the relevant mandate or other contemporaneous record to establish
 that the change was duly authorized. However, no such material has been filed
 by the Appellant before the District Commission as well as before this
 Commission.
10. Similarly, the Appellant has failed to produce any cogent material to establish
 when and in what manner the internet banking facility was upgraded from "View
 Only" to a transaction-enabled facility and pursuant to whose request or
 authorization such change was effected. Additionally, the Appellant being the
 custodian of the relevant banking records was in a position to produce such
 material and the failure to produce the same assumes significance when the
 disputed transactions were carried out thereafter and the Respondent has
 consistently denied having authorized such transactions.
DISMISSED PAGE 10 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI
11. The Appellant has also relied upon the RBI guidelines dated 06.07.2017 relating
 to customer protection in unauthorized electronic banking transactions. However,
 before seeking to attribute liability to the Respondent, the Appellant was required
 to establish the circumstances in which the disputed transactions were
 authenticated and to demo

title: State Bank Of India vs Shakuntala Mehtani on 8 October, 2026
text:
ctions. However,
 before seeking to attribute liability to the Respondent, the Appellant was required
 to establish the circumstances in which the disputed transactions were
 authenticated and to demonstrate compliance with the prescribed procedure. The
 Appellant has failed to establish that the Respondent had authorized the change
 of the registered mobile number or the alteration of the internet banking facility.
 The mere fact that the transactions were carried out through internet banking or
 that alerts were generated on the registered mobile number cannot, in the
 circumstances of the present case, establish authorization by the Respondent.
12. In view of the aforesaid discussion, it is clear that the Appellant Bank failed to
 establish that the change of the registered mobile number and the alteration of the
 internet banking facility were carried out pursuant to a valid mandate or consent
 of the Respondent. The Appellant also failed to produce the relevant banking
 records or the internal investigation report to substantiate its defense.
13. In these circumstances, we are of the considered view that the Appellant Bank
 was deficient in providing its banking services and failed to exercise the requisite
 care and diligence expected from it, which resulted in the unauthorized
 withdrawal of the amount from the accounts of the Respondent. The finding of
 deficiency in se

title: State Bank Of India vs Shakuntala Mehtani on 8 October, 2026

ailed to exercise the requisite
 care and diligence expected from it, which resulted in the unauthorized
 withdrawal of the amount from the accounts of the Respondent. The finding of
 deficiency in service recorded by the District Commission, therefore, does not
 call for any interference.
14. In view of the foregoing, we are in agreement with the reasons given by the
 District Commission and fail to find any cause or reason to reverse the findings
 of the District Commission. Consequently, we uphold the order dated
 11.08.2025 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum-II,

 Area (Behind Qutub Hotel), New Delhi -110016.

 ORDER
1. This Revision Petition has been filed under
Section 21(b)
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, hereinafter referred to as the "Act 1986‟, challenging the Order dated 17.09.2014 passed by the Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (for short "State Commission") in First Appeal No. A/629/08 arising out of the Order dated 09.06.2008 in C.C. No. 559 of 2007 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Nagpur, (for short, 'The District Forum") wherein the appeal was partly allowed.
2.       Briefly stated facts relevant for the disposal of this Petition, are that   the complainant Premnath purchased a Sonalika thresher machine from Nagpur Agriculture Equipment Engineers Private Ltd. (OP-1) for Rs. 1,02,500/-. The machine was manufactured by M/s Sonalika Agro Industries Corporation (OP-2). It was alleged that due to the throwing of dust from the feeding hole, the machine could not work efficiently. The thresher work could not be done. The complainant alleged that it was due to manufacturing defect in the machine. The OP-1 did not heed attention to the repeated complaints of the complainant. The complainant sustained a loss of his earnings at Rs

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
nt alleged that it was due to manufacturing defect in the machine. The OP-1 did not heed attention to the repeated complaints of the complainant. The complainant sustained a loss of his earnings at Rs. 3,000/- per day. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the OPs the complainant filed a complaint before the District Forum, Nagpur seeking compensation and replacement of the machine.
3.       The OPs filed their respective replies and raised preliminary objection that the complainant was not a consumer; he purchased the machine for business purpose. The OP- 1 filed a civil suit against the complainant for recovery of unpaid price of the machine in question. The complainant has not filed any expert report to show that there was defect in the machine. The OPs denied any manufacturing defects in the thresher machine.
4.       The District Forum, after taking into account the averments of  the parties held that the complainant was using the machine for business purpose, thus not consumer and there was no expert report to prove defective machine and dismissed the complaint.
5.       The Complainants filed Appeal under
Section 15
of the Act before the State Commission. The Appeal was partly allowed by the State Commission with observation in its paras 10 and 11 as below:
10.   The complaint shows that the appellant does not have any land in his name, so as to support his livel

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
was partly allowed by the State Commission with observation in its paras 10 and 11 as below:
10.   The complaint shows that the appellant does not have any land in his name, so as to support his livelihood. He has filed the 7/12, extract showing name of some other person. This shows that the purchase of machine was only to support his livelihood. It's a common experience that the persons from village always claim their profession to be farming though they may not have sufficient land which alone can sustain their livelihood so that any other extra profession can be termed as an extra commercial activity. Also the respondents have not produced any evidence to show that the appellant was dependent on another profession like farming and the thresher was purchased purely for commercial activity to earn profits. Thus, we see that the thresher was purchased only to earn livelihood by the appellant and can not be claimed to be an extra commercial activity so as to throw him out of the definition of Consumer. We feel the Forum erred in considering the livelihood activity to be the commercial activity.
11.  The major contention raised by the respondent in the absence of technical report regarding defect in the thresher machine. But as a consumer, the appellant has filed the complaint with his experience of working on the machine that , it was throwing dust through feeding hole thereby m

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
arding defect in the thresher machine. But as a consumer, the appellant has filed the complaint with his experience of working on the machine that , it was throwing dust through feeding hole thereby making difficult to feed the raw material for processing. The appellant's experienced difficulty in the functioning of the thresher. It then becomes the responsibility of the manufacturer and the seller i.e respondent Nos. 1&2 to give the reasons for the same and remove said defect. We do not find any cogent explanation, evidence or reason, to disbelieve the case of the appellant while operating it. Hence we find no necessity of any specific technical certification by any expert on behalf of appellant to show the defect in the machine. It also becomes incumbent, upon the respondent Nos. 1 & 2 to repair the machine and provide satisfactory service to the purchaser- consumer. The respondents do not appear to have done it, but the respondent No. 1 has resorted to file a counter case to add tangent, to the complaint of the consumer and deny him the service. We therefore hold that, the complaint of the appellant is justifiable and the respondents are bound to repair the machine or compensate it as fair trade practice.
(paras 10 and 11  from order of State Commission)

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
ld that, the complaint of the appellant is justifiable and the respondents are bound to repair the machine or compensate it as fair trade practice.
(paras 10 and 11  from order of State Commission)

 

The State Commission vide its order dated 17.09.2014 and directed the OPs to pay Rs. 1,02,500/- jointly and severally with interest @ 9 % from 01.10.2007 (date of purchase), OP-1 to pay to the complainant Rs. 5,000/- as compensation for mental and physical torture and Rs. 3,000/- towards the cost. It was further directed to the OPs to pay jointly and severally Rs. 100/- per day as loss of earning from the date of purchase till the date of payment.
6.       Being aggrieved the OPs filed the instant Revision Petition before this Commission.
7.       Heard the learned counsel for both the sides. The complainant was present during argument with his Counsel. Perused the material on record. Original record from the District Forum was requisitioned.
8.       Learned Counsel for the complainant argued that he noticed a defect within two months of purchase of the Sonalika thrasher machine. It was throwing dust from the same hole / entrance from which the food grains are pushed in the machine. Therefore it was impossible to stand near the inlet and impossible to push continuously the food grains material. The complainant immediately approached to the OP-1 for the said defect.   The OP-1 se

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
Therefore it was impossible to stand near the inlet and impossible to push continuously the food grains material. The complainant immediately approached to the OP-1 for the said defect.   The OP-1 sent a mechanic for seven times within two months, but the defect was not cured. Even the Complainant with the help of four villagers took the machine for repairs to the OP-1 workshop at Mandhal Tq. Kuhi but machine was not repaired. The complainant was facing hardship and suffered heavy financial loss from the date of purchase of the machine.
9.       The learned counsel for OPs submitted that the complainant suppressed the use of thrasher machine for commercial purpose. Thus, he was not a Consumer under the Act, 1986. The complaint being afflictive in nature and it was to be adjudicated only in a Civil Court. Before purchase of Sonalika thrasher machine the complainant was shown other machines. The complainant with his previous experience gone through the brochures, done comparative evaluation of all products, and decided to purchase the said thrasher. The Sonalika thrasher machine was ISI marked with certified International quality. It was installed by an expert having no manufacturing defect.
10.     The main thrust of the argument from the learned counsel for the petitioners that the onus to prove there was manufacturing defect in the thrasher was upon the complainant and the co

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
g defect.
10.     The main thrust of the argument from the learned counsel for the petitioners that the onus to prove there was manufacturing defect in the thrasher was upon the complainant and the complaint failed to produce any expert report.  I would like to place reliance upon the view taken by this Commission in RP No. 381 of 2012 decided on 17.10.2014/05.11.2014, "Ankur Seeds Private Limited & Anr. vs Moti Lal & Anr.", which has been stated as below:
"It is cardinal principle of law that ordinarily the burden of proving the fact rests on the party who asserts the affirmative issues and not on the party who denies it. Nevertheless, there is distinction between the phrase burden of proof and onus of proof. Explaining the said distinction, in
A. Raghavamma & Anr. Vs. A. Chenchamma & Anr.
AIR 1964 SC 136, a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that: there is essential distinction between burden of proof and onus of proof: burden of proof lies on the person who has to prove a fact and it never shifts, but the onus of proof shifts. Such a shifting of onus is a continuous process in the evaluation of evidence."
In my view therefore, to give effect to the Objective of the Act, its provisions have to be construed by resorting to the Doctrine of 'Purposive Construction'. Considered from that perspective, in my opinion, if a Complainant is able to create a high degree

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
the Act, its provisions have to be construed by resorting to the Doctrine of 'Purposive Construction'. Considered from that perspective, in my opinion, if a Complainant is able to create a high degree of probability of deficiency on the part of the Opposite Party, the onus would shift on to the Opposite Party (the defendant) to discharge the onus to prove his denial."
11.     The manufacturer as well as the supplier has a duty to exercise due care and caution in providing a product/ machine which is fit for the purpose for which it is sold. Throwing of dust from the feeding hole, in it shows that there is manufacturing defect in the machine and no need to prove it. Thus, the technical certification was not absolute in this case.
12.     I see, there is no such concept of goods suffering from manufacturing defect enshrined by the provision of the Act,1986, it only defines the word defect by way of
Section 2(1) (f)
which is to the following effect:
"Defect" means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied, or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods.
Thus in my view, it is a misconceived notion that any machine or vehicle for that purpose any goods can be ordered to be re

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods.
Thus in my view, it is a misconceived notion that any machine or vehicle for that purpose any goods can be ordered to be replaced or the cost can be ordered to be refunded only if they suffer from manufacturing defect.
13.     Generally, whenever a consumer goes for brand new goods like a thrasher in this case has minimum expectation that he would not encounter or face any inconvenience or hardship for few months or a year or within warranty.  In case if he had to take the machine  time and again to the workshop or call the technician time and again for removing one defect or the other, certainly he suffers immensely loss of time, loss of business, physical discomfort and emotional sufferings for purchasing such new machine by paying heavy amount.
14.      I find, the defect in thrasher in the instant case continues for months together and erupts time and again, thus no other inference can be drawn than that the machine suffers from manufacturing defect as defect which is not of manufacturing nature can be rectified or removed without its recurrence or without giving any further inconvenience to the consumer.
15.     My view is that the onus shifts to the manufacturer to show that the machine  does not suffer from manufacturing defect once complainant has proved and discharged the initial onus that the

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
er.
15.     My view is that the onus shifts to the manufacturer to show that the machine  does not suffer from manufacturing defect once complainant has proved and discharged the initial onus that the machine was defective on    showing that machine was attended for many occasion (seven times) for removing one defect.  It is pertinent to note that the thrasher machine was taken to OP's workshop with the help of four people is sufficient to draw the inference that the machine was a defective one.
16.     For such type of manufacturers and service providers the Hon'ble Supreme court has in
Ghaziabad Development Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
(2004) 5 Supreme Court Cases 65 come down heavily and called upon the Consumer Forum and Commissions established under the Act, 1986 to not only compensate the consumer as to the actual loss suffered by him but also to compensate him as to the mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering, physical discomfort, loss of business, loss of time by taking vehicle time and again to the workshop.
17.     Based on the discussion above and considering that the machine purchased in 2007 has already become very old and the complainant suffered loss and agony for more than one decade, I do not find any illegality, irregularity or jurisdictional error in the order passed by the State Commission. Accordingly, the said order is upheld and the Revision Petition,

title: Nagpur Agriculture Equipment ... vs Premnath on 2 July, 2020
text:
r more than one decade, I do not find any illegality, irregularity or jurisdictional error in the order passed by the State Commission. Accordingly, the said order is upheld and the Revision Petition, being without any merit, is dismissed, as there does not seem to be any sufficient ground to interfere in the exercise of the revisional jurisdiction by this Commission.
There shall be no order as to costs.
...................... DR. S.M. KANTIKAR PRESIDING MEMBER

6. On 31.05.2016, Opposite Party No.3 informed Opposite Party
No.2 about the cancellation of flight and the information was
passed on to the Complainant through Opposite Party No.1. The
Opposite Party No.3 refunded the cost of flight tickets which were
promptly paid to the Complainant.
7. The Complainant is demanding refund of hotel booking,
darshan tickets and cab services from Opposite Party No.2 which
were done subject to terms and conditions of respective operators,
therefore, this Opposite Party No.2 is in no way concerned with the
allegations and reliefs claimed by the Complainant. All the reliefs
and damages are directly attributable to the cancellation of the
flight, hence they seek dismissal of the complaint against this
Opposite Party with costs.
8. The Opposite Party No.3 was set exparte. The Opposite Party
No.4 is the Insurance Company and as per their written version
the flight was cancelled by the Airlines-Opposite Party No.3 and
the amount was refunded to the Complainant. As per their policy
terms and conditions Section VIII reads as follows:-
4
Section VIII: Trip Cancellation:
"Subject to all other terms and conditions, the company will
indemnify the insured subject to limits shown in schedule, for loss of
ticke

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
ion VIII reads as follows:-
4
Section VIII: Trip Cancellation:
"Subject to all other terms and conditions, the company will
indemnify the insured subject to limits shown in schedule, for loss of
ticket charges paid or contracted to be paid by the insured, which
are not recoverable from any other source."
9. In this case, Opposite Party No.3 has refunded the ticket
amount to the Complainant, therefore, the Complainant is not
liable for any compensation from this Opposite Party No.4 the
Insurance Company. The Complainant is taking a chance litigation
and in view of the facts and circumstances , they seek dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
10. Before the District Commission, the Complainant filed
Evidence Affidavit and got marked Ex.A1 to A6. The Opposite Party
No.4 filed evidence affidavit. Ex.B1 & B2 are marked on their
behalf.
11. The District Commission after hearing and considering the
material on record, allowed the complaint directing the Opposite
Party No.1 to 3 to pay each Rs.50,000/- in all with interest @ 12%
p.a. from the date of cancellation of flight ticket till realization. The
Opposite Party No.4 is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- with interest @
18% p.a. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposi

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
a. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 preferred this appeal with the
following grounds:
 The District Forum grossly erred in holding that alternative
 arrangements were not done by the Opposite Parties. The
 alternative arrangements had to be done by Opposite Party
 No.3/Airlines but not by Appellant.
 The District Forum failed to consider that the Appellant is
 only facilitator and neither it had control nor operation of
 flight and cancellation.
5
 The District Forum failed to consider that the ticket amounts
 were refunded to Respondent No.1/Complainant.
  The District Forum failed to appreciate that the hotel rooms
 were booked through cleartrip.com and as per terms, if the
 person does not arrive on the first night of accommodation
 booked, the property will be released and they will be
 charged full. Hence, there is no role of Appellant in refund of
 hotel charges.
 The District Forum ought not to have held that there is a
 deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of
 the Appellant without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity o

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
nt without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or whether it is liable to be set aside, modified
or interfered with, in any manner? To what relief?
14. We have perused the material available on record and heard
the counsel for the parties. On perusal of the record, we find that
Opposite Party No.3-Airlines was set exparte in the
CC.No.162/2018 on the file of District Commission, Adilabad,
however vide IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 they filed their
written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey and rights of the
passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and
these conditions constitute a valid binding contract between
parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
16. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
ent
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

Tickets were booked on 17.05.2016 through travel agent Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 in the main complaint.
17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the
General Insurance Company engaged in the business of general
insurance including Air Travel Insurance in collaboration with
Respondent No.3/Opposite Party No.3.
18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant requested the Opposite Parties to arrange
alternate arrangements as they were on their way to Hyderabad
and the schedule was booked in advance for Darshan at Tirupathi
and accommodation at hotels in various places of pilgrimage. Due
to the sudden cancellation of the flight, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant incurred a heavy loss and suffered great
7
hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight ticke

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
light is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
b

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
oking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
pposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
9
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
ticket for

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs 1. Sri Menga Pradeep Raj on 7 December, 2023
text:
iled are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
9
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.
26. For the reasons stated herein above and after giving
thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
R

ugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the

The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the

International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
Cause Title/Judgement-Entry STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION WEST BENGAL 11A, Mirza Ghalib Street, Kolkata - 700087   First Appeal No. A/1298/2017 ( Date of Filing : 14 Dec 2017 ) (Arisen out of Order Dated 30/05/2017 in Case No. Complaint Case No. CC/54/2011 of District Nadia)   1. International Car and Motors Ltd. Vill.- Chak Gujran, P.O. Piplanwala Jalandhar Road, Hoshiarpur, Punjab. ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. Sri Shyam Sundar Sen S/o Shibapada Sen, Buroshibtola Road, Harishava Para, P.O. & P.S. - Navadwip, Dist. Nadia, Pin -741 302. 2. Sri Mrinmoy Saha, Prop., M. Enterprise International Mankara, Akher Mill, NH-34, Berhampore, Murshidabad, Pin -741 302. 3. Sri Badal Banik S/o Lt. Lakshman Chandra Banik, Bowbazar Road(near Asha Cycle), Nabadwip, Nadia, Pin -741 302. ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HON'BLE MR. SHYAMAL GUPTA PRESIDING MEMBER   HON'BLE MR. UTPAL KUMAR BHATTACHARYA MEMBER   For the Appellant: Mr. Sankar Mukhopadhyay, Ms. Sreetama Das, Advocate For the Respondent: Mr. Srijan Nayak.Mr. Debesh Halder.Mr. Saikat Mali., Advocate Dated : 14 Jan 2020 Final Order / Judgement

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
For the Appellant: Mr. Sankar Mukhopadhyay, Ms. Sreetama Das, Advocate For the Respondent: Mr. Srijan Nayak.Mr. Debesh Halder.Mr. Saikat Mali., Advocate Dated : 14 Jan 2020 Final Order / Judgement 

Sri Shyamal Gupta, Member
In this Appeal, the legality of the Order dated 30-05-2017 of the Ld. District Forum, Nadia passed in CC/54/2011 is called in question by the Appellant.
The complaint relates to a defective car being purchased by the Respondent.
We have heard the submission advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the documents on record.
Documents on record reveal that the Respondent took delivery of the car in question on 01-06-2010 and within a period of one year (till May, 2011), the said car had to be sent to the service centre not once or twice, but 5 times in a row.
It appears, vide impugned order the Forum below directed the Appellant and Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to either return the vehicle in a roadworthy condition after removing the defects or pay back the cost of the vehicle in question.  They were further directed to pay compensation and litigation cost to the tune of Rs. 10,000/- and Rs. 5,000/-, respectively.
From whatever angle we look at it, there can be no manner of doubt as to the fact that the Ld. District Forum at its wisdom passed a well balanced order.
The Appellant cannot disagree to the fact that if a brand new car starts malfunctioning every

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
no manner of doubt as to the fact that the Ld. District Forum at its wisdom passed a well balanced order.
The Appellant cannot disagree to the fact that if a brand new car starts malfunctioning every now and then, it defeats the very purpose of having it. There being nothing to show that the car in question developed problem on account of mishandling of the same by the Respondent No. 1, in our considered opinion, the Appellant cannot escape its liability.
In uncertain terms, the Ld. District Forum directed the Appellant to return the car to the Respondent No. 1.  However, it seems, it took no positive step to return the same on its own and instead passed the buck upon the Respondent No. 1 to collect the same from its place.  It was a flagrant violation of the direction of the Ld. District Forum and for obvious reason; the Respondent No. 1 did not give in to the dictate of the Appellant.
The Appellant refused to accept that the car in question is suffering from any sort of manufacturing defect. If it is presumed for the sake of argument that the car in question is not suffering from any sort of manufacturing defect, in that case, the inevitable conclusion would be that the service centre is incapable of repairing it properly.
Notwithstanding the Appellant underlined the need for expert opinion to prove the allegation of 'manufacturing defect' as made by the Respondent No. 1, it

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
centre is incapable of repairing it properly.
Notwithstanding the Appellant underlined the need for expert opinion to prove the allegation of 'manufacturing defect' as made by the Respondent No. 1, it appears that the Hon'ble National Commission in
Tata Motors v. Rajesh Tyagi & Anr.
,  2014 (1) CLT 238 (NC) dealt on this issue at great length.  The solemn observation of the Hon'ble Commission assumes great significance in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present dispute and as such the same is appended below.
"6. We have examined the entire material on record and given a thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced before us. The main thrust of the line of argument taken by the petitioners revolves around the fact that there was no evidence of any manufacturing defect in the vehicle. The onus to prove the manufacturing defect is on the complainant and the same should be proved by expert evidence, in the absence of which no liability can be attributed to the petitioner to compensate the complainant. On the other hand, the State Commission in their order have relied upon the definition of defect as contained in the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
and stated that a complainant is liable to be compensated, if there is any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, etc. of the vehicle. The State Commission observed in their order as follows:

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
lainant is liable to be compensated, if there is any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, etc. of the vehicle. The State Commission observed in their order as follows:-
5. In our view, it is misconceived notion that any vehicle for that purpose any goods can be ordered to be replaced or the cost can be ordered to be refunded only if they suffer from manufacturing defect. There is no such concept of goods suffering from manufacturing defect enshrined by the provision of
Consumer Protection Act
.
Consumer Protection Act
only defines the word defect by way of
Section 2(1) (f)
of the Act which is to the following effect:-
Defect means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied, or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods.
6. In such cases we have taken a sustained view that whenever a consumer goes for a brand new goods like the vehicle his minimum expectation is that he would not encounter or face any inconvenience or hardship for few months or a year and if he had to take the vehicle time and again to the workshop for removing one defect or the other, he suffers immensely in terms of loss of time, loss of business, physical discomfort and

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
a year and if he had to take the vehicle time and again to the workshop for removing one defect or the other, he suffers immensely in terms of loss of time, loss of business, physical discomfort and emotional sufferings having not reaped the fruits of paying heavy amount for purchasing a new vehicle.
7. We have also taken a view that onus shifts to the manufacturer to show that the vehicle does not suffer from manufacturing defect once complainant has proved and discharged the initial onus that the vehicle was defective vehicle on the basis of large number of job cards showing that vehicle was taken on many occasion for removing one defect or the other. Complainant has already suffered immensely and is a wronged person by having been sold a defective goods and to expect him to again incur expenses by obtaining expert opinion to show the vehicle suffers from manufacturing defect will be too much. Large number of visits to the workshop from the day of purchase of vehicle for removing some or other defects is sufficient to draw the inference that the vehicle is a defective vehicle. The circumstance of the vehicle having been taken for removal of defects within or after the period of warranty leaves no manner of doubt that the goods sold to the consumer is not only defective but also suffers from manufacturing defect.
If the defect continues for months together and years together

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
warranty leaves no manner of doubt that the goods sold to the consumer is not only defective but also suffers from manufacturing defect.
If the defect continues for months together and years together and erupts time and again no other inference can be drawn than that the vehicle suffers from manufacturing defect as defects which are not of manufacturing nature can be rectified or removed without their recurrence or without giving any further inconvenience to the consumer.
7. The State Commission have further observed in their order:-
..Bare perusal of the definition of word defect shows that any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods.
9. Thus in our view whenever a manufacturer of the vehicle offers to sell the brand new vehicle to the consumer there is an implied contract as to the claim of the manufacturer that the vehicle being sold by it does not suffer from and will not suffer from any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency and standard which is required to be maintained.
10. The audacity and impunity on the part of the respondent to rub salt on the wounds of the complaina

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency and standard which is required to be maintained.
10. The audacity and impunity on the part of the respondent to rub salt on the wounds of the complainant that he should prove that he had been visiting time and again is demonstrated from their reply sent by both respondent as well as reply of notice and other notice sent by the complainant to the respondent No.1. For such type of manufacturers and service providers the Supreme court has in
Ghaziabad Development Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
(2004) 5 Supreme Court Cases 65 come down heavily and called upon the Consumer Forum and Commissions established under the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
to not only compensate the consumer as to the actual loss suffered by him but also to compensate him as to the mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering, physical discomfort, loss of business, loss of time by taking vehicle time and again to the workshop.
8. From the entire factual matrix of the case, it is very clearly brought out that the vehicle in question is a defective vehicle when judged from the definition of defect as contained in
section 2(1)(f)
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986. In reply to the legal notice dated 18.07.2003, sent by the petitioner to the complainant, there is a non-ambiguous admission on the part of the OPs that the allegation levelled in the complaint about the

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text: eply to the legal notice dated 18.07.2003, sent by the petitioner to the complainant, there is a non-ambiguous admission on the part of the OPs that the allegation levelled in the complaint about the defect of water accumulation inside the vehicle are true. The basic question is whether this kind of situation about the vehicle as admitted in the reply to the show-cause notice can be categorised as manufacturing defect or not. In the strict technical terminology, this kind of situation may not lead to the conclusion that there is a manufacturing defect; but still, it goes without saying that whatever defect has been observed in the vehicle for which the complainant had to suffer the mental agony of taking the vehicle to the workshop so many times, has to be attended to in proper perspective. It is the bound duty of both the manufacturer and the dealer to attend to the said defect and make it a defect-free vehicle and if they are not in a position to do so, they should either refund the cost of the vehicle or provide a new vehicle to the consumer. We, therefore, agree with the conclusion arrived at by the State Commission that whenever a brand new vehicle is sold to a consumer, there is an implied contract that the vehicle being sold does not suffer from and will not suffer from any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency and standard which

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
is an implied contract that the vehicle being sold does not suffer from and will not suffer from any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency and standard which is required to be maintained.
9. It is further observed that the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
is a benevolent social legislation as held by the Honble Apex Court in their judgements from time to time and is aimed at providing for better protection of the interests of the consumers as defined in the preamble to the Act itself. Given the facts at hand, the interests of the consumer in the present case can be protected only if he is provided a vehicle which is free from defects from all angles and he is not subjected to the technicalities of proving whether any manufacturing defect exists or not".
If a new car turns defunct at regular intervals within few months of its purchase, it hardly requires any expert opinion to certify the inherent defect of the same.  Still we find that the Ld. District Forum took a very lenient view and directed the Appellant to handover the car after removing its defects properly.  Such is the ego of the Appellant that, in order to test the tenacity of the Respondent No. 1 further, it preferred this Appeal. There being no merit in this Appeal, the same deserves no favourable consideration.
As we find, the car is languishing at the service centre for more t

title: International Car And Motors Ltd. vs Sri Shyam Sundar Sen on 14 January, 2020
text:
pondent No. 1 further, it preferred this Appeal. There being no merit in this Appeal, the same deserves no favourable consideration.
As we find, the car is languishing at the service centre for more than 8-½ years.  In such circumstances, it hardly requires any emphasis that even if the same is repaired temporarily, the defective car would not last long and since the warranty period already got over, the Respondent No. 1 would not be entitled to warranty benefits any more.
Considering all aspects, we deem it appropriate to modify the impugned order to the effect that the Appellant and Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 shall jointly and/or severally return the price of the car in question along with simple interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the complaint case till full and final payment is made.  Rest of the order shall remain unaltered.
In the result, we dismiss this Appeal.     [HON'BLE MR. SHYAMAL GUPTA] PRESIDING MEMBER 
     [HON'BLE MR. UTPAL KUMAR BHATTACHARYA] MEMBER

are the Opposite Party No.1, 3 and 4 in CC.No.195/2018.

3. The facts of the complaint are that the Complainant is a
resident of Nirmal District and booked her flight tickets to travel to
Tirupathi from Hyderabad. Onward journey was booked for travel
to Tirupathi on 01.06.2016 and return on 04.06.2016. The tickets

Limited. The Policy vide No.OG-17-1901-9905-00001192 was valid
for the period 01.06.2016 to 30.06.2016 for a premium of
Rs.100/-.
4. It is the Complainant's grievance that Opposi

ral Insurance Company
Limited. The Policy vide No.OG-17-1901-9905-00001192 was valid
for the period 01.06.2016 to 30.06.2016 for a premium of
Rs.100/-.
4. It is the Complainant's grievance that Opposite Party No.3
intimated him on 31.05.2016 at 14:00 hours about the flight
cancellation when arrangements were already made at Tirupathi
for the hotel accommodation and other arrangements for seeing

and non-attendance at Tirupathi for Darshan has caused the

5. The Opposite Party No.1 failed to appear and was set

ervice of booking flight tickets from Hyderabad to

hotel rooms for the duration of his stay.
6. On 31.05.2016, Opposite Party No.3 informed Opposite Party
No.2 about the cancellation of flight and the information was
passed on to the Complainant through Opposite Party No.1. The
Opposite Party No.3 refunded the cost of flight tickets which were
promptly paid to the Complainant.
7. The Complainant is demanding refund of hotel booking,

12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 preferred this appeal with the
following grounds:
 The District Forum grossly erred in holding that alternative
 arrangements were not done by the Opposite Parties. The
 alternative arrangements had to be done by Opposite Party
 No.3/Airlines but not by Appellant.
 The District Forum failed to consider that the Appellant is
 only facilitator and neither it had control nor operation of
 flight and cancellation.
5
 The District Forum failed to consider that the ticket amounts
 were refunded to Respondent No.1/Complainant.
  The District Forum failed to appreciate that the hotel rooms
 were booked through cleartrip.com and as per terms, if the
 person does not arrive on the first night of accommodation
 booked, the property will be released and they will be
 charged full. Hence, there is no role of Appellant in refund of
 hotel charges.
 The District Forum ought not to have held that there is a
 deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of
 the Appellant without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or

 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or whether it is liable to be set aside, modified
or interfered with, in any manner? To what relief?
14. We have perused the material available on record and heard
the counsel for the parties. On perusal of the record, we find that
Opposite Party No.3-Airlines was set exparte in the
CC.No.195/2018 on the file of District Commission, Adilabad,
however vide IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 they filed their
written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as

The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey

below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as

The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their

passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and

parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.

complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:

04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the

18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent

hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight ticke

light is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a

20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably

of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy

pposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for

ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the

ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.
26. For the reasons stated herein above and after giving
thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.

impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the

additional items of purchase in the bills. It is clear that the repudiation of the

complainant had failed to furnish satisfactory proof of purchase /loss and had

12.1 Further, the repudiation of the claim was made by the insurance company
on 29.08.2008 but the complainant took no action of filing the complaint during a
period of five years till 2013 when a further communication with the insurer was
made by the insured. As such, the complaint was filed as late as on 24.12.2013.
The perusal of the complaint which was filed has no inherent explanation
explaining such unreasonable delay. The OP bank in its written version in
para-10 took a preliminary objection that the complaint is barred by limitation.
Apart from this, though the complainant had already obtained the survey report
which, and the repudiation letter also, categorically brought out that the purchase
Page 25 of 29
bills from M/s JalaRam Enterprises, M/s Dhiraj Jewellers, M/s Shivam Bangles
and M/s Skyline presented to the surveyor to establish the quantum of loss were
fraudulently and palpably manipulated by inserting additional figures in the bill so
as to fraudulently inflate the value of purchases, the complaint filed or the
evidence filed thereafter, has not categorically and sharply attempted to explain
the allegation or to dispr

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
n the bill so
as to fraudulently inflate the value of purchases, the complaint filed or the
evidence filed thereafter, has not categorically and sharply attempted to explain
the allegation or to disprove the allegation by producing any cogent evidence.
Such overwriting and inflation to the extent of nearly Rs.6.19 lakhs in 20
purchase bills as tabulated above is dealt with by the State Commission in para
14 and 15 of its order with the conclusion that "all this clearly show that the bills
of purchase were corrected. Commission under the Act has power to compare
the handwriting, which when done, complainant's writing of 2, 4, k, and p match
with many of them". The FSL report also clearly establishes such intended
addition of amounts in the bills so as to artificially inflate the purchase. The FSL
report scientifically support such finding firstly of the surveyor and the insurer and
of thereafter of the State Commission. Additionally, the complainant himself in
the complaint in para 6 of the complaint (page 178) has stated that M/s Bittoo
Bindia Selection (from whom also major purchases are stated to have been
made to justify the quantity and value of loss) has been paid cash against
purchases to the extent of as high as Rs.29 lakhs, the fact and source of which
could not be reasonably explained through cogent corroborative material,
though, even if prima facie established, the s

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
purchases to the extent of as high as Rs.29 lakhs, the fact and source of which
could not be reasonably explained through cogent corroborative material,
though, even if prima facie established, the stale and non-comtemporaneous
evidence or explanation after 5 years of the survey report would have limited
reliability. Though it is the averment in the complaint that "all documents were
submitted", the fundamental issue of dishonest and fraudulent inflation of the
purchases has remained wholly unexplained in the complaint or thereafter. Page
no. 146 to 160 are the copies of the bank statement of M/s Bittoo Bindia
selection (page 146, 147) and of the complainant (page 148 to 160). Page 161
gives the details of alleged payment through bank transfer totalling to Rs.19.17
lakhs made to M/s Bittoo Bindia selection on the strength of which it was averred
before the State Commission that notwithstanding the overwriting in the bills, the
same are genuine. Not only the State Commission has dealt with the issue and
brought out the fallacy of the contention, it has also been demonstrated in para
14 and 15 of the State Commission that the bills presented to the surveyor are
inflated and depict transactions which are far from real and substantially inflated.
Page 26 of 29
Apart from this, the entries in the bank statement have not been specifically
correlated so as to establish that alleged p

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
ransactions which are far from real and substantially inflated.
Page 26 of 29
Apart from this, the entries in the bank statement have not been specifically
correlated so as to establish that alleged payment of Rs. 19.17 lakhs made to M/s
Bittu Bindiya selection has come out from the bank account of the insured or that
the alleged cash payments to M/s Bindiya is genuinely and contemporaneously
made as claimed. As can be seen, the eight entries on page 146 for the period
from 04.02.2006 to 10.04.2006 categorically show the payment by the insured of
only nearly Rs.6.5 lakhs to M/s Bittu Bindiya Selections. The balance pages of
Bank Statement on page 147 to 160 nowhere establishes that any payment is
made by the insured to any specific party and neither the supporting ledger
account copy nor any contra account copy nor any certificate from the Bank
either of the complainant himself or from the banker of the alleged recipient of
the amount has been filed to support the contention of the payment of Rs. 19.17
lakhs or, for that matter, the cash of Rs. 29 as per Page 161 and para 6 of the
complaint. The amount of Rs. 7.19 lakhs is of course credited in account of M/s
Bittu Bindiya Selections (page 147). However, it also does not show or establish
as to from which particular account the amount is debited. In any case, the
amount is not shown to have been debited in the complainant's acc

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
ns (page 147). However, it also does not show or establish
as to from which particular account the amount is debited. In any case, the
amount is not shown to have been debited in the complainant's account on
17.08.2007 because the copy of the complainant's bank statement for the period
August 2007 has not been placed on record. Further, as noted earlier, as per the
complainant's own averment in the complaint, huge cash payment of Rs.29 lakhs
is made to M/s Bindiya and there is no evidence on record regarding the source
of cash and how such cash payment for purchases is made and reflected in the
sales book and the cash book. Similarly, qua the alleged copies of stock
statements allegedly submitted to he Bank, placed at Page No.73 to 109, firstly
these stocks statement do not show any acknowledgement receipt of the Bank.
Secondly, the Bank in its Written version in para 12 has categorically stated that
the complainant has not deposited any stock statement and further that the bank
does not have any such copy on record. Otherwise also the mere filing of stock
statement with the bank showing any arbitrary figure therein does not in itself
establish the quantum and value of stock as on the date of the incident. Thus,
the Bank statements or stock-statements allegedly submitted to the Bank or any
other records, in our opinion also, do not refute or dilute the serious and
conclusive ev

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
the date of the incident. Thus,
the Bank statements or stock-statements allegedly submitted to the Bank or any
other records, in our opinion also, do not refute or dilute the serious and
conclusive evidence of fraud and dishonesty in manipulating the documents
(purchase bills) submitted to the surveyor in support of the claim and therefore
Page 27 of 29
no fault indeed can be found in the conclusions of the State Commission as duly
supported by the Survey Report, the CA's report and the FSL report.
13. Be that as it may, the dishonest and fraudulent manipulation of the
purchase bills with inflation component of Rs.6.19 lakhs is unimpeachably
established on record. Therefore, we have no hesitation in holding that the
insurer and the State Commission are absolutely right in their conclusion that
the complainant has violated the fundamental condition of uberrima fide
incorporated in condition no.7/8 of the policy as reproduced by State
Commission in para 8, as rightly concluded by the State Commission in that
para. The evidenced dishonestly and fraud on the part of the complainant for
enhancing the claim goes to the root of the insurance contract and the insurer is
absolutely justified in wholly repudiating the liability. We also find no substance in
the contention on behalf of the complainant that the State Commission exceeded
its jurisdiction by overstepping the limited directio

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
d in wholly repudiating the liability. We also find no substance in
the contention on behalf of the complainant that the State Commission exceeded
its jurisdiction by overstepping the limited directions of this Commission while
remanding the matter. As such, the reference to FSL has assisted the State
Commission in re-considering and re-appreciating the evidence brought on
record and indeed the State Forum has inherent powers to make expert
reference as and when considered necessary even during remand proceedings
when there is neither any express direction nor any express bar in the remand
order of this Commission. Also, the State Commission's order dated 25.02.2020
allowing the insurance company's application for such reference to the
Forensic/handwriting expert appears to have attained finality by not having been
challenged before any higher fora. The reliance placed by the Ld. Counsel for the
complainant on decisions as cited in para 9 supra is also misplaced for two
reasons. First, the decisions are in the context of criminal proceedings while the
proceedings before the State Commission are not only civil in nature but they are
also of summary nature wherein the evidence is to be evaluated not on the basis
of "beyond reasonable doubt", but on the basis of preponderance of probability.
Second, the handwriting expert's report is not the sole basis for the State
Commission to

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
be evaluated not on the basis
of "beyond reasonable doubt", but on the basis of preponderance of probability.
Second, the handwriting expert's report is not the sole basis for the State
Commission to have arrived at its findings. There were already material in the
nature of survey report, which as per the settled principle is a primary and
significant piece of evidence, CA's report and the fact of dishonest insertion of
amounts in the purchase bills evident even to the naked eyes. The State
Commission has also duly and minutely considered the affidavits of the
Page 28 of 29
complainant as also the proprietor of M/s Bitto Bindia and concluded that the
 same is of no assistance to the complainant in establishing his claim. Moreover,
 though not noted by the State Commission, we cannot overlook the fact that the
 proprietor/partners of M/s JalaRam Enterprises, M/s Dhiraj Jewellers, M/s
 Shivam Bangles and M/s Skyline, the parties whose bills are found to have been
 manipulated by the complainant, have not been presented for any
 cross-examination. On the other hand, the affidavits of the surveyor Shri Sunil
. Kumar P. Bhatt as also of the Chartered accountant Shri Pravin Kumar Shah
 have been filed by the insurance company wherein both of them have reiterated
 the findings given by them. These have duly been considered by the State
 Commission in para 13 of the order. After consid

title: M/S. Kangan Palace vs Branch Manaer Union Bank Of India & Anr. on 15 May, 2026
text:
ave been filed by the insurance company wherein both of them have reiterated
 the findings given by them. These have duly been considered by the State
 Commission in para 13 of the order. After considering the totality of the facts, we
 are therefore of the considered opinion that the claim of the complainant was
 based on altered, inflated and unreliable documents, and the repudiation by the
 Insurance Company was fully justified and was in accordance with policy
 conditions and with the violation of the solemn principle of utmost good faith. If
 the insured engages into dishonest means for enhancing or supporting the
 indemnification amount, the insurer would be fully entitled to repudiate the whole
 claim. Accordingly, the findings recorded by the State Commission do not suffer
 from any error of fact or law warranting any interference. The present Appeal
 therefore lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed and the impugned order dated
 12.11.2021 is affirmed. No order as to costs.
Sd/-

by extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the airline,

taken. It, then, specifies what these extra ordinary circumstances

shall include, namely, political instability, natural disaster, civil war,

insurrection or riot, flood, explosion, governmental regulation or

cessation, slowdown or interruption of work or any other factors that

are beyond the control of the airline. Under clause 1.4, the airline is

exonerated from liability on account of delay, if it is attributable to Air

Traffic Control (ATC), meteorological conditions, security risks or any

other causes that are beyond control of the airline.
