 This is an appeal under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (in short, "the Act") wherein challenge is made to order dated 09.07.2009 passed by the Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, New Delhi (in short, "the District Forum") in Complaint Case No. 285/2007.
Briefly the facts relevant for the disposal of present appeal are as under:
The respondent herein was the complainant before the Ld. District Forum.  A complaint under
Section 12
of the Act was filed by him alleging therein that he got a ticket booked on 19.12.2006 for journey from Kolkata to Delhi on 27.12.2006 through M/s Oswal Air Travels by Flight No.S2-303 for an amount of Rs.3,666/-.  It was alleged that when respondent/complainant reached Kolkata Airport for boarding and waited up till the schedule time of flight, the appellant/OP was informed that the flight had been cancelled and passengers were directed to make their own arrangements for their journey.  The agent of the other Airlines approached the respondent/complainant and other co-passengers and offered to travel through their respective Airlines by giving tickets at higher amount.  It was alleged that since the respondent/complainant had to attend

title: Air Sahara/Jet Lite India Ltd. vs M.K. Singh on 22 December, 2015
text:
dent/complainant and other co-passengers and offered to travel through their respective Airlines by giving tickets at higher amount.  It was alleged that since the respondent/complainant had to attend an interview at Sri Nagar in the next morning, having no other option, the respondent/complainant travelled through Air Deccan to reach the destination.  On demand of refund money, the appellant's/OP's official informed that it would be refunded through the account of travelling agent i.e. M/s Oswal Air Travels.  The appellant/OP did not refund the amount of ticket to the respondent/complainant. The respondent/complainant alleged that the appellant/OP had committed deficiency in service within the meaning of Act and had prayed for compensation for the delay caused in the journey and for having purchased ticket at higher rate including not refunding the price of ticket.
The appellant/OP had opposed the complaint case by filing written version wherein it was alleged that flight No.S2-303 dated 27.12.2006 Kolkata Delhi Sector was cancelled as the flight S2-303 dated 26.12.2006 which departed from Kolkata on time could not land at Delhi Airport due to poor visibility and went back to Kolkata the same night, consequently the next day flight i.e. 27.12.2006 could not be scheduled as such it was cancelled due to prevailing bad weather in Delhi Sector.  It was alleged that there was no de

title: Air Sahara/Jet Lite India Ltd. vs M.K. Singh on 22 December, 2015
text:
ata the same night, consequently the next day flight i.e. 27.12.2006 could not be scheduled as such it was cancelled due to prevailing bad weather in Delhi Sector.  It was alleged that there was no deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP as the flight in question was cancelled due to bad weather conditions.
Both the parties led evidence by way of affidavits before the Ld. District Forum.
After hearing the Counsel for the parties, the Ld. District Forum held that the flight in question was cancelled due to bad weather conditions at Delhi and went back to Kolkata.  The Ld. District Forum held that in these circumstances, the sufferings of the respondent/complainant for failure to appear in the next day interview cannot be attributed to appellant/OP.  However, for non-refund of price of ticket to the respondent/complainant, the Ld. District Forum held that there was deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP.  The price of ticket was Rs.3,666/-.  Accordingly the Ld. District Forum ordered as under:
"1.       OP will pay to the Complainant Rs.3666/- being the price of ticket.
2.        On account of deficiency of service, mental agony and harassment, OP will pay Rs.10,000/- to the Complainant.
3.        OP will pay Rs.5,000/- towards Cost of litigation.
This order be complied within 30 days.
Pronounced in open court on 9.7.09."
Aggrieved with the aforesaid order, p

title: Air Sahara/Jet Lite India Ltd. vs M.K. Singh on 22 December, 2015
text:
000/- to the Complainant.
3.        OP will pay Rs.5,000/- towards Cost of litigation.
This order be complied within 30 days.
Pronounced in open court on 9.7.09."
Aggrieved with the aforesaid order, present appeal is filed.
Ld. Counsel for the appellant has contended that there is no deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP as the ticket price had already been refunded to respondent/complainant through the agent from whom the ticket was booked.  It is contended that the Ld. District Forum has not considered the  evidence led in this regard.  Ld. Counsel has relied upon Ex-OPC, a handwritten note wherein it is alleged that the amount of the ticket in question was refunded through agent.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondent/complainant has contended that when flight was cancelled, the respondent/complainant was told that price of ticket would be refunded to him through the travel agent only.  It is contended that the same was never refunded.  It is contended that Ex-OPC is not believable.  Ld. Counsel for respondent/complainant has relied upon affidavit of respondent/complainant dated 26.2.08 in this regard.
We have considered the submission made and perused Ex-OPC.  Ex-OPC is a photocopy of handwritten note wherein it is alleged that sale and refund of ticket in question has been affected through the agent in 2nd fortnight of December, 2006.  The name of th

title: Air Sahara/Jet Lite India Ltd. vs M.K. Singh on 22 December, 2015
text:
OPC.  Ex-OPC is a photocopy of handwritten note wherein it is alleged that sale and refund of ticket in question has been affected through the agent in 2nd fortnight of December, 2006.  The name of the person who has allegedly written note is not given in Ex-OPC.  Further the name of agent to whom it is alleged that the amount is refunded is also not given.  No account statement is filed to substantiate that payment has been made to the agent as is alleged.  The date, as to when the alleged note is written, is also not mentioned.  Further as per alleged note, money is refunded to agent in 2nd fortnight of December, 2006.  The flight was cancelled on 27.12.06.  The exact date is not given as to when money was allegedly refunded to the agent. The alleged note lacks material particulars. The appellant ought to have given the necessary details to substantiate that the price of ticket has been refunded through the agent.  The respondent/complainant has categorically averred in the complaint that on demand, the refund was not given to him.  There is an affidavit of respondent/complainant to this effect also.  We find no reason to disbelieve the affidavit of respondent/complainant.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, no illegality or perversity is seen in the impugned order whereby the appellant has been directed to refund the price of the ticket i.e. Rs.3,666/- towards refund

title: Air Sahara/Jet Lite India Ltd. vs M.K. Singh on 22 December, 2015
text:
facts and circumstances of the case, no illegality or perversity is seen in the impugned order whereby the appellant has been directed to refund the price of the ticket i.e. Rs.3,666/- towards refund of ticket. The compensation and litigation cost awarded is also reasonable.
No case for interference is made out.  Appeal stands dismissed.  There is no order as to costs.
FDR, if any, deposited by the appellant be released after completing due formalities.

 forthwith.  Thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.

darshan tickets and cab services from Opposite Party No.2 which
were done subject to terms and conditions of respective operators,
therefore, this Opposite Party No.2 is in no way concerned with the
allegations and reliefs claimed by the Complainant. All the reliefs
and damages are directly attributable to the cancellation of the
flight, hence they seek dismissal of the complaint against this
Opposite Party with costs.
8. The Opposite Party No.3 was set exparte. The Opposite Party
No.4 is the Insurance Company and as per their written version
the flight was cancelled by the Airlines-Opposite Party No.3 and
the amount was refunded to the Complainant. As per their policy
terms and conditions Section VIII reads as follows:-
4
Section VIII: Trip Cancellation:
"Subject to all other terms and conditions, the company will
indemnify the insured subject to limits shown in schedule, for loss of
ticke

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
ion VIII reads as follows:-
4
Section VIII: Trip Cancellation:
"Subject to all other terms and conditions, the company will
indemnify the insured subject to limits shown in schedule, for loss of
ticket charges paid or contracted to be paid by the insured, which
are not recoverable from any other source."
9. In this case, Opposite Party No.3 has refunded the ticket
amount to the Complainant, therefore, the Complainant is not
liable for any compensation from this Opposite Party No.4 the
Insurance Company. The Complainant is taking a chance litigation
and in view of the facts and circumstances, they seek dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
10. Before the District Commission, the Complainant filed
Evidence Affidavit and got marked Ex.A1 to A4. The Opposite Party
No.4 filed evidence affidavit. Ex.B1 & B2 are marked on their
behalf.
11. The District Commission after hearing and considering the
material on record, allowed the complaint directing the Opposite
Party No.1 to 3 to pay each Rs.50,000/- in all with interest @ 12%
p.a. from the date of cancellation of flight ticket till realization. The
Opposite Party No.4 is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- with interest @
18% p.a. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposit

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 preferred this appeal with the
following grounds:
 The District Forum grossly erred in holding that alternative
 arrangements were not done by the Opposite Parties. The
 alternative arrangements had to be done by Opposite Party
 No.3/Airlines but not by Appellant.
 The District Forum failed to consider that the Appellant is
 only facilitator and neither it had control nor operation of
 flight and cancellation.
5
 The District Forum failed to consider that the ticket amounts
 were refunded to Respondent No.1/Complainant.
  The District Forum failed to appreciate that the hotel rooms
 were booked through cleartrip.com and as per terms, if the
 person does not arrive on the first night of accommodation
 booked, the property will be released and they will be
 charged full. Hence, there is no role of Appellant in refund of
 hotel charges.
 The District Forum ought not to have held that there is a
 deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of
 the Appellant without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
t without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or whether it is liable to be set aside, modified
or interfered with, in any manner? To what relief?
14. We have perused the material available on record and heard
the counsel for the parties. On perusal of the record, we find that
Opposite Party No.3-Airlines was set exparte in the
CC.No.199/2018 on the file of District Commission, Adilabad,
however vide IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 they filed their
written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
y the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey and rights of the
passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and
these conditions constitute a valid binding contract between
parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
16. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
ent
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

Tickets were booked on 17.05.2016 through travel agent Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 in the main complaint.
17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the
General Insurance Company engaged in the business of general
insurance including Air Travel Insurance in collaboration with
Respondent No.3/Opposite Party No.3.
18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant requested the Opposite Parties to arrange
alternate arrangements as they were on their way to Hyderabad
and the schedule was booked in advance for Darshan at Tirupathi
and accommodation at hotels in various places of pilgrimage. Due
to the sudden cancellation of the flight, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant incurred a heavy loss and suffered great
7
hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight ticke

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
light is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
b

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
oking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
pposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
iled are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.
26. For the reasons stated herein above and after giving
thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
R

title: M/S.Riya Travels And Tours India Pvt. ... vs Sri Anumula Suresh on 7 December, 2023
text:
ugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
Respondent No.1/Complainant a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards
compensation. Time for compliance is six weeks, failing which the
amount of Rs.10,000/- shall carry interest @ 8% p.a. till
realization. The parties to bear their own costs.

JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL, PRESIDENT:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant/complainant

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
nt No.1&3: Shri Devinder Kumar, Advocate.
 For respondent No.2 :Shri Ammish Goel, Advocate.

JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL, PRESIDENT:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant/complainant

against the order dated 6.4.2017 passed by District Consumer

Disputes Redressal Forum, Ludhiana (in short, "the District Forum"),

whereby the complaint filed by him, under Section 12 of the
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 2
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
(in short, "
C.P. Act
") for issuance of

following directions to the opposite parties:-
i) to refund, replace or repair his i-phone;

 ii) to pay compensation of ₹25,000/- on account of mental

 tension, pain and agony; and

 iii) to pay ₹11,000/-, as litigation expenses,

was dismissed.
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties will

be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Forum.
3. Brief facts, for the disposal of the present appeal, are that the

complainant purchased an Apple i-phone 5S, 16 GB MM, Silver

Colour bearing product serial/IMEI No.358690056911296

manufactured by opposite party No.1 through opposite party No.2,

vide Invoice No.IN003036 dated 12.12.2013 by paying ₹61,856/-
under the Scheme of Reliance Truly Unlimited Plan for 24 months.

The amount was to be paid in monthly instalments at the rate of

₹2,999/-, payable in 24 Equal Monthly Instalments. In the first week

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
under the Scheme of Reliance Truly Unlimited Plan for 24 months.

The amount was to be paid in monthly instalments at the rate of

₹2,999/-, payable in 24 Equal Monthly Instalments. In the first week

of November 2014 some problem occurred in the display of this

mobile phone and half of the display screen became black suddenly.

The complainant claimed that he had been keeping the i-phone in

good condition and had been using the same carefully and

cautiously. On 7.11.2014 the complainant deposited the said mobile

phone in question with opposite party No.3 i.e. Service Centre of

opposite party No.1. After checking, the said mobile phone was

returned to the complainant by claiming that damage had occurred,

which could not be repaired under warranty. For repair, demand of
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 3
₹21,500/- was made. Despite repeated requests, the mobile phone

has neither been repaired nor replaced nor the price of the same has

been refunded. As such, registered legal notice dated 17.11.2014

was served upon opposite parties through his counsel but no reply

thereto has been received. Alleging deficiency in service on the part

of the opposite parties, the present complaint was filed by the

complainant in the District Forum praying the aforesaid relief.
4. It needs to be noticed that earlier this complaint was allowed,

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
art

of the opposite parties, the present complaint was filed by the

complainant in the District Forum praying the aforesaid relief.
4. It needs to be noticed that earlier this complaint was allowed,

vide order dated 17.4.2015 passed by the District Forum. Against

that order, FA No.604 of 2015 was preferred by opposite party No.1.

The same was allowed and the order dated 17.4.2015 was set aside.

The case was remanded back to the District Forum for deciding the

same afresh by proceeding in accordance with the provisions of the
C.P. Act
. After receipt of the consumer complaint, separate written

statements were filed by opposite parties Nos.1 and 2 and opposite

party No.3 preferred to remain ex parte before the District Forum.

Thereafter the present impugned order has been passed.

Defence of opposite party No.1:
5. Opposite party No.1 in its reply claimed that the complaint has

been filed with mala fide intention, which is devoid of merits. The

consumers, who willfully destroy, damage or negligently handle the

product, are not eligible to claim relief under the
C.P. Act
and in case

damage to the product caused by external factors, then benefit of

warranty clauses is not available. So far as the purchase of the

mobile phone is concerned, the same was admitted. Rather it is

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
ase

damage to the product caused by external factors, then benefit of

warranty clauses is not available. So far as the purchase of the

mobile phone is concerned, the same was admitted. Rather it is

claimed that opposite party No.3, the Service Centre of opposite
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 4
party No.1, made diligent efforts for diagnosing the problem, when

the mobile phone was brought to it on 7.11.2014. Opposite party

No.3 after thorough technical analysis and visual mechanical

inspection found that the display of the mobile phone had turned

black and there were lines on it. Opposite Party No.1 found that all

that occurred due to pressure damage with the display. Services

were offered to be provided on payment basis because the loss

occurred due to pressure damage and claim was not covered under

the warranty clauses. The complainant alleged that it was a

manufacturing defect but actually it is own fault of the complainant

that he had caused damage by exerting high pressure on the screen.

It was admitted that the complainant had deposited the mobile phone

with opposite party No.3 on 7.11.2014 and the repair bill of the

mobile phone amounting to ₹21,500/- was also admitted. Thus the

damage to the mobile phone was not covered under the warranty

clause. A prayer for dismissal of the complaint qua it has been

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
of the

mobile phone amounting to ₹21,500/- was also admitted. Thus the

damage to the mobile phone was not covered under the warranty

clause. A prayer for dismissal of the complaint qua it has been

made.
Defence of opposite party No.2:
6. Opposite party No.2 filed its separate reply almost on the

identical lines as has been filed by opposite party No.1. It was

pleaded that the complainant has no locus-standi to file the

complaint against opposite party No.2 under
Section 7-B
of the

Indian Telegraph Act. Opposite party No.2 has only sold the mobile

set and the defects and other liabilities are of the manufacturer.

Damage to the product had been caused due to illegal act of the
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 5
complainant. Denying all other allegations made in the complaint, a

prayer for dismissal of the complaint has been made.
7. The parties produced evidence in support of their respective

averments before the District Forum, which after going through the

same and hearing learned counsel on their behalf, dismissed the

complaint, vide impugned order. Hence, this appeal.
8. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have

carefully gone through the records of the case.

Contentions of the Parties:
9. Learned counsel for the complainant has vehemently

contended that Ex.C-4 and Ex.R-3 is one and the same document

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
have

carefully gone through the records of the case.

Contentions of the Parties:
9. Learned counsel for the complainant has vehemently

contended that Ex.C-4 and Ex.R-3 is one and the same document

i.e. Service Delivery Challan. In this document reason/cause of

damage has not been mentioned. Due service was not provided by

the Service Centre. It is alleged that opposite party No.3 had

discussed the problem with him and it was specifically stated that it

was a case of pressure damage and due to pressure display screen

damaged and turned half black. It has further been contended that

since the i-phone is under the warranty period, therefore, the same

should be replaced or repaired free of cost by the opposite parties.

The District Forum committed an illegality and infirmity while

dismissing the complaint. It has been prayed that this appeal be

allowed; the impugned order passed by the District Forum be set

aside; and the complaint be allowed as prayed for.
10. On the other hand, learned counsel for opposite party No.1 has

vehemently contended that damage was on account of external

cause and the warranty is not applicable to the damage caused by
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 6
accident, abuse, misuse, fire, earthquake or other external cause.

Exerting of pressure on the mobile certainly falls in the category of

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
plicable to the damage caused by
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 6
accident, abuse, misuse, fire, earthquake or other external cause.

Exerting of pressure on the mobile certainly falls in the category of

damage on account of external cause. Therefore, the complainant is

not entitled to free repair in view of putting of pressure on the mobile

phone. He prayed that there is no merit in the present appeal and

the same is liable to be dismissed.
11. Learned counsel for opposite party No.2 has vehemently

contended that opposite party No.2 is only the seller and the

warranty, if any, is to be provided by opposite party No.1-

manufacturer. Moreover, the damage to the mobile phone in

question has been caused due to external pressure put on the

mobile phone and, as such, the benefit of warranty clauses cannot

be given. The District Forum has committed no illegality or infirmity

in passing the impugned order and the same is liable to be upheld.

Consideration of Contentions:
12. We have given our thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the learned counsel for the parties.
13. Against the column "Problem Reported" in Service Delivery

Challan, Ex.C-4/Ex.R-3, it has been mentioned that "DUE TO

PRESSURE DAMAGE DISPLAY DAMAGE & HALF SCREEN

BLACK". The said Delivery Challan is dated 7.11.2014 and the

mobile phone was also returned on the same day. The complainant

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
been mentioned that "DUE TO

PRESSURE DAMAGE DISPLAY DAMAGE & HALF SCREEN

BLACK". The said Delivery Challan is dated 7.11.2014 and the

mobile phone was also returned on the same day. The complainant

has admitted this fact that opposite party No.3-Service Centre had

returned the i-phone saying that it could not be repaired under

warranty and demanded ₹21,500/- for repairing the same and the

cause of defect has also been clearly mentioned as due to external
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 7
pressure put on the phone, which is not covered under the warranty.

For that reason the complainant was asked to pay the amount of

₹21,500/- for repairing the mobile phone in question. Once the

damage has been caused due to the negligence of the complainant

himself, as the pressure was exerted on the display screen, which

resulted into non-display and half of it turned black, the warranty

does not apply. For this view, there is categorical finding recorded

by the District Forum that this defect had occurred due to the

external pressure and was not a manufacturing defect or otherwise

defect. For that reason the damage caused to the mobile phone is

not covered under the warranty.
14. In view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

impugned order passed by the District Forum. There is no merit in

title: Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
text:
aused to the mobile phone is

not covered under the warranty.
14. In view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

impugned order passed by the District Forum. There is no merit in

the present appeal and the same is hereby dismissed.
(JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL)
 PRESIDENT

 (MRS. KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER

The Respondent as complainant filed
a complaint before the District Forum, Udhagamandalam, alleging deficiency
against the opposite party to pay a sum of Rs.97,120/- as compensation, and to
pay cost of the proceedings. The District Forum, allowed the complaint against
the opposite party. Against the said order, this appeal is preferred by the opposite

 RATIONALE

 

 5- Issue  Nos. 1 to 3- The Opposite Party  has raised objection to the jurisdiction of the Forum and given the reference of Hon. Supreme Court in case of Ravneet Singh Bagga v/s KLM Royal Dutch Airlines [(2000) 1 SCC 66] has propounded upon the issue of deficiency in service and has said that only on intentionally providing deficient service the issue of deficient service is proved. In the present complaint the Opposite Party has not, while providing service to the Complainant, intentionally provided deficient service to the Complainant and therefore the present complaint should not be heard in this Forum. Also they have referenced that the Hon. National Forum has propounded the legal principle in the case of Kishore Chandrakant Rathod v/s ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Co. Ltd. and Others (review petition no. 3390/2013) that the Complainant is an educated person and has fully read the terms and conditions of the contract and then taken insurance cover, and for any breach of these conditions resulting in the Opposite Party rejecting the insurance claim the complaint cannot be conducted in front of the Forum. The Opposite Party has said that therefore the Forum has no jurisdicti

conditions resulting in the Opposite Party rejecting the insurance claim the complaint cannot be conducted in front of the Forum. The Opposite Party has said that therefore the Forum has no jurisdiction to conduct the hearing on this complaint. It is proved that after the insurance contract between the Opposite Party and the Complainant, the complainant has not given in writing to the Opposite Party within 15 days of the contract any intimation to cancel the said policy. After the documents submitted by the Complainant to the opposite Party were scrutinized by the specialists appointed by the Opposite Party it was diagnosed that the Complainant had diabetes and the Opposite Party came to know that treatment for the same had been taken and it was verified from the documents submitted by the Complainant but it was established that the Complainant had not disclosed this information to the Opposite Party voluntarily. Therefore it was proved that the complainant had intentionally not given this information to the Opposite Party - - - therefore the Opposite Party has repudiated the Complainant's   insurance  claim under
section 45
of the Insurance Act 1938, as also under the terms mentioned in condition 5 B (i) of the contract. Therefore the Opposite Party have sent a letter to the Complainant dated 21/12/2012 informing him about the insurance claim being rejected. Since the complain

ned in condition 5 B (i) of the contract. Therefore the Opposite Party have sent a letter to the Complainant dated 21/12/2012 informing him about the insurance claim being rejected. of the Consumer Protection Act based on the available documents. After stating this, as held by Hon. Supreme Court in the judgments in the cases of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s harchand Rai Chand Rai Chandalal I (2003) CPJ 393 and Vikram Greentech (I) Ltd. & Another v/s New India Assurance Co. s of the insurance contract is sufficient reason to repudiate the insurance claim and similarly in the present complaint also the Opposite Party has repudiated the insurance claim on valid reasons.

 

The  Opposite Party has repudiated the Complainant's claim based mainly on the breach of terms and conditions of the insurance contract. On reading the terms and conditions of the insurance contract, it is clear that the said insurance contract has been executed relative to the personal information provided by the Complainant and verification thereof by the Opposite Party with the Complainant before the contract was executed. In the opinion of the Opposite Party, the Complainant deliberately withheld information about his diabetes and its continuing treatment, thereby not following the terms and conditions of the insurance contract, especially condition no. 5 B (I) and therefore the insurance contract is rendered invalid from the date of its inception. Therefore according to the Indian Contracts Act at the time of taking the insurance cover the Complainant has agreed to certain terms and conditions and then breached them by not disclosing the information about his pre- existing illness thereby hindering the basic validity of the insurance contract. The Opposite Party have stated that they have repudiated the insurance claim on the basis of the deliberate withholding of informatio

ss thereby hindering the basic validity of the insurance contract. The Opposite Party have stated that they have repudiated the insurance claim on the basis of the deliberate withholding of information by the Complainant which is a  just reason invalidating the insurance contract and therefore the Opposite Party have not provided deficient service to the Complainant by repudiating the insurance claim. On going through the insurance claim submitted by the Complainant to the opposite Party, the information about the Complainant having been diagnosed with diabetes is not entered. Also before taking the insurance cover the Complainant has undergone complete medical check - up by the specialists of the Opposite Party and after this the insurance contract has come into existence. It is proved by the Complainant's statements that in the tests done by the Opposite Party's specialists it was found that the Complainant had no illnesses. Nearly 4 years after the insurance coverage was provided by the Opposite Party to the Complainant he felt the stomach pain for the first time. Insurance Act
1938,

tion 45
it is clearly provided that after expiry of two years after the insurance contract commences the insurance services providing insurance company cannot question the untrue statements related to the insurance contract ; or cannot deny the stated services and also because the Complainant is an elderly person and as such has no reason to withhold any information, therefore it is stated that the insurance claim submitted by the Complainant with the Opposite Party is a valid claim. On a close scrutiny of the Complainant's insurance claim, it can be seen that as per the terms and conditions only the documents related to the Complainant having taken treatment for diabetes have been submitted by the Opposite Party along with the evidential affidavit. That this was not disclosed by the Complainant in the insurance contract with the Opposite Party is proved by the arguments presented in the opposite Party's evidential affidavit. An insurance contract is entered into on the basis of true information being given by both the parties. Although it has been proved that all the various terms and conditions of the Opposite Party were not adhered to in the present complaint, the Hon. Supreme Court has stated in the judgment of the case of Amlendu Sahu v/s Oriental Insurance Co. 6- From the above conclusions the following order is being passed.

 

 FINAL ORDER 

 
 
 

The complaint no. 982/2014 is partially admitted.
 
 
 

It is declared that the Opposite Party has provided deficient services to the Complainant by repudiating the Complainant's insurance reimbursement claim.
 
 
 

The Opposite Party is ordered to pay to the Complainant within 60 days of receiving this order 75 % of the insurance reimbursement claim amount i.e Rs. 4,15,030 /- (Rupees Four Lakh Fifteen Thousand Thirty Only) as described in the conclusion above.
 
 
 

If the opposite Party does not comply with paragraph 3 above within the time frame mentioned , then the Opposite Party must pay 12 % p.a interest on the insurance claim amount Rs. 4,15,030 /- (Rupees Four Lakh Fifteen Thousand Thirty Only) from 21/12/2012 till the payment of the complete amount to the Complainant.
 
 
 

The Opposite Party must pay to the Complainant a total of Rs. 1,00,000/- towards expenses , mental hardship , financial and physical hardship within 60 days of the receipt of this order.

The opposite party Insurance Co. appealed in the State Commission. The State Commission had heard both sides, appraised the evidence, and, vide its Order dated 8.9.2017, dismissed the appeal: 

 

[12] On perusal of order passed by the Ld. District Forum it appears that the Ld. District Forum has considered that the claim of complainant cannot be rejected on technical grounds and allowed 75 % claim of complainant on non- standard basis, on the basis of ruling relied on by the complainant. We are of the opinion that when there is no evidence on record that the complainant had deliberately concealed facts about medical health at the time of obtaining policy from the opposite party, Complainant is entitled to get the hospital charges from the opposite party. We are also of opinion that the view taken by the Ld. District Forum that the claim of complainant cannot be rejected on the technical ground and granted 75 % claim of complainant on non standard basis along with compensation, appears to be legal and correct. Under such circumstances, we are of the opinion that the appeal is liable to be dismissed and order passed by the Ld. District Forum is to be confirmed. Hence, we proceed to pass the following order-

der such circumstances, we are of the opinion that the appeal is liable to be dismissed and order passed by the Ld. District Forum is to be confirmed. Hence, we proceed to pass the following order-

 

 ORDER
1] Appeal is hereby dismissed with costs.
2] Impugned Order dated 31/10/2015 passed by the Ld. Raigad District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum ,Alibaug in consumer complaint No. 982 of 2014 is hereby confirmed.

5.         The opposite party Insurance Co. has filed the instant revision petition under
section 21 (b)
of the Act 1986 against the said Order dated 8.9.2017 of the State Commission.
6.           We find the Order dated 8.9.2017 of the State Commission to be well-appraised and well-reasoned. The State Commission concurred with the District Forum in its findings of deficiency in service. Within the meaning and scope of
section 21(b)
, we find no grave error in appreciating the evidence by the two fora below, as may cause to require re-appreciation of the evidence in revision. And, on the face of it, we find no jurisdictional error, or a legal principle ignored, or miscarriage of justice.
7.         We uphold and affirm the award made by the two fora below in their concurrent findings of defici

t, we find no jurisdictional error, or a legal principle ignored, or miscarriage of justice.
7.         We uphold and affirm the award made by the two fora below in their concurrent findings of deficiency in service. The award of the District Forum shall be made good by the opposite party Insurance Co. within four weeks of the pronouncement of this Order.
8.         In addition, however, we further note that it is an admitted fact that the opposite party Insurance Co. had issued "ICICI-Pru Hospital Care Policy" in 2008 and the complainant was paying the premium regularly. The complainant had no illness during 2008 to August 2012, but, due to abdominal pain, he got admitted in Bombay Hospital on 18.09.2012, wherein he was diagnosed as suffering from renal (kidney) ailments. He underwent dialysis, and subsequently kidney transplant was performed. The opposite party Insurance Co. repudiated the insurance claim for hospitalization expenses of Rs. 5,53,375/-. It was repudiated on the ground of non-disclosure of pre-existing medical condition by the complainant at the time of filling the proposal form. The proposal form was filled in the year 2008 (on 29.07.2008). The insured incurred hospitalization charges in the year 2012, and filed his insurance reimbursement claim with the opposite party Insurance Co. However, the opposite party Insurance Co. repudiated the claim by relying prin

title: Icici Prudential Life Insurance Co. ... vs Dattatrey Bhivsan Gujar on 14 June, 2019
text:
spitalization charges in the year 2012, and filed his insurance reimbursement claim with the opposite party Insurance Co. However, the opposite party Insurance Co. repudiated the claim by relying principally on one certificate (ext. P-2) issued by one Dr. Rajendra G. Chandorkar which states that Mr. Dattatrey (the insured) was a known patient of diabetes and hypertension for the last 10 years.  The verbatim of the certificate is reproduced as under:
"This is to certify that Mr. Dattatray B. Gurjar is a regular pt. of mine and regularly comes for follow up regarding minor illness like cold / cough and fever.  He is a known pt. of Diabetes & Hypertension, since last 10 years."
9.         The opposite party Insurance Co. relied principally on this one certificate issued by this one Dr. Chandorkar (as mentioned in para 8). It is pertinent to note that the said Dr. Chandorkar is a pediatrician. He is neither a physician, nor an endocrinologist, to certify a person as a 'diabetic and hypertensive for past 10 years'. Moreover, nothing is on record that the said Dr. Chandorkar has either examined or treated the complainant for diabetes or hypertension in the past 10 years. Ex facie, a suspicious medical certificate was issued. It is not viewed favourably. It prima facie amounts to professional misconduct under the Code of Medical Ethics Regulation, 2002 of the Medical Council of India.

title: Icici Prudential Life Insurance Co. ... vs Dattatrey Bhivsan Gujar on 14 June, 2019
text:
icious medical certificate was issued. It is not viewed favourably. It prima facie amounts to professional misconduct under the Code of Medical Ethics Regulation, 2002 of the Medical Council of India.
The medical record of Bombay Hospital does not,   explicitly and categorically, confirm that the complainant was diabetic and hypertensive prior to 2008. Logically, and medically, time or onset of diabetes and / or hypertension cannot be accurately predicted. The complainant could possibly have started suffering from diabetes and / or hypertension subsequent to the year 2008, and it cannot be anyhow averred, on the basis of an ex facie suspicious certificate, that he was suffering from the same prior to 2018.
10.       We would not like to turn a blind eye on the issuance of the ex facie suspicious medical certificate by the said Dr. Rajendra G. Chandorkar to unduly help the opposite party Insurance Co. in taking its principal ground for repudiation of the insurance claim. Issuance of such medical certificate is unethical and amounts to professional misconduct, which needs suitable action from the concerned professional regulatory body. To check such unethical medical practices we, thus, direct the Registrar of this Commission to refer this matter to the Maharashtra Medical Council, Mumbai, for the appropriate necessary action against Dr. Rajendra G. Chandorkar, as per the Council

title: Icici Prudential Life Insurance Co. ... vs Dattatrey Bhivsan Gujar on 14 June, 2019
text:
us, direct the Registrar of this Commission to refer this matter to the Maharashtra Medical Council, Mumbai, for the appropriate necessary action against Dr. Rajendra G. Chandorkar, as per the Council's rules and wisdom.
11.       Further, we note that the act of the opposite party Insurance Co. in obtaining (by whatever means and in whichever manner) such suspicious certificate in such facts and circumstances and principally using such certificate to repudiate the insurance claim is an unfair and deceptive act and amounts to unfair trade practice within the meaning of
section 2(1)(r)
of the Act 1986. For this, in addition to the award made by the two fora below in respect of deficiency in service (which has been upheld and affirmed by us), the opposite party Insurance Co. is put to stern advice of caution in respect of unfair trade practice through imposition of cost of Rs. 5 lakh to be deposited in the Consumer Legal Aid Account of the District Forum, within four weeks of the pronouncement of this Order.
12.      The revision petition of the opposite party Insurance Co. is dismissed, with directions as above (paras 7, 10 and 11).
13.       Needless to add that the District Forum shall undertake execution as per the law.
14.      A copy each of this Order be sent to the District Forum and to the complainant within ten days by the Registry.
A copy each of this order be sent to

title: Icici Prudential Life Insurance Co. ... vs Dattatrey Bhivsan Gujar on 14 June, 2019
text:
shall undertake execution as per the law.
14.      A copy each of this Order be sent to the District Forum and to the complainant within ten days by the Registry.
A copy each of this order be sent to the Maharashtra Medical Council, Mumbai and be placed before the Registrar of this Commission within ten days by the Registry.

State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
ADDITIONAL BENCH

STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PUNJAB, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.618 of 2019
 Date of institution : 18.09.2019
 Reserved on : 28.03.2022
 Date of decision : 07.04.2022

Ram Ishwar Yadav son of Sh. Kanhaiya Yadav, R/o H.No.94, Gobind
Nagar, Railway Station Road, Malerkotla, Tehsil Malerkotla, District
Sangrur.
 .....Appellant/Complainant
 Versus

State Bank of India, Branch Office : College Road, Malerkotla, Tehsil
Malerkotla, District Sangrur, through its Branch Manager-148023.

 ....Respondent/Opposite Party

 First Appeal under
Section 15
the
 Consumer Protection Act, against the order
 dated 31.05.2019 of the District Consumer
 Disputes Redressal Forum (now
 'Commission'), Sangrur.
Quorum:-
 Mr. Rajinder Kumar Goyal, Presiding Member
Mrs. Kiran Sibal, Member

Present:-
For the appellant : Sh. Pardeep Singh, Advocate
 For respondent : None

KIRAN SIBAL, MEMBER

 The instant appeal has been filed by the
appellant/complainant against the order dated 31.05.2019 passed by

District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Sangrur (in short, now

"the District Commission"), whereby the complaint filed by complainant
FA No.618 of 2019 2
against opposite party (in short 'OP'), under the
Consumer Protection

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
edressal Forum, Sangrur (in short, now

"the District Commission"), whereby the complaint filed by complainant
FA No.618 of 2019 2
against opposite party (in short 'OP'), under the
Consumer Protection

Act, 1986
, was dismissed. The relevant portion of the impugned order

is reproduced as under:-
"6........... As proceedings before the Consumer Forum

 are summary in nature, but allegations of forgery

 leveled in this case requires elaborate evidence and as

 such, complainant, if advised may approach the Civil

 Court of competent jurisdiction because complex

 question of law and facts qua fraud can be decided by

 that Court and not in these summary proceedings".
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties

will be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Commission.
3. Brief facts for the disposal of the appeal are that the

complainant was having a saving bank account No.31162067573 with

OP Bank and had been availing ATM Card facility and on every

transaction, message was being sent on the registered mobile

No.98144-84053 of the complainant. On 25.10.2017, an unidentified

and unknown person fraudulently exchanged the ATM card from the

son of the complainant in ATM House situated at Truck Union, Near

Kewal Shiv Mandir, Malerkotla. The ATM card, which was fraudulently

handed over to the son of the complainant, was in the name of one

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
on of the complainant in ATM House situated at Truck Union, Near

Kewal Shiv Mandir, Malerkotla. The ATM card, which was fraudulently

handed over to the son of the complainant, was in the name of one

Kalyan Singh Rajput of Udaipur. The said unidentified person, in

connivance with the officials of OP, just to usurp huge amount and to

play fraud upon the complainant, first stopped message service on the

registered mobile phone of the complainant and thereafter withdrew
FA No.618 of 2019 3
the total amount of Rs.2,77,902/- on various dates and misutilized the

same. The complainant was unaware about the said transactions as

no message was sent on the registered mobile phone of the

complainant by the OP. The complainant came to know about the said

illegal transactions on 14.11.2017 when he went to ATM for withdrawal

of amount. He approached OP, who assured the complainant that

whole amount would be reversed. But OP did not initiate any action in

the said matter. Therefore, the complainant lodged an FIR No.121

dated 24.11.2017 under
Section 420
IPC, at P.S.City-1, Malerkotla

against unknown person, but nothing was recovered. Alleging

deficiency in service on the part of the OP, the complainant filed the

consumer complaint before the District Commission and sought refund

of Rs.2,77,902/- along with interest @18% p.a. and compensation to

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
ncy in service on the part of the OP, the complainant filed the

consumer complaint before the District Commission and sought refund

of Rs.2,77,902/- along with interest @18% p.a. and compensation to

the tune of Rs.50,000/- on account of mental tension, agony and

physical harassment and Rs.11,000/- as litigation expenses.
4. The complaint was contested by the OP, who filed written

reply before the District Commission. In its written reply, OP raised

certain legal objections, inter alia, that the complainant has alleged the

commission of fraud and cheating with him by fraudster and lodged

FIR under
section 420
IPC before the policy authorities, therefore, the

complaint was not maintainable before District Commission. The

complainant was negligent as well as was responsible in regard to

operation of his account as his son had shared the Card Credentials

with fraudster person standing in the ATM room, beside handing over

the ATM card to him and sharing the secret PIN code to withdraw the
FA No.618 of 2019 4
amount of Rs.10,000/-. As such, the complainant had no locus standi

to file the complaint and the complaint was bad for non joinder of

necessary parties. On merits, OP stated that as regard the receipt of

messages regarding withdrawal through ATM card is concerned, the

messages are not sent by the OP. The SMS is generated and

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
r of

necessary parties. On merits, OP stated that as regard the receipt of

messages regarding withdrawal through ATM card is concerned, the

messages are not sent by the OP. The SMS is generated and

delivered to the customer's registered mobile numbers by the SMS

INFRONICS Team, who informed the OP that there was no log found

for the disputed transactions. No CCTV footage had been provided to

the OP by the outsourced agencies. There was no deficiency in

service on the part of the OP. After denying the other averments made

in the complaint, OP prayed for dismissal of the complaint.
5. Parties led their evidence in support of their respective

contentions before the District Commission and after hearing the

learned counsel for the parties, the complaint was dismissed vide

impugned order dated 31.05.2019 as above. Aggrieved by the said

order, this appeal has been filed by the appellant/complainant for

setting aside the same.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and have

also gone through written submission filed by parties as well as record

of the case.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant, vehemently contended

that the District Commission wrongly and illegally dismissed the

complaint of the appellant/complainant on the ground that allegations

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
ase.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant, vehemently contended

that the District Commission wrongly and illegally dismissed the

complaint of the appellant/complainant on the ground that allegations

of forgery have been leveled in the complaint but it failed to appreciate
FA No.618 of 2019 5
the fact that there is also negligence on the part of the respondent

Bank. The District Commission further failed to appreciate the fact that

the appellant/complainant lost his amount due to non sending of

messages by the respondent/OP bank. The respondent/OP bank has

received charges from appellant/complainant for sending of messages

to him but it has stopped sending the messages without giving any

information or reason for the same. The appellant was unaware about

the withdrawals by the said person as no message was sent to him by

the respondent/OP Bank on his registered mobile number. The

learned counsel further contended that RBI has issued guidelines

dated 06.07.2017 regarding Zero liability of a customer. The relevant

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
by

the respondent/OP Bank on his registered mobile number. The

learned counsel further contended that RBI has issued guidelines

dated 06.07.2017 regarding Zero liability of a customer. The relevant

portion of the said guideline is reproduced as under:-
(a) Zero Liability of a Customer
6. A customer's entitlement to zero liability shall arise where the
 unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events:
(i) Contributory fraud/ negligence/ deficiency on the part of the
 bank (irrespective of whether or not the transaction is reported
 by the customer).
(ii) Third party breach where the deficiency lies neither with
 the bank nor with the customer but lies elsewhere in the system,
 and the customer notifies the bank within three working days
 of receiving the communication from the bank regarding the
 unauthorised transaction.
Alleging negligence and deficiency in service on the part of the

respondent/OP, the learned counsel prayed for acceptance of the

present appeal and setting aside of the impugned order.
8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the

respondent/OP contended that the District Commission has rightly

dismissed the complaint filed before it as the complainant had alleged

the commission of fraud and cheating with him. The learned counsel
FA No.618 of 2019 6
further contended that the ATM card facility was provided only to the

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
d before it as the complainant had alleged

the commission of fraud and cheating with him. The learned counsel
FA No.618 of 2019 6
further contended that the ATM card facility was provided only to the

appellant/complainant and as per banking norms, the person other

than the ATM card holder is not legally entitled to operate the ATM

Card, even with the permission of the ATM card holder. The card

holder is bound to keep the PIN number confidential. Admittedly, the

appellant/complainant handed over the ATM card and disclosed the

four digit PIN number to his son and allowed him to use the same and

his son further handed over the ATM card to a stranger, who withdrew

the money fraudulently. The alleged fraudulent withdrawals occurred

as the ATM and its Pin Number fell in wrong hands due to the

negligence on the part of the appellant/complainant. There is no

negligence and deficiency in service on the part of the respondent/ OP

bank. The learned counsel prayed for dismissal of the present appeal.
9. We have given thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the parties.
10. The admitted facts of the case are that the

appellant/complainant is having his saving bank account with the OP

bank and an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- has been withdrawn/transferred

by unidentified person through the ATM Card of the complainant. The

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
llant/complainant is having his saving bank account with the OP

bank and an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- has been withdrawn/transferred

by unidentified person through the ATM Card of the complainant. The

complainant approached the OP bank but they failed to redress the

grievance of the complainant. Therefore, the complainant filed a

Consumer Complaint before the District Commission, which was

dismissed, vide impugned order reproduced as above. The grievance

of the appellant/complainant is that the District Commission, instead of

appreciating the fact of negligence on the part of the OP Bank, has
FA No.618 of 2019 7
dismissed the complaint of the complainant without going into merits of

the case on the ground that fraud and forgery needs voluminous

evidence therefore the complaint was not maintainable.
11. The foremost point for consideration before us is whether

the District Commission has rightly dismissed the complaint on the

ground of forgery or not? A perusal of the complaint and perusal of

affidavit of the complainant, Ex. C-1, shows that allegations made in

the complaint are with regard to unauthorized use of ATM card by a

third person, who had withdrawn an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- on

various dates through ATM withdrawal, online purchase and transfer to

another account. The appellant/complainant, being a consumer of the

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
hird person, who had withdrawn an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- on

various dates through ATM withdrawal, online purchase and transfer to

another account. The appellant/complainant, being a consumer of the

respondent/OP Bank, also leveled allegations that due to non-sending

of messages by the bank on his mobile number he suffered the said

loss. The District Commission, while passing the impugned order,

relied on the Judgment of Hon'ble National Commission, in case titled

Bright Transport Company Versus Sangli Sahakari Bank Limited

reported in II (2012) CPJ-151 (NC), wherein it was held that the

complaints which are based on allegations of fraud, forgery etc and

trial of which would require voluminous evidence and consideration are

not to be entertained by the Consumer Commission. But the authority

relied upon by the District Commission is not applicable to the facts of

the present case, as the facts of that case are distinguishable from the

present case. In the cited authority the amount was encashed by

putting forged signatures on the cheque, but in the present case, the

amount was withdrawn by exchanging the ATM card of the

complainant by a third person illegally. Therefore, we do not agree
FA No.618 of 2019 8
with the finding of the District Commission that Consumer

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
mount was withdrawn by exchanging the ATM card of the

complainant by a third person illegally. Therefore, we do not agree
FA No.618 of 2019 8
with the finding of the District Commission that Consumer

Commissions have no jurisdiction to decide the present case.
12. This matter is no more res-integra. The Hon'ble Supreme

Court in case "
Dr. J.J. Merchant & Ors. v. Shrinath Chaturvedi
",

2002 (2)
CPC
-640, held that "under the Act, the Hon'ble National

Commission is headed by a retired Judge of the Hon'ble Supreme

Court and the State Commission is headed by a retired High Court

Judge. Similarly, the District Forums are headed by retired

District/Additional Session Judge or the person of legal background

having equivalent experience and, as such, they are competent to

decide the complicated issues of law or facts. It is expected of them to

decide the cases on merits, on the basis of prima facie evidence on

the record."
Similarly, in
Shiv Kumar Agarwal v. Arun Tonden &

Anr.
, 2007 (2)
CPC
129 (NC), it was observed by the Hon'ble National

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
cide the cases on merits, on the basis of prima facie evidence on

the record."
Similarly, in
Shiv Kumar Agarwal v. Arun Tonden &

Anr.
, 2007 (2)
CPC
129 (NC), it was observed by the Hon'ble National

Commission in Para No.5, which is reproduced below:-
5. We heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and
 perused the material on record. Like before the State
 Commission, the learned Counsel for the petitioner argued
 before us that this case involves complicated questions of fact
 and law and will need expert evidence, which is not possible
 in the summary procedure adopted by the Consumer Fora.
After seeing the complaint, written version as also the
 judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
Dr.
 J.J. Merchant and Ors. v. Shrinath Chaturvedi
, and other
 catena of judgments, we are of the view that Consumer
 Forum, which is headed by Senior Judicial Officers, are
 capable of dealing with even complex questions.
The
 Consumer Protection Act, 1986
under
Section 13
provides for
 calling for expert evidence, if necessary.
13.
In view of the ratio of law
laid down in
the authority

discussed above, the Consume Fora , now "Consumer Commissions"
are being presided by the competent senior judicial authorities and
FA No.618 of 2019 9
they are capable of dealing with even complex questions of law.

Accordingly, the order of dismissal of the complaint on the ground that

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
e competent senior judicial authorities and
FA No.618 of 2019 9
they are capable of dealing with even complex questions of law.

Accordingly, the order of dismissal of the complaint on the ground that

allegations of forgery have been leveled for which elaborate evidence

is required to be led before the Civil Court, is set aside.
14. Now, coming to the merits of the case, the only question

arises for adjudication before us is that whether there is any

fault/negligence on the part of the OP Bank or not? To determine this

controversy, we have perused the entire evidence and pleadings on

record. From the perusal of complaint filed by the complainant as well

as his affidavit Ex.C-1 and even the FIR, Ex. C-2, it clearly shows that

the appellant/complainant himself handed over the ATM card to his

son for using the same and disclosed the four digit PIN number to him.

Furthermore, admittedly his son, handed over the said ATM card to a

stranger/third party and also disclosed the PIN number to him.

Resultantly, the said unknown person cleverly exchanged the ATM

card from the son of the complainant, who was about 28 years old,

and withdrew the alleged amount on different dates through different

modes. Moreover, in the "SBI Debit Card User Guide" placed on

record by respondent/OP Bank as Ex. OP/1, it has been specifically

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
and withdrew the alleged amount on different dates through different

modes. Moreover, in the "SBI Debit Card User Guide" placed on

record by respondent/OP Bank as Ex. OP/1, it has been specifically

mentioned as under:-
• Please keep the PIN secret and do not disclose the PIN to
 anybody including your family members and close
 relatives.
• Giving your card and disclosing PIN to someone is like
 giving a blank signed cheque.
• Please refrain from taking help from any stranger while
 doing ATM transaction.
FA No.618 of 2019 10
Accordingly, as per Banking norms, the ATM card holder is bound to

keep the PIN number confidential. Nowadays, banks in India have

been incessantly warning people against scamsters, urging customers

to never share their banking details, ATM pin details, credit card

numbers etc. Despite these warnings, if customers still fail to adhere to

the basic precautionary norms and fall prey to fraudulent schemes or

activities, they will not be able to hold the banks responsible for it.

Further, reliance is placed upon the Circular DBR.No.Leg.BC.

78/09.07.005/2017-18 dated 06.07.2017 issued by the Reserve Bank

of India regarding limiting liability of Customers in Unauthorized

Electric Banking Transactions. The relevant clause is reproduced as

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
8/09.07.005/2017-18 dated 06.07.2017 issued by the Reserve Bank

of India regarding limiting liability of Customers in Unauthorized

Electric Banking Transactions. The relevant clause is reproduced as

under:-
"Limited Liability of Customer
(a) Zero Liability of a Customer
6. A customer's entitlement to zero liability shall arise where the
 unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events:
(i) Contributory fraud/ negligence/ deficiency on the part of the
 bank (irrespective of whether or not the transaction is reported
 by the customer).
(ii) Third party breach where the deficiency lies neither with
 the bank nor with the customer but lies elsewhere in the system,
 and the customer notifies the bank within three working days
 of receiving the communication from the bank regarding the
 unauthorised transaction.
(b) Limited Liability of a Customer
7. A customer shall be liable for the loss occurring due to
 unauthorised transactions in the following cases:
(i) In cases where the loss is due to negligence by a customer,
 such as where he has shared the payment credentials, the
 customer will bear the entire loss until he reports the
 unauthorised transaction to the bank. Any loss occurring after
 the reporting of the unauthorised transaction shall be borne by
 the bank.
FA No.618 of 2019 11
(ii) In cases where the responsibility for the unauthorised
 electronic banking tran

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
ss occurring after
 the reporting of the unauthorised transaction shall be borne by
 the bank.
FA No.618 of 2019 11
(ii) In cases where the responsibility for the unauthorised
 electronic banking transaction lies neither with the bank nor
 with the customer, but lies elsewhere in the system and when
 there is a delay (of four to seven working days after receiving
 the communication from the bank) on the RBI,DBR,CO - 4 -
continuation sheet part of the customer in notifying the bank of
 such a transaction, the per transaction liability of the customer
 shall be limited to the transaction value or the amount
 mentioned in Table 1, whichever is lower."
The complainant was duped because of his own negligence, as

discussed above, therefore Clause 7(i) of the above said circular is

applicable that " in cases where the loss is due to negligence by a

customer, such as where he has shared the payment credentials,

the customer will bear the entire loss until he reports the

unauthorised transaction to the bank". The contention of learned

counsel for the appellant/complainant is that if the respondent/OP

Bank had sent the messages regarding the alleged unauthorized

transactions to the appellant, he might be alerted and the remaining

amount could be saved. But to support this contention, nothing has

been placed on record by the appellant/complainant that he is availing

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
ions to the appellant, he might be alerted and the remaining

amount could be saved. But to support this contention, nothing has

been placed on record by the appellant/complainant that he is availing

any SMS alert service of the respondent/OP bank with regard to every

transactions made by him. In the absence of any cogent evidence like

printout of previous SMSs or bank statement showing debit entry of

payment for availing such service, it is hard to believe that

appellant/complainant has been availing the said service of the bank.

Accordingly, we do not find any force in the contention raised by the

learned counsel for the appellant/complainant and the same is hereby

rejected. We are of the considered view that there is no deficiency in

service or negligence on the part of respondent/OP bank for the
FA No.618 of 2019 12
alleged loss suffered by the appellant/complainant. Hence, as per

clause 7(i), as discussed above, the liability is of the

appellant/complainant and he shall bear the entire loss as he shared

the payment credentials and there is negligence on his own part.
15. Sequel to our above discussion, we do not find any merit in

the present appeal as well as in the complaint filed before the District

Commission and the same are hereby dismissed with no order as to

costs.
16. The appeal could not be decided within the stipulated

title: Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
text:
present appeal as well as in the complaint filed before the District

Commission and the same are hereby dismissed with no order as to

costs.
16. The appeal could not be decided within the stipulated

period due to heavy pendency of Court cases and non-sitting of this

Commission due to pandemic of Covid-19.
(RAJINDER KUMAR GOYAL)
 PRESIDING MEMBER

 (KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER
